strengths: Two-layer runtime patch architecture is genuinely solid: theme registry emits a validated, allow-listed <style> patch (apps/web/src/themes/registry.ts:233-259) and appearance preferences emit a second patch that always wins by document order (apps/web/src/themes/appearancePreferences.ts:668-678). Values are sanitized (FORBIDDEN_VALUE_PATTERN, 200-char cap, per-kind validation, registry.ts:20-71) and Tailwind's build-time --alpha() is materialized to runtime color-mix (registry.ts:87-123). This pipeline can carry new liquid-glass tokens as-is.

The phone glass material system is the house's proven model: blur+saturation travel as ONE filter token so the Solid step resolves to `none` and never forces a backdrop root (appearancePreferences.ts:552-560, index.css:579-664); per-tier WCAG coverage floors are documented and asserted against composited worst-case backdrops (appearancePreferences.ts:509-513); the scrim-split math keeps the blurred layer thin while preserving guaranteed contrast (splitGlassCoverage, appearancePreferences.ts:533-541). The desktop redesign should copy this architecture, not invent a new one.

Accessibility enforcement is centralized at the material layer: prefers-reduced-transparency and forced-colors are handled once in index.css (717-793) without mutating the stored preference, and the settings UI can report the OS override (isSurfaceTransparencyReducedBySystem, appearancePreferences.ts:339-341). Every keyframe animation in index.css carries a prefers-reduced-motion guard.

Neutral tokens are alpha-based, not opaque: --border: --alpha(var(--color-black) / 8%), --muted/--secondary/--accent at 4% black/white (index.css:380-388, 419-427). These composite correctly over any backdrop, which is inherently glass-friendly — most components need no change when their substrate becomes translucent.

Default theme has real light/dark parity discipline: status colors ship paired foreground tones that shift per scheme (--destructive-foreground red-700 light / red-400 dark, index.css:390-401 vs 425-435), and dark primary is lightened (oklch 0.488 -> 0.588) rather than reused.

Radius is a single-token scale: all seven steps derive from --radius via px offsets in @theme (index.css:170-176), and the user radius preference rewrites every step with clamping (appearancePreferences.ts:432-448) — no per-component radius drift in the token layer.
Custom primary color computes its foreground via WCAG relative luminance (resolvePrimaryForeground, appearancePreferences.ts:643-655).

Theme switches suppress transitions correctly (.no-transitions + forced reflow + rAF removal, index.css:290-297, useTheme.ts:106-125), and cross-tab sync covers all four storage keys (useTheme.ts:183-194).
Scrollbar colors are first-class themable tokens (types.ts:28-31) with per-theme derivation from the palette foreground (builtin.ts:130-134).

Token CSS is unusually well documented — the --font-heading shim (index.css:139-144), the dock inset max() rationale (338-355), and the single-filter-token reasoning (appearancePreferences.ts:550-553) make conventions discoverable for the redesign.
patterns: All theming flows through CSS custom properties patched by two runtime <style> elements: #ryco-active-theme (registry.ts:258) then #ryco-appearance-preferences (appearancePreferences.ts:379), the latter re-appended to <head> on every write so it wins by order. New material tokens must be reachable through this pipeline.

THEME_TOKEN_NAMES (themes/types.ts:1-39) is a hard allow-list: tokensToCss drops anything not on it (registry.ts:236-243). Any new glass/elevation token that should be theme-visible must be added to THEME_TOKEN_NAMES + THEME_TOKEN_META or it silently won't emit.

--alpha(<color> / n%) is build-time only; every runtime-injected value must be materialized to color-mix(in srgb, ...) (materializeTokenValue, registry.ts:82-123). Custom themes forking the default rely on this.

One Material axis: the single surfaceTransparency key serves desktop and phone; components consume only derived --app-* variables (buildSurfaceTransparencyCssVariables, appearancePreferences.ts:572-600), never the step name. prefers-reduced-transparency is enforced ONLY in CSS (index.css:717-767), never in the derivation — the settings UI reports the override instead of displaying it as the selection.

Phone glass tiers are selected exclusively via glassSurfaceClassName(tier) (components/mobile/GlassSurface.tsx:42-44); no consumer names a blur, alpha, or shadow. The web phone tier is frozen — desktop must get its own tier vocabulary, not extend sheet/chip/dock.

Overlay surfaces are popover-tinted: dialog, sheet, tooltip, toast, autocomplete, command all use .app-surface (color-mix over --popover) + text-popover-foreground; --card is for in-flow panels. (ui/dialog.tsx:81, ui/sheet.tsx:84, ui/tooltip.tsx:41, ui/toast.tsx:557).

House elevation-highlight convention: 1px border + hairline inner bevel `before:shadow-[0_1px_--theme(--color-black/4%)] dark:before:shadow-[0_-1px_--theme(--color-white/6%)]` repeated verbatim across dialog/popover/tooltip/toast/autocomplete/command — a de facto token that should become a real one.

Dark mode is the .dark class custom variant (index.css:3) with color-scheme set per scheme; theme patches target `:root { } :root.dark { }` (registry.ts:258). Tier gating uses data-tier stamped on root with phone:/not-phone: variants (index.css:6-8); wco variant marks Electron window-controls-overlay.

House motion: ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) and --app-motion-duration-{sheet,stack,chip} zeroed under reduced motion (appearancePreferences.ts:602-617); the stated contract is that no correctness depends on a transition completing.

syncBrowserChromeTheme (hooks/useTheme.ts:92-104) derives meta theme-color and html/body background from the computed sidebar-inset surface — any new surface architecture must keep this derivation working or replace it deliberately.
Base UI (not Radix) primitives animate via data-starting-style/data-ending-style transition classes; popups portal to body, so glass popovers escape ancestor backdrop roots in the DOM.

issues.title: Sidebar color tokens don't exist — bg-sidebar/text-sidebar-foreground/border-sidebar-border compile to nothing
issues.evidence: sidebar.tsx uses "flex h-full w-(--sidebar-width) flex-col bg-sidebar text-sidebar-foreground" (214), "bg-sidebar p-0 text-sidebar-foreground" (232), "bg-sidebar group-data-[variant=floating]:border-sidebar-border" (302), and the resize rail "hover:after:bg-sidebar-border" (581). No --color-sidebar/--sidebar/--sidebar-foreground/--sidebar-border token is defined anywhere — index.css is the only CSS file and contains none (verified via grep across src/**.css). In Tailwind v4 unknown theme utilities are simply not generated, so the sidebar renders transparent (accidentally showing html's --app-chrome-background) and the resize-handle hover indicator paints nothing.
issues.glassImpact: The app's largest chrome region has no material of its own — it only looks right because the opaque body shows through. The moment the desktop goes translucent/vibrant, the sidebar has no surface at all. The redesign must introduce real sidebar surface tokens (and add them to THEME_TOKEN_NAMES) rather than inherit this accident.
issues.recommendation: Define --sidebar, --sidebar-foreground, --sidebar-border (+ @theme --color-* mappings) as intentional tokens — likely transparent-over-chrome by design on desktop — and fix the dead resize-rail hover indicator. Add them to the theme allow-list so themes can tint chrome separately from content.

issues.title: Root chrome is stamped opaque — html/body background plus runtime inline-style stamping block a translucent window
issues.evidence: index.css @layer base sets `html { background-color: var(--app-chrome-background); }` and body likewise (199-206), and syncBrowserChromeTheme writes the resolved computed color as inline styles: `document.documentElement.style.backgroundColor = backgroundColor; document.body.style.backgroundColor = backgroundColor;` plus meta theme-color (useTheme.ts:101-103). normalizeThemeColor only rejects fully transparent values (70-82), so any solid computed surface color is pinned at the root on every theme apply.
issues.glassImpact: This is the anchor assumption an Apple-style liquid glass desktop must remove: Electron vibrancy/translucent windows require a transparent html/body. Every in-app 'glass' surface currently blurs this opaque backdrop, not the desktop behind the window. The stamping happens in JS, so a CSS-only redesign cannot override it.
issues.recommendation: Make chrome opacity a first-class token (e.g. --app-chrome-background allowed to be translucent, with a vibrancy flag from the Electron shell). Gate syncBrowserChromeTheme so it stamps meta theme-color only, not inline backgrounds, when the window is vibrant.

issues.title: At least 9 ad-hoc translucent surface recipes bypass the Material axis entirely
issues.evidence: Each floating surface hand-picks alpha and blur: PlanSidebar "bg-card/90 shadow-xl supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-card/75" + "backdrop-blur" (120-123); ComposerCommandMenu "bg-popover/96 shadow-lg/8 backdrop-blur-xs" (160); ThreadMessageSearchBar "bg-popover/96 ... shadow-lg/12 backdrop-blur" (50); MessagesTimeline hover card "bg-popover/95 ... shadow-xl shadow-black/25 backdrop-blur" (770); overviewLayouts sticky header "bg-card/92 ... backdrop-blur supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-card/85" (303); ThemeEditor sticky header "bg-muted/72 ... backdrop-blur-sm" (261); ChatView jump pill "bg-card/80 ... backdrop-blur" (3603); PhoneGetAppInterstitial "bg-background/72 backdrop-blur-sm" (27); PairingRouteSurface "bg-card/90 ... shadow-2xl shadow-black/20 backdrop-blur-md" (35). That is ≥7 distinct alphas (72–96%) and 5 blur radii (xs/sm/default/md + none), none reading --app-surface-opacity.
issues.glassImpact: These surfaces stay translucent even at Material=Solid (the shipped default) and ignore prefers-reduced-transparency, because only .app-surface/.app-glass-* rules are covered by the index.css enforcement blocks (717-767). They are exactly the surfaces a liquid-glass system must own; today each one would fight the new material tokens.
issues.recommendation: Introduce desktop material tiers (mirroring the phone's sheet/chip/dock discipline) and migrate every floating surface to them. Nothing should name its own alpha or blur — that is already the phone system's stated contract (GlassSurface.tsx:23).

issues.title: Desktop Material axis produces translucency without blur, and three competing glass recipes coexist
issues.evidence: Default dialogs use "app-surface" (color-mix alpha only, index.css:539-541) with no backdrop-filter — at Material=Glass (28% transparency) a dialog is 72%-alpha unblurred over busy content, with only the viewport's backdrop-blur-[2px] (dialog.tsx:40) behind it. Meanwhile menus/popovers/selects use .selection-glass-surface with blur(10px) saturate(132%) contrast(1.03) (index.css:688-689), and six specific dialogs add .project-glass-surface with blur(30px) saturate(142%) contrast(1.04) (index.css:796-797) via a surface="glass" prop. Same concept — an elevated translucent panel — has three materials chosen per-callsite.
issues.glassImpact: This is the core gap the redesign exists to close: the desktop needs one blur/alpha/scrim ramp driven by the Material step (as the phone tiers already do), not an unblurred alpha axis plus two hand-tuned glass classes. Unblurred translucency also has the worst legibility-to-payoff ratio.
issues.recommendation: Fold selection-glass-surface and project-glass-surface into a desktop tier system emitting --app-glass-* style token triples per Material step; give app-surface consumers a blur component that resolves to `none` at Solid (single-filter-token pattern, appearancePreferences.ts:552-560).

issues.title: Status and domain colors bypass semantic tokens in ~107 places across 39 component files
issues.evidence: grep for raw accent palette utilities in components returns 107 hits in 39 files. Examples: the composer stop action uses "bg-rose-500/90 text-white ... hover:bg-rose-500" instead of --destructive (ComposerPrimaryActions.tsx:127); ReasoningChip defines SLATE_TINT = "bg-slate-400/15 text-slate-700 dark:bg-slate-500/20 dark:text-slate-300" (37); PullRequestThreadDialog uses "text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400/80" (133) duplicated verbatim in ThreadStatusIndicators.tsx:51; WorkItemDetail uses "text-slate-500" (1343). Semantic --info/--success/--warning/--destructive tokens exist and are themable.
issues.glassImpact: Raw palette tints tuned against opaque zinc surfaces will read differently over translucent material; a token-routed status system can be retuned once for glass.
issues.recommendation: Route status/domain tints through the semantic tokens (or add missing ones, e.g. a neutral/idle status tone) before the redesign; otherwise every custom theme and every material change leaves 39 files off-palette.

issues.title: Sidebar status shimmer hardcodes Tailwind palette variables parallel to the themable status system
issues.evidence: The sidebar's most visible status text is colored with raw palette vars: `.sidebar-status-text--review { --sidebar-status-text-base-color: var(--color-amber-600); --sidebar-status-text-shimmer-color: var(--color-orange-300); }` and similarly sky/indigo/violet/emerald/lime/fuchsia across lines 896-965. Theme patches to --warning/--info/--success never reach these; a Nord or High Contrast user keeps stock Tailwind amber/violet in the sidebar.
issues.glassImpact: None directly, but the shimmer colors were tuned for the default opaque sidebar; over glass chrome they will need one retune, which only works if they reference tokens.
issues.recommendation: Map each status to the semantic tokens (base from --warning/--info/etc., shimmer via color-mix lightening) so themes and the glass retune propagate.

issues.title: presetTokens collapses status *-foreground tokens to the raw status color — below AA as text in light presets
issues.evidence: presetTokens sets `"info-foreground": palette.info, "success-foreground": palette.success, "warning-foreground": palette.warning` (builtin.ts:124-129). The default theme deliberately uses darker -700 shades for these text roles in light (index.css:390-401). Catppuccin Latte gets warning-foreground #df8e1d on background #eff1f5 (~2.5:1) and GitHub Light warning #9a6700 is borderline; any component rendering text-warning-foreground on light preset surfaces is below WCAG AA.
issues.recommendation: Give PresetPalette optional per-role foreground overrides and derive darkened text tones (color-mix toward black) for light variants, mirroring the default theme's -700 convention.

issues.title: Dark-only built-in themes silently fall back to the Default light palette in light mode
issues.evidence: resolveTokens overlays the theme on the default: `const base = (variant === "dark" ? DEFAULT_THEME.dark : DEFAULT_THEME.light) ?? {}; const overlay = (variant === "dark" ? theme.dark : theme.light) ?? {};` (227-231). Nord, Dracula, One Dark Pro, Tokyo Night, and Midnight Graphite define only `dark` (builtin.ts:147-184, 259-345, 442-467). A user selecting Nord with Theme variant = Light (or System on a light OS) gets the stock Default light palette with no indication their theme isn't rendering.
issues.recommendation: Either force/suggest dark variant when a dark-only theme is active, or badge dark-only themes in the picker and show 'renders in dark mode only' when variant is light.

issues.title: --destructive-foreground semantics diverge from shadcn convention; on-destructive text is hardcoded white
issues.evidence: In this system --destructive-foreground is the red *text-on-surface* tone (--color-red-700 light / --color-red-400 dark, index.css:390/429), while actual text on destructive fills is literal `text-white`: button destructive variant "border-destructive bg-destructive text-white" (button.tsx:36) and badge "bg-destructive text-white" (badge.tsx:25). A theme author following shadcn convention (destructive-foreground = on-color) gets near-invisible destructive text on surfaces; a theme with a light destructive color gets white-on-light buttons.
issues.glassImpact: Hardcoded text-white also breaks when destructive fills become translucent tints over glass.
issues.recommendation: Introduce an explicit on-destructive token (or reuse primary-foreground-style derivation) and document the -foreground naming; audit info/success/warning for the same dual meaning.

issues.title: No elevation token scale — shadows are per-component literals (12+ distinct recipes)
issues.evidence: Inventory across surfaces: shadow-lg/5 (dialog.tsx:81, popover.tsx:62), shadow-md/5 (tooltip.tsx:41), shadow-xs/5 (command.tsx:160), shadow-lg/8 (ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:160), shadow-lg/10 (MobileDock.tsx:81), shadow-lg/12 (ThreadMessageSearchBar.tsx:50), shadow-xl shadow-black/25 (MessagesTimeline.tsx:770), shadow-2xl shadow-black/20 (PairingRouteSurface.tsx:35), shadow-2xl shadow-black/10 (HostedNativeAuthorizationRoute.tsx:108), plus hardcoded slate shadows inside .selection-glass-surface: `0 18px 54px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.09), 0 2px 10px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.035)` (index.css:686-687). @theme defines no --shadow-* tokens.
issues.glassImpact: Liquid glass derives depth from blur + shadow, not 1px borders; without an elevation ramp every surface must be re-tuned individually and will drift again. The pervasive border+faint-shadow pattern is border-instead-of-elevation.
issues.recommendation: Define a 3-4 step elevation token scale (shadow + optional bevel highlight) in @theme, mapped to the material tiers, and migrate the literal recipes.

issues.title: House motion tokens are phone-only in practice; desktop surfaces hardcode durations/curves and ignore the Motion preference
issues.evidence: buildMotionCssVariables zeroes only --app-motion-duration-{sheet,stack,chip} (607-617), but desktop surfaces never consume them: menu popups use "transition-[scale,opacity] duration-200 ease-out" with no motion-reduce variant (menu.tsx:65), dialog popups "duration-[240ms] ease-out" with no motion-reduce (dialog.tsx:78), ProjectSettingsDialog overrides to "duration-[320ms] ease-[cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)]" (1079), and toast uses a different curve entirely: "[transition:transform_.5s_cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),opacity_.5s,height_.15s]" (toast.tsx:557). Sheet does carry motion-reduce:transition-none (sheet.tsx:84), so coverage is inconsistent.
issues.recommendation: Extend the motion token vocabulary to desktop (popup/dialog/toast durations consuming --app-motion-duration-*), which makes the in-app Motion=Reduced preference and OS setting actually govern desktop chrome; unify on the house ease.

issues.title: Custom primary applies one hex to both schemes with no dark-mode lightness adjustment
issues.evidence: buildPrimaryColorCssRule emits `:root, :root.dark { --primary: ${primaryColor}; --ring: ${primaryColor}; --primary-foreground: ${primaryForeground}; }` (634-640). The built-in pair lightens primary for dark (oklch 0.488 -> 0.588, index.css:378/417); the custom default Indigo #4f46e5 lands around 3:1 against the near-black dark background, and --chat-link tracks --primary (index.css:397), so chat links inherit the shortfall.
issues.recommendation: Derive a dark-scheme variant (e.g. oklch lightness floor via color-mix toward white) instead of reusing the raw hex in :root.dark.

issues.title: Terminal hardcodes its entire ANSI/cursor/selection palette and requires an opaque background
issues.evidence: terminalThemeFromApp branches only on the .dark class and returns fixed values — cursor "rgb(180, 203, 255)", selectionBackground "rgba(180, 203, 255, 0.25)", 16 hardcoded ANSI colors per scheme (229-281) — so Nord/Dracula/GitHub theme users get a foreign terminal palette in a coding-agent app where the terminal is a primary surface. Background falls back to "rgb(14, 18, 24)" when the computed drawer color is transparent (212, 220-223).
issues.glassImpact: xterm panes are opaque slabs; under a glass drawer they will punch an opaque rectangle through the material. The transparent-color fallback confirms the opaque-background assumption is load-bearing.
issues.recommendation: Derive at least background/foreground/selection/cursor from tokens (they already read computed styles — extend to the rest via a small token-to-ANSI bridge), and decide explicitly whether terminal surfaces are exempt from the material system.

issues.title: THEME_TOKEN_NAMES advertises radius/font tokens that tokensToCss silently drops
issues.evidence: THEME_TOKEN_NAMES includes "radius", "font-family-sans", "font-family-mono", "font-size-base" (types.ts:35-38), but tokensToCss filters them out via GLOBAL_APPEARANCE_TOKEN_NAMES (registry.ts:22-27, 236-238). An imported theme carrying a radius or font does nothing, with no warning. Separately, the appearance layer emits `--radius-${token}: ... !important` (appearancePreferences.ts:435), so no later layer could override the derived steps anyway.
issues.recommendation: Either remove these from THEME_TOKEN_NAMES (with import-time migration) or surface 'controlled by Appearance settings' when a theme carries them. Keep the single-ownership rule — appearance owns type/radius — but make it visible.

issues.title: --chat-link is documented as a theme override point but is not themable
issues.evidence: index.css:393-397 says "override this token alone to give links their own color" for `--chat-link: var(--primary)`, but "chat-link" is absent from THEME_TOKEN_NAMES (types.ts:1-39) and tokensToCss rejects unknown names (registry.ts:237), so no custom theme can set it.
issues.recommendation: Add chat-link to the allow-list (kind: color) or delete the override claim from the comment.

issues.title: ComposerStashPicker stacks app-surface with bg-popover/96 — the Material machinery is dead code there
issues.evidence: className="app-surface relative overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border/80 bg-popover/96 shadow-lg/8 backdrop-blur-xs". .app-surface lives in @layer components (index.css:539) while bg-popover/96 is a utility; the utilities layer wins regardless of class order, so the surface is pinned at 96% alpha at every Material step and app-surface never paints.
issues.recommendation: Drop the hardcoded alpha (and blur) and let the surface class own the material; lint for app-surface combined with bg-* utilities.

issues.title: ::selection is never styled — UA default selection clashes with custom themes
issues.evidence: grep for "::selection" across src returns zero hits, while scrollbars (511-525) and caret (color-scheme, 300/409) are themed. On Dracula/Nord/High Contrast the stock blue selection highlight ignores the palette; on High Contrast it can approach illegibility over yellow accents.
issues.recommendation: Add a token-driven ::selection (e.g. color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 25%, transparent)) so themes and the glass palette carry through text selection.

issues.title: Horizontal scrollbars are unstyled-height: only width is set on ::-webkit-scrollbar
issues.evidence: `::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 6px; }` (511-513) sets no height, so horizontal scrollbars (diff tables, chat code blocks with overflow-x: auto, chat-markdown-table-scroll) render at the UA default ~15px with the custom thumb — visibly fatter than the 6px vertical bars.
issues.recommendation: Add `height: 6px` (and consider a shared thin-scrollbar utility instead of the bespoke .model-picker-list and .markdown-file-link-tooltip-scroll blocks at 1360-1371/1189-1205).

issues.title: Literal black/white color utilities where tokens exist (swatch borders, lightbox scrim)
issues.evidence: The swatch-ring literal "border border-black/10 shadow-xs dark:border-white/20" is repeated in AppearanceSettings.tsx:970 and 1035, ProviderInstanceCard.tsx:223, and AddProviderInstanceDialog.tsx:412. ExpandedImageDialog uses a hardcoded "bg-black/75" scrim (63) while a themable scrim system exists (--app-sheet-backdrop-alpha, index.css:567-569). (AccountSettings.tsx:854 bg-white around the QR code is a justified exception — scanners need white.)
issues.recommendation: Promote the swatch ring to a shared class/token and route the lightbox scrim through the backdrop token so reduced-transparency enforcement reaches it.

issues.title: Ad-hoc z-index registers: toast at 9999, phone interstitial at 120, overlays at 50
issues.evidence: Toasts use "z-[calc(9999-var(--toast-index))]" (toast.tsx:557); the phone get-app interstitial uses "z-[120]" (PhoneGetAppInterstitial.tsx:27, PhoneGetAppInterstitialBackdrop.tsx:28); every dialog/sheet/popover overlay sits at z-50. There is no layering scale token.
issues.glassImpact: A glass redesign reorders stacking (backdrop-filter creates stacking contexts); magic numbers like 9999 make the final z-order emergent rather than designed.
issues.recommendation: Define a small named z-scale (base/panel/overlay/toast) as tokens before introducing new glass stacking contexts.

issues.title: PlanSidebar puts backdrop-blur on a static in-flow panel with nothing scrolling beneath it
issues.evidence: "flex min-h-0 flex-col backdrop-blur" (120) with panel mode "my-3 mr-3 w-[340px] shrink-0 self-start ... bg-card/90 ... supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-card/75" (122) — an in-flow flex sibling, not an overlay. Its backdrop samples only the static chrome background, so the blur pays a persistent backdrop-root/offscreen pass for near-zero visual effect. Note also the ThemeEditor sticky header's backdrop-filter (261) nests inside the project-glass-surface SettingsDialog popup (SettingsDialog.tsx:213), stacking two backdrop roots.
issues.glassImpact: Backdrop roots multiply under a glass system; the redesign needs a rule for when a surface earns a filter (overlays over scrollable content) versus a plain translucent fill.
issues.recommendation: Drop the blur from in-flow panels (keep the alpha), and budget nested backdrop roots deliberately in the new material tiers.

issues.title: Font stack: 14 @font-face declarations with mixed variable/static families and missing Atkinson mid-weights
issues.evidence: 14 @font-face blocks (index.css:10-132). Every declared family maps to a selectable option (6 sans / 6 mono, appearancePreferences.ts:30-94) and loads lazily via font-display: swap — no upfront cost issue. But IBM Plex Mono ships four static faces (400/500/600/700, lines 98-132) while every other family is a single variable file, and Atkinson Hyperlegible ships only 400/700 (45-61), so the UI's pervasive font-medium (500) and font-semibold (600) synthesize faux weights for Atkinson users — notable since it's the accessibility-focused option.
issues.recommendation: Swap IBM Plex Mono and Atkinson to their variable releases (@fontsource-variable) so weight rendering is uniform across all selectable families.

issues.title: Chart series palette is fixed oklch values, independent of theme and scheme
issues.evidence: CHART_COLORS = ["oklch(0.62 0.19 264)", "oklch(0.70 0.12 195)", ...] (14-21) — eight hardcoded series colors used in both schemes and under every theme; a Nord or High Contrast user gets the stock purple-blue ramp, and none of it routes through --primary or the status tokens.
issues.recommendation: Seed series 1 from --primary and expose the ramp as --chart-1..8 tokens (shadcn convention) so themes can restyle statistics.

verdicts.title: Sidebar color tokens don't exist — bg-sidebar/text-sidebar-foreground/border-sidebar-border compile to nothing
verdicts.note: index.css is the only stylesheet (main.tsx imports it alone, no @plugin/@config/@source) and its @theme block (lines 134-193) defines no --color-sidebar/--color-sidebar-foreground/--color-sidebar-border/--color-sidebar-accent; no --sidebar* color var exists anywhere (only unrelated --sidebar-status-text-* shimmer vars and the inline --sidebar-width). Tailwind v4 emits nothing for color utilities outside the theme namespace, so bg-sidebar (sidebar.tsx:156,214,232,302,584), text-sidebar-foreground, border-sidebar-border, hover:after:bg-sidebar-border (581), bg-sidebar-border (657) and hover:bg-sidebar-accent (713) are all no-op classes. These components are live (AppSidebarLayout.tsx, ChatRightPanel.tsx import Sidebar/SidebarRail), so the sidebar genuinely has no background of its own and the rail hover indicator paints nothing. THEME_TOKEN_NAMES (types.ts) contains no sidebar entries either.

verdicts.title: Root chrome is stamped opaque — html/body background plus runtime inline-style stamping block a translucent window
verdicts.note: Verified exactly as cited: index.css @layer base sets html and body background-color to var(--app-chrome-background) (199-206), and syncBrowserChromeTheme (useTheme.ts:92-104) writes the resolved computed color as inline styles on document.documentElement and document.body plus the theme-color meta. normalizeThemeColor (70-82) only nulls fully-transparent values, so any solid surface color is stamped on every applyTheme call (module load, theme/appearance change, system-scheme change). Because the stamping is inline JS style, CSS alone cannot override it; a vibrant/translucent Electron window would be occluded. This is a design-direction finding rather than a today-visible bug, but the code evidence is exact.

verdicts.title: At least 9 ad-hoc translucent surface recipes bypass the Material axis entirely
verdicts.note: All nine call sites verified verbatim: PlanSidebar.tsx:120-125 (bg-card/90, /75, /95 + backdrop-blur), ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:160 (bg-popover/96 backdrop-blur-xs), ThreadMessageSearchBar.tsx:50 (bg-popover/96 backdrop-blur), MessagesTimeline.tsx:770 (bg-popover/95 backdrop-blur), overviewLayouts.tsx:303 (bg-card/92, /85 backdrop-blur), settings/ThemeEditor.tsx:261 (bg-muted/72 backdrop-blur-sm), ChatView.tsx:3603 (bg-card/80 backdrop-blur), shell/phone/PhoneGetAppInterstitial.tsx:27 (bg-background/72 backdrop-blur-sm), auth/PairingRouteSurface.tsx:35 (bg-card/90 backdrop-blur-md). None reads --app-surface-opacity, and the prefers-reduced-transparency/forced-colors enforcement blocks in index.css only cover .app-surface/.app-muted-surface/.selection-glass-surface/.app-glass-surface/scrims — so these stay translucent at Material=Solid (the default, SURFACE_TRANSPARENCY_OPTIONS value "default" = 0%) and under reduced transparency.

verdicts.title: Desktop Material axis produces translucency without blur, and three competing glass recipes coexist
verdicts.note: dialog.tsx:81 gives default dialogs "app-surface" (index.css:539-541, color-mix alpha with no backdrop-filter) while the viewport carries only backdrop-blur-[2px] (dialog.tsx:40); the Glass step is 28% transparency (appearancePreferences.ts:118), yielding an unblurred 72%-alpha panel. selection-glass-surface has blur(10px) saturate(132%) contrast(1.03) and is used by dialogs-with-surface="glass", menus, popovers, selects, comboboxes, command; project-glass-surface adds blur(30px) saturate(142%) contrast(1.04). Only correction: surface="glass" appears at 12 call sites, not "six specific dialogs" — the inconsistency is broader than claimed, which strengthens rather than weakens the finding. The single-filter-token pattern cited (buildGlassTierVariables, blur<=0 → "none") exists at appearancePreferences.ts:550-560 as described.

verdicts.title: Terminal hardcodes its entire ANSI/cursor/selection palette and requires an opaque background
verdicts.note: terminalThemeFromApp (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:210-283) branches solely on document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark") and returns fixed cursor "rgb(180, 203, 255)", selectionBackground "rgba(180, 203, 255, 0.25)", and 16 hardcoded ANSI colors per scheme; only background/foreground come from computed drawer/body styles. Nord, Dracula, and GitHub are real built-in themes (themes/builtin.ts:149,321,349) that would get this foreign palette. normalizeComputedColor (197-208) falls back to opaque rgb(14, 18, 24)/rgb(255, 255, 255) whenever the computed color is transparent, confirming the opaque-background assumption.

verdicts.title: THEME_TOKEN_NAMES advertises radius/font tokens that tokensToCss silently drops
verdicts.note: THEME_TOKEN_NAMES includes radius, font-family-sans, font-family-mono, font-size-base (types.ts:34-38), but tokensToCss's first filter rejects anything in GLOBAL_APPEARANCE_TOKEN_NAMES — exactly those four names (registry.ts:22-27, 233-238) — with no warning path; GLOBAL_APPEARANCE_TOKEN_NAMES is referenced nowhere outside registry.ts, so no UI surfaces the drop. Separately verified that buildRadiusCssVariables emits every derived --radius-* step with !important (appearancePreferences.ts:431-440), so appearance ownership is absolute. An imported theme carrying these tokens validates but has no effect.

verdicts.title: --chat-link is documented as a theme override point but is not themable
verdicts.note: index.css:393-397 comment reads "override this token alone to give links their own color" in a sentence explicitly about themes ("a theme that restyles its accent restyles links for free"), yet "chat-link" is absent from THEME_TOKEN_NAMES (types.ts:1-39) and tokensToCss drops any name not in KNOWN_TOKEN_NAMES (registry.ts:237), so no built-in or custom theme can set it — links can only be recolored as a side effect of --primary. Low severity as claimed: the comment overpromises, the mechanism doesn't exist.

verdicts.title: ComposerStashPicker stacks app-surface with bg-popover/96 — the Material machinery is dead code there
verdicts.note: ComposerStashPicker.tsx:126 has className="app-surface ... bg-popover/96 shadow-lg/8 backdrop-blur-xs" exactly as cited. .app-surface is declared inside @layer components (index.css:538-541) while bg-popover/96 is a Tailwind v4 utility in the later utilities layer, so the utility wins regardless of class order and the element is pinned at 96% popover alpha at every Material step. Worse than claimed: the prefers-reduced-transparency override for .app-surface (index.css ~717) is also inside @layer components, so even the OS accessibility enforcement is defeated on this element.

verdicts.title: Horizontal scrollbars are unstyled-height: only width is set on ::-webkit-scrollbar
verdicts.note: index.css:511-513 is exactly `::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 6px; }` with no height property anywhere in the global block (only track/thumb rules follow), and horizontal-overflow containers exist (.chat-markdown-table-scroll with overflow-x: auto at index.css:1269-1271, .markdown-file-link-tooltip-scroll, overflow-x-auto in ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1423 and ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:807). In WebKit/Chromium, styling ::-webkit-scrollbar switches to custom scrollbars where the unset dimension keeps the UA default (~15px), so horizontal bars render fat with the custom thumb. The bespoke .model-picker-list (1360-1371) and .markdown-file-link-tooltip-scroll (1194ff) blocks cited in the recommendation also exist.

strengths: Control heights compose exactly across the family: Input inner h-8.5 + 2px wrapper border = 36px = Button h-9; sm sizes land on h-8/h-7 the same way (apps/web/src/components/ui/input.tsx:35, button.tsx:19). The sm: breakpoint doubles as a density axis (desktop denser) consistently everywhere.

One hairline-bevel convention on every raised surface: before:inset-0 rounded-[calc(radius-1px)] shadow-[0_1px_--theme(--color-black/4%)] light / dark:[0_-1px_--theme(--color-white/6%)] — card.tsx:11, popover.tsx:62, tooltip.tsx:41, toast.tsx:557, input.tsx:49, button.tsx:38. This is already a proto-material top-light and maps directly onto a glass inner bevel (selection-glass-surface uses inset 0 1px 0 white/.36 the same way, index.css:684).

selection-glass-surface (index.css:666-793) is a genuinely complete desktop glass material: light/dark variants, @supports no-backdrop-filter fallback, prefers-reduced-transparency fallback, and forced-colors fallback all handled centrally — the redesign has a proven pattern to extend.

Icon sizing grammar is uniform and override-friendly: [&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-4.5 sm:size-4 plus [&_svg:not([class*='opacity-'])]:opacity-80 across button, menu, select, toggle, autocomplete, combobox; badges step to 3.5/3 (badge.tsx:10).
Disabled grammar is one token nearly everywhere: disabled:opacity-64 / data-disabled:opacity-64 (button.tsx:11, badge.tsx:10, menu.tsx:136, checkbox.tsx:11, select.tsx:15).

44px touch-floor baked into primitives via pointer-coarse:after pseudo hit-expansion (button.tsx:11, toggle.tsx:9, select.tsx:24, autocomplete.tsx:55) and the documented TOUCH_INPUT_CLASS_NAME export (input.tsx:18-19).

Popup anatomy is one architecture everywhere: Portal > Positioner (z-50, owns position transitions) > Popup (origin-(--transform-origin) scale-98/opacity entrance) > inner viewport that owns scroll + padding — menu.tsx:53-75, select.tsx:124-163, popover.tsx:46-88. Scroll containers live INSIDE the surface, which is exactly right for glass.

Radius is a derived scale off one token (--radius-sm..--radius-4xl, index.css:170-176) so the appearance radius preference propagates; primitives consistently use rounded-lg for controls, rounded-2xl for dialogs/cards, rounded-sm for list rows.
data-slot attributes on every part enable the :has()-driven contextual spacing system (DialogPanel pt/pb reacting to header/footer presence, dialog.tsx:173) without prop plumbing.

ScrollArea's mask-based scrollFade (scroll-area.tsx:27-28) fades content against *whatever* is behind it — mask, not a painted gradient — so it is already glass-compatible, unlike the select scroll arrows.
patterns: Materials are named CSS component classes in @layer components (app-surface, app-muted-surface, selection-glass-surface, app-glass-surface-*) driven by :root variables that themes/appearancePreferences.ts rewrites (index.css:539-798, themes/appearancePreferences.ts:572-596). A desktop liquid-glass tier must be added as another variable-driven class here, never as inline blur utilities.

Both pseudo-elements are spoken for on interactive primitives: before: is the hairline/bevel layer (inset-0, radius-1px), after: is the pointer-coarse hit-target expander (button.tsx:11). New material layers need real elements or must respect this allocation.

Borders are alpha tokens (--border: black/8%, --input: black/10%, dark white/6-8%, index.css:387-427) and light-mode surfaces pair them with not-dark:bg-clip-padding so the translucent border doesn't stack over the fill (input.tsx:49, card.tsx:11). Any new surface must keep this or borders double-darken.

Two sanctioned focus grammars: clickables get focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-1 ring-offset-background (button.tsx:11, checkbox.tsx:11, switch.tsx:11); text fields get focus-visible:border-ring + ring-[3px] with ring-ring/24 halo (input.tsx:49, textarea.tsx:20, select.tsx:24, input-group.tsx:14, combobox.tsx:332). Invalid state layers destructive onto the same grammar (border-destructive/36 → /64 + ring-destructive/16 light /24 dark).
Popup surface opacity flows through --app-surface-opacity / --app-glass-*-popover-alpha (the Material axis); primitives never hardcode popover alpha — chart.tsx:100 is the one violation.

useRender + mergeProps + cva + data-slot is the component authoring pattern (button.tsx:56-72, card.tsx:8-22); Dropdown* aliases re-export Menu* names (menu.tsx:334-375) so both vocabularies must keep working.

sm: means desktop density, phone:/not-phone: custom variants mean presentation tier (index.css:7-8); these are orthogonal axes and primitives use both (dialog.tsx:73 phone: bottom-stick, button.tsx:19 sm: height).

Group/ToggleGroup merge adjacent controls via sibling selectors that assume each child keeps its border+before: structure (group.tsx:20-22, toggle-group.tsx:36-37) — restyling button borders will break the seam math.

The house motion tokens exist (--app-motion-ease: cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), --app-motion-duration-*, index.css:367-370) and are auto-zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion, but today only phone-tier components consume them; desktop primitives hardcode durations.
shortcut hints hide on coarse pointers via pointer-coarse:hidden with the stated invariant that every shortcut action keeps a button path (menu.tsx:269-271, command.tsx:208-210).

issues.title: Popover-family split into two materials: glass menus vs flat popovers
issues.evidence: MenuPopup, ContextMenuPopup, SelectPopup and ComboboxPopup ship 'selection-glass-surface' (menu.tsx:65, select.tsx:147, combobox.tsx:170) with blur(10px) saturate(132%); PopoverPopup default, Tooltip, AutocompletePopup and toasts ship 'app-surface not-dark:bg-clip-padding shadow-lg/5 before:shadow-[0_1px_--theme(--color-black/4%)]' (popover.tsx:62, tooltip.tsx:41, autocomplete.tsx:107, toast.tsx:557) — no blur, different shadow (shadow-lg/5 vs glass's 0 18px 54px rgb(15 23 42/0.09)). Popover/Command expose an opt-in surface="glass" prop while menus are unconditionally glass.
issues.recommendation: Pick one floating-surface material and make it the default for the whole popover family (menu, select, combobox, autocomplete, popover, tooltip, anchored toast); keep surface="default" as the escape hatch rather than the default. Unify shadow scale and border treatment in the material class, not per component.
issues.glassImpact: This is the central blocker: today a user sees a glass menu next to a flat popover from the same trigger row. The redesign target already exists (selection-glass-surface) but only half the family uses it.

issues.title: ComboboxPopup paints an opaque app-surface layer on top of its glass shell
issues.evidence: Outer span (line 170): "selection-glass-surface relative flex ... rounded-lg border"; inner ComboboxPrimitive.Popup (line 175): "app-surface flex max-h-[min(var(--available-height),23rem)] flex-1 flex-col". app-surface is color-mix(var(--popover) var(--app-surface-opacity)) with --app-surface-opacity: 100% by default (index.css:306,539), so the inner layer fully covers the glass background/gradients; only the glass border and outer shadow survive.
issues.recommendation: Drop app-surface from the inner popup (the shell already provides the surface) or move the glass class to the scrolling element like MenuPopup does (menu.tsx:65-71).
issues.glassImpact: Combobox popups render opaque while menus/selects render glass — visibly different today, and the double paint means at translucent Material steps you get two stacked alphas instead of the tuned glass value.

issues.title: Offset focus rings assume an opaque backdrop (ring-offset-background)
issues.evidence: "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-1 focus-visible:ring-offset-background" — the offset ring is implemented as a solid box-shadow of --background (var(--color-white) light / near-neutral-950 dark, index.css:371,410). Repeated in badge.tsx:10, checkbox.tsx:11, radio-group.tsx:22, switch.tsx:11, toggle.tsx:9, scroll-area.tsx:26, toast.tsx:102, color-picker.tsx:273.
issues.recommendation: For the glass tier, replace ring-offset with a non-painting separation: 2px ring of ring/full plus a 1px inner keyline (inset shadow), or outline with outline-offset (which doesn't paint the gap). Centralize as one focus utility so all ten call sites move together.
issues.glassImpact: On any translucent surface the 1px offset paints an opaque --background halo around every focused control — the single most visible artifact glass will surface.

issues.title: selection-glass-surface hardcodes backdrop-filter even when its background is fully opaque
issues.evidence: "-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(132%) contrast(1.03); backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(132%) contrast(1.03);" while --app-glass-light-popover-alpha defaults to 100% (index.css:315), so at the default Material step every menu/select/combobox pays a backdrop root + offscreen pass for an invisible effect. The phone tier explicitly avoids this: "the `Solid` step can resolve to `none` rather than to a zero-radius filter, which would still force a backdrop root" (index.css:582-583, appearancePreferences.ts:551-552).
issues.recommendation: Route the filter through a variable the Material axis resolves (none at Solid/default, blur(...) at translucent steps), exactly like --app-glass-<tier>-filter.
issues.glassImpact: The desktop glass tier should adopt the phone tier's filter-as-token discipline; as-is, adding more glass surfaces multiplies always-on backdrop roots.

issues.title: app-surface popovers go translucent without blur at the Material glass step
issues.evidence: app-surface = color-mix(var(--popover) var(--app-surface-opacity), transparent) with no backdrop-filter (index.css:539-541); at surfaceTransparency "glass" the opacity drops to 72% (appearancePreferences.ts:243,576). Dialogs compensate with viewport backdrop-blur-[2px] (dialog.tsx:40), but PopoverPopup default, Tooltip (tooltip.tsx:41), AutocompletePopup (autocomplete.tsx:107) and toasts (toast.tsx:557) float 72%-alpha text directly over scrolling content.
issues.recommendation: Any surface the Material axis makes translucent must gain the corresponding blur (or be excluded from the axis). Folding these surfaces into the unified glass material resolves both this and issue #1.
issues.glassImpact: Translucency-without-blur is the anti-pattern liquid glass exists to avoid; legibility collapses over busy transcript content.

issues.title: Select scroll arrows fade with an opaque popover gradient outside the glass surface
issues.evidence: ScrollUpArrow: "before:h-[200%] before:rounded-t-[calc(var(--radius-lg)-1px)] before:bg-linear-to-b before:from-50% before:from-popover/85" (and ScrollDownArrow line 156). The arrows are siblings of the 'selection-glass-surface' div (line 147), so the fade band is an 85%-popover paint sitting over the glass list.
issues.recommendation: Move the arrows inside the surface and use a mask-based fade (like ScrollArea's scrollFade, scroll-area.tsx:27-28) instead of a painted from-popover gradient.
issues.glassImpact: At translucent Material steps the fade band is visibly more opaque than the glass it covers — a seam right where content scrolls under the edge.

issues.title: Sidebar color tokens are never defined; bg-sidebar/sidebar-accent utilities emit no CSS
issues.evidence: sidebar-inner uses "bg-sidebar", menu buttons use "hover:bg-sidebar-accent hover:text-sidebar-accent-foreground" (line 764), the rail uses "hover:after:bg-sidebar-border" (line 581), and the outline variant uses shadow-[0_0_0_1px_hsl(var(--sidebar-border))] (line 779) — but no --color-sidebar* exists in @theme (index.css:134-193) and no --sidebar* var is declared anywhere (grep over src/*.css and themes/ finds only sidebar-status-text vars). Tailwind v4 therefore generates none of these utilities, and hsl(var(--sidebar-border)) is invalid twice over. Sidebar IS used (ChatRightPanel.tsx:17, ChatThreadRouteView.tsx).
issues.recommendation: Either declare the --sidebar token set in :root + @theme, or strip sidebar.tsx down to the tokens the app actually has (bg-background/accent). Decide before the redesign — dead styling here will silently swallow new glass classes too.
issues.glassImpact: The right-panel sidebar currently renders transparent by accident, not by design — the redesign cannot treat its current look as intentional baseline.

issues.title: Destructive menu items lose their destructive color exactly on highlight
issues.evidence: MenuItem: "data-highlighted:bg-accent/80 ... data-[variant=destructive]:text-destructive-foreground data-highlighted:text-accent-foreground" — when a destructive item is highlighted both text rules match at equal specificity, and there is no data-[variant=destructive]:data-highlighted:bg-destructive/* treatment at all, so the pre-click state reads as a normal accent row.
issues.recommendation: Add compound destructive-highlight styling (e.g. data-[variant=destructive]:data-highlighted:bg-destructive/10 and keep text-destructive-foreground winning), matching how destructive buttons keep their tone in every state (button.tsx:36).
issues.glassImpact: None directly, but destructive tinting on a glass row will need the compound variant anyway.

issues.title: Reduced-motion is honored by sheets only; dialogs, menus, popovers, toasts animate regardless
issues.evidence: SheetBackdrop/SheetPopup carry "motion-reduce:transition-none" (sheet.tsx:25,84); DialogPopup "transition-[scale,opacity,translate] duration-[240ms]" (dialog.tsx:78), MenuPopup "transition-[scale,opacity] duration-200" (menu.tsx:65), toast "[transition:transform_.5s_cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),...]" (toast.tsx:557), CollapsiblePanel duration-200 (collapsible.tsx:25) have no guard. The house --app-motion-duration-* tokens zero themselves under prefers-reduced-motion (index.css:446-452) but no desktop primitive references them.
issues.recommendation: Either add motion-reduce: guards uniformly or (better) migrate primitive durations onto var(--app-motion-duration-*) so the existing token collapse covers them.
issues.glassImpact: Glass entrances tend to add scale+blur transitions; wire them to the tokens now so reduced-motion stays one switch.

issues.title: Duration/easing zoo; the house curve is defined but unused by primitives
issues.evidence: Toast: ".5s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)"; dialogs/command: duration-[240ms] ease-out (dialog.tsx:78, command.tsx:75); menus/selects/popovers: duration-200 ease-out; sheet: duration-200 ease-in-out (sheet.tsx:84); sidebar width: duration-200 ease-linear (sidebar.tsx:277); disclosureMotion: 220ms ease-out; DialogBackdrop 240ms vs CommandDialogBackdrop 200ms. Meanwhile --app-motion-ease: cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (index.css:367) appears in zero ui/*.tsx files.
issues.recommendation: Collapse to a 3-step duration scale (fast ~120, base ~200, entrance ~240-260) on var(--app-motion-ease); two different expressive cubic-beziers (toast vs house) should not coexist.
issues.glassImpact: A material language reads as one system largely through consistent motion; this is cheap to fix pre-redesign.

issues.title: Hover-state transitions differ per primitive: buttons snap, selects animate
issues.evidence: SelectTrigger: "transition-[color,box-shadow,background-color]"; Button/Toggle: "transition-shadow" only (button.tsx:11, toggle.tsx:9) so bg-primary/90 hover snaps; AutocompleteClear: "transition-[color,background-color,box-shadow,opacity]" (autocomplete.tsx:208); ComboboxTrigger: "transition-opacity" (combobox.tsx:107); toast orb: "transition-[color,background-color,box-shadow]" (toast.tsx:101).
issues.recommendation: Standardize one transition property list per role (control surface vs icon button) — likely transition-[background-color,border-color,color,box-shadow] at the fast duration.
issues.glassImpact: Glass hover states (alpha/scrim shifts) will look broken if half the controls animate them and half snap.

issues.title: Third and fourth focus-ring grammars beyond the two sanctioned ones
issues.evidence: Color-picker sliders: "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40" (no offset, 40% alpha); select ghost: "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring" (select.tsx:26, no offset); sidebar: "outline-hidden ring-ring ... focus-visible:ring-2" (sidebar.tsx:764, no offset, and outline-hidden vs outline-none elsewhere).
issues.recommendation: Fold these into the clickable grammar (or the halo grammar for field-like widgets) when the focus treatment is redesigned for glass (see high-severity ring-offset issue).
issues.glassImpact: Focus is the state most likely to be redesigned for glass; four grammars means four migration paths unless collapsed first.

issues.title: ChartTooltipContent bypasses the surface system it claims to match
issues.evidence: Doc comment says "Tooltip body styled to match popovers" but the class is "min-w-32 rounded-lg border border-border bg-popover px-2.5 py-1.5 text-popover-foreground shadow-md" — opaque bg-popover (ignores --app-surface-opacity), full-strength shadow-md (family uses shadow-md/5), no hairline before:, rounded-lg while Tooltip is rounded-md (tooltip.tsx:41).
issues.recommendation: Reuse the tooltip surface classes (or the future glass material) instead of hand-rolling; align radius and shadow with tooltip.
issues.glassImpact: An opaque hardcoded popover will be the one flat rectangle left when everything else goes glass.

issues.title: Elevation is border-first: 1px border + /5-strength shadows on every floating surface
issues.evidence: AutocompletePopup: "rounded-lg border ... shadow-lg/5"; PopoverPopup: "border ... shadow-lg/5" (popover.tsx:59,62); Card "border ... shadow-xs/5" (card.tsx:11); Tooltip "border ... shadow-md/5" (tooltip.tsx:41). In dark mode --border is white/6% (index.css:426) so the border does nearly all separation work; the /5 shadows are almost invisible.
issues.recommendation: For the glass tier, shift separation to elevation + inner bevel (selection-glass-surface already does: 0 18px 54px + inset highlights, index.css:683-687) and demote the border to a light-catch edge; keep border-first only for the flat fallback.
issues.glassImpact: Border-instead-of-elevation is exactly what fights a translucent material — a 1px opaque-ish line around glass reads as a sticker edge.

issues.title: Overlay scrim architecture differs across the three modal primitives
issues.evidence: Sheet: scrim on Backdrop "app-sheet-backdrop ... backdrop-blur-sm" (black/32%); Dialog: invisible Backdrop (dialog.tsx:27 has no bg) with scrim on Viewport "app-dialog-viewport-scrim ... backdrop-blur-[2px]" (white 48% light / black 28% dark, dialog.tsx:40); Command: "app-command-backdrop" (background 60%, no blur, command.tsx:33). Fade durations also differ: 200ms vs 240ms.
issues.recommendation: One scrim recipe (tint token + blur token + duration) applied in one place per primitive; the Material axis already scales these alphas (appearancePreferences.ts:578-581) so a single utility is straightforward.
issues.glassImpact: Backdrop blur ancestors create backdrop roots that clip descendant glass sampling — dialog already special-cases surface="glass" to disable viewport blur (dialog.tsx:67); a unified scrim avoids per-primitive special cases.

issues.title: AlertDialog is the only overlay without a glass surface option
issues.evidence: AlertDialogPopup hardcodes "app-surface ... shadow-lg/5 ..." with no surface prop, while DialogPopup, CommandDialogPopup and PopoverPopup accept surface?: "default" | "glass" (dialog.tsx:60, command.tsx:67, popover.tsx:37).
issues.recommendation: Add the same surface prop (or inherit the unified material) so destructive confirms don't stay flat inside an otherwise glass app.
issues.glassImpact: Directly blocks completing the glass language for confirm flows.

issues.title: Dead utility: transition-shadows (plural) on ScrollArea viewport
issues.evidence: "overscroll-contain rounded-[inherit] outline-none transition-shadows focus-visible:ring-2" — Tailwind has transition-shadow, not transition-shadows; no CSS is emitted.
issues.recommendation: Fix to transition-shadow or drop it (rings aren't transitioned elsewhere).
issues.glassImpact: None.

issues.title: SVG namespace typo in SelectItem indicator
issues.evidence: xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1500/svg" (checkbox.tsx:33 and menu.tsx:189 use the correct .../2000/svg). React namespaces by JSX context so it renders, but the attribute is wrong in the DOM.
issues.recommendation: Correct to http://www.w3.org/2000/svg; consider extracting the shared check-path SVG (duplicated in menu, select, checkbox) into one component.
issues.glassImpact: None.

issues.title: Keyboard shortcuts styled two ways; Kbd radius bypasses the radius scale
issues.evidence: Kbd: "rounded bg-muted px-1 ... text-xs" chip (literal `rounded` = fixed 0.25rem, not the --radius-derived scale); MenuShortcut/CommandShortcut: bare "font-medium font-sans text-muted-foreground/72 text-xs tracking-widest" (menu.tsx:271, command.tsx:210 — identical duplicated implementations); input-group patches kbd corners ad hoc: "[&>kbd]:rounded-[calc(var(--radius)-5px)]" (input-group.tsx:25).
issues.recommendation: One shortcut presentation (chip or text) exposed from one module; use rounded-sm so the radius preference applies.
issues.glassImpact: Minor, but chips on glass need the shared treatment to pick up scrim-aware bg.

issues.title: Switch implementation forked inline in menu with different thumb size
issues.evidence: MenuCheckboxItem variant="switch" re-implements the whole switch: "[--thumb-size:--spacing(4)] ... sm:[--thumb-size:--spacing(3)]" (lines 171-175) vs Switch's "[--thumb-size:--spacing(5)] ... sm:[--thumb-size:--spacing(4)]" (switch.tsx:11), duplicating the squash animation string "[transition:translate_.15s,border-radius_.15s,scale_.1s_.1s,transform-origin_.15s]".
issues.recommendation: Extract switch visuals into a shared class/component with a size knob so the two stay in lockstep through the redesign.
issues.glassImpact: Redesigning the switch material will silently miss the menu copy.

issues.title: pointer-coarse hit-target pseudo not centered on badge and select
issues.evidence: Badge: "[button&,a&]:pointer-coarse:after:absolute ... after:min-h-11 after:min-w-11" and SelectTrigger: "pointer-coarse:after:absolute pointer-coarse:after:size-full pointer-coarse:after:min-h-11" (select.tsx:24, also missing min-w) — neither has the after:top-1/2 after:left-1/2 -translate-x/y-1/2 centering Button uses (button.tsx:11), so the expanded target grows from the top-left corner instead of around the control.
issues.recommendation: Copy Button's centered variant to badge/select (and Toggle already has it, toggle.tsx:9).
issues.glassImpact: None.

issues.title: Toast dismiss orb runs backdrop-blur inside an opacity-animating toast root
issues.evidence: Orb: "app-surface ... border-border/60 ... shadow-sm outline-none backdrop-blur-sm" sits inside Toast.Root which transitions opacity/transform (line 557); animated opacity makes the root a backdrop root, so the orb's blur samples only within the toast (visually nothing) while still forcing an offscreen pass. Also drifts: raw shadow-sm (family uses shadow-sm/5) and border-border/60 (family uses plain border).
issues.recommendation: Drop backdrop-blur-sm; align shadow/border with the family tokens.
issues.glassImpact: Demonstrates the nested-backdrop-root trap the glass tier must design around (no blur inside opacity/transform-animated ancestors).

issues.title: Sidebar disabled/hover grammar diverges from the system (opacity-50, no transition tokens)
issues.evidence: sidebarMenuButtonVariants: "disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 ... aria-disabled:opacity-50" and SidebarMenuSubButton line 960 same — everything else uses opacity-64 (button.tsx:11). Sidebar width motion is "transition-[width] duration-200 ease-linear" (line 277), the only ease-linear spatial animation in the family.

issues.title: List-row highlight alphas drift across menu/select/autocomplete/combobox

issues.evidence: GroupText: "before:shadow-[0_1px_--theme(--color-black/6%)]" — every other light-mode hairline is --color-black/4% (button.tsx:38, input.tsx:49, card.tsx:11).

issues.title: Switch disabled uses cursor-not-allowed while the family uses pointer-events-none
issues.evidence: "data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:opacity-64" vs Button "disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-64" (button.tsx:11) and Checkbox data-disabled:opacity-64 with no cursor rule (checkbox.tsx:11).

issues.glassImpact: None.

verdicts.title: Popover-family split into two materials: glass menus vs flat popovers
verdicts.note: Every cited line checks out: menu.tsx:65, select.tsx:147, combobox.tsx:170 ship selection-glass-surface (blur(10px) saturate(132%) contrast(1.03), 0 18px 54px shadow, inset white keylines) unconditionally, while popover.tsx:62 (default of an opt-in surface prop), tooltip.tsx:41, autocomplete.tsx:107, toast.tsx:557, and command.tsx:78 ship the flat app-surface + shadow-lg/5 + before:shadow hairline treatment. At the default Solid step the difference is border/shadow styling; at translucent Material steps appearancePreferences.ts lowers --app-surface-opacity and the popover alphas together, so app-surface popovers go translucent WITHOUT any backdrop blur next to blurred glass menus — the split is real and worst exactly where the redesign lives.

verdicts.title: ComboboxPopup paints an opaque app-surface layer on top of its glass shell
verdicts.note: combobox.tsx:168-181 verified: outer span has selection-glass-surface, inner ComboboxPrimitive.Popup has app-surface and (flex-1) fills the shell. index.css:539-541 defines app-surface as color-mix(var(--popover) var(--app-surface-opacity)) with 100% default (index.css:306), covering the glass background/gradients/inset highlights; only border and outer shadow survive. appearancePreferences.ts:576/585 sets --app-surface-opacity and --app-glass-*-popover-alpha to the SAME surfaceOpacity, so at translucent steps the two alphas stack instead of the tuned single value. One nuance: at the default Solid step both layers are the same opaque --popover color, so the visible delta today is subtle (lost inset highlights) — the stark divergence appears at translucent Material steps. AutocompletePopup (autocomplete.tsx:105-118) is structurally identical but has no such duplicate surface layer, confirming the inner app-surface is redundant.

verdicts.title: Offset focus rings assume an opaque backdrop (ring-offset-background)
verdicts.note: button.tsx:11 verified, and all other cited call sites exist (badge.tsx:10, checkbox.tsx:11, radio-group.tsx:22, switch.tsx:11, toggle.tsx:9, scroll-area.tsx:26, toast.tsx:102 plus 211/213, color-picker.tsx:273). Compiled the app's real index.css through the repo's Tailwind v4: ring-offset-background emits --tw-ring-offset-color: var(--color-background) and ring-offset-1 emits --tw-ring-offset-shadow: 0 0 0 var(--tw-ring-offset-width) var(--tw-ring-offset-color) — a solid, non-inset box-shadow paint. On any translucent surface the 1px gap renders as an opaque --background halo. Real CSS mechanism, correctly characterized as a glass-tier design defect rather than a bug visible on today's opaque surfaces.

verdicts.title: Select scroll arrows fade with an opaque popover gradient outside the glass surface
verdicts.note: select.tsx:141-160 verified: ScrollUpArrow/ScrollDownArrow are siblings of the selection-glass-surface div (line 147), overlaying it (z-50, before:inset-x-px/top-px sized to sit inside the popup border) with a painted before:bg-linear from-popover/85 fade. At the default Solid step popover/85 over opaque popover is invisible as a seam, but at translucent steps the band is a flat 85%-of-popover paint stacked on the lower-alpha glass — more opaque than the surface it fades into, with no mask-based alternative like ScrollArea's scrollFade (scroll-area.tsx:27-28) in use. Manifests only when scroll arrows render (overflowing selects) at translucent Material steps, matching the claimed medium severity.

verdicts.title: Sidebar color tokens are never defined; bg-sidebar/sidebar-accent utilities emit no CSS
verdicts.note: Verified by compiling the app's real index.css through the repo's own Tailwind v4: bg-sidebar, bg-sidebar-accent, and text-sidebar-foreground emit NO CSS (bg-background emits fine, proving the pipeline works). src/index.css is the only stylesheet, its @theme block (lines ~134-193) has no --color-sidebar*, no --sidebar color vars exist anywhere (only --sidebar-status-text-* and the --sidebar-width layout vars), and there is no tailwind.config.*, @config, or @plugin that could add them. sidebar.tsx:302 (bg-sidebar), :581 (hover:after:bg-sidebar-border), :764 (hover:bg-sidebar-accent), :779 (shadow-[0_0_0_1px_hsl(var(--sidebar-border))] — doubly invalid: undefined var inside hsl()) all confirmed, and Sidebar is genuinely used via ChatRightPanel.tsx:17. The sidebar background is transparent by accident.

verdicts.title: Dead utility: transition-shadows (plural) on ScrollArea viewport
verdicts.note: scroll-area.tsx:26 contains transition-shadows; compiling against the app's index.css with the repo's Tailwind v4 emits transition-shadow but nothing for transition-shadows, and no custom utility by that name exists in index.css. Dead class, no CSS emitted.

verdicts.title: SVG namespace typo in SelectItem indicator
verdicts.note: select.tsx:196 has xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1500/svg" while checkbox.tsx:33/48 and menu.tsx:189/225 use the correct 2000/svg. React creates the element in the SVG namespace from JSX context regardless, so it renders — the wrong value just lands in the DOM as a literal attribute. Cosmetic/correctness-in-markup only; low severity is right.

strengths: 52px chrome-row convention held across surfaces: SidebarChromeHeader h-[52px] (apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarChrome.tsx:101), ChatView header min-h-[52px] (apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:3425), NoActiveThreadState h-[52px] (apps/web/src/components/NoActiveThreadState.tsx:20), DiffPanelShell drag header h-[52px] (apps/web/src/components/DiffPanelShell.tsx:20) — one titlebar height to re-skin, not four.

WCO integration is centralized and reactive: a single `@custom-variant wco` (apps/web/src/index.css:5) driven by a real `geometrychange` listener (apps/web/src/lib/windowControlsOverlay.ts:21-40, wired in main.tsx:33), consumed purely in CSS via env(titlebar-area-*). A glass titlebar can build on this seam directly.

Drag-region handling is one class with an automatic interactive-descendant reset (`.drag-region` + `button/input/textarea/select/a` no-drag, apps/web/src/index.css:497-508) — robust, and all header controls audited are real <button>/<a> elements so the reset holds.

One resize primitive serves both shell edges: pointer-captured, rAF-throttled, localStorage-persisted SidebarRail with a `shouldAcceptWidth` constraint contract (apps/web/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:340-603); the right panel reuses it with min/max + composer-aware acceptance (apps/web/src/components/ChatRightPanel.tsx:254-259).

The presentation-tier seam is architecturally disciplined: SidebarProvider + route subtree stay mounted across tier flips, only chrome forks (apps/web/src/components/AppSidebarLayout.tsx:101-137) — a redesign can restyle chrome without touching workspace state.

Accessibility fallback discipline in the material layer: prefers-reduced-motion (index.css:446-452), prefers-reduced-transparency (index.css:717-767), and forced-colors (index.css:769-793) each pin every translucent surface opaque — the desktop glass tier inherits a proven enforcement pattern.

Session-tabs state is already presentation-agnostic: createSessionTabsSelector is cached, draft-aware, and worktree-scoped (apps/web/src/sessionTabs.selectors.ts:74-125); ChatView computes it on desktop for subscription prewarm (ChatView.tsx:842-882) — a desktop glass tab strip needs zero new state.

Sidebar density is genuinely restrained: h-7 text-xs thread rows (Sidebar.logic.ts:511), py-1.5 text-xs project headers, hover-revealed row actions that are also focus-within reachable (SidebarThreadRow.tsx:524) — quiet chrome worth preserving through the redesign.

A house motion system exists as tokens: --app-motion-ease cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) + per-role durations with OS/preference collapse (index.css:364-370, 446-452), and the right panel already animates on that exact curve (ChatRightPanel.tsx:112,242).
Empty-thread choreography is deliberate: hero sized to content between two flex-1 regions so hero + composer center as one block and yield to the keyboard (ChatView.tsx:3612-3655, 3791-3795).
patterns: Titlebar geometry only via the `wco:` variant + env(titlebar-area-x/width/height); the right-controls inset formula `calc(100vw-env(titlebar-area-width)-env(titlebar-area-x)+1em)` is the established (if duplicated) idiom (NoActiveThreadState.tsx:25, ChatView.tsx:3427, DiffPanelShell.tsx:20); sheets clear the titlebar with wco:mt-[env(titlebar-area-height)] (rightPanelLayout.ts:5).
Tier gating via `phone:` / `not-phone:` custom variants stamped as data-tier on :root (index.css:6-8); the phone tier is frozen — desktop work must be expressed through not-phone/default styles only.

Flat, border-separated surfaces: chrome uses border-r/border-b + bg-card/bg-background; elevation (shadow + .app-surface opacity) is reserved for the popup layer (menu/select/popover/toast/dialog). The shell itself never uses shadows or backdrop-filter today.

Three-layer token cascade: index.css :root defaults -> theme-registry <style> patch (themes/registry.ts) -> appearancePreferences <style> patch (themes/appearancePreferences.ts:379). Any new chrome material tokens must be plain :root custom properties so both patch layers can rewrite them.

Persisted layout via CSS var + localStorage: sidebar widths live in --sidebar-width on [data-slot=sidebar-wrapper] with keys chat_thread_sidebar_width (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:12) and chat_diff_sidebar_width (ChatRightPanel.tsx:31); resize logic queries [data-slot=...] structural attributes — keep data-slot/data-sidebar attributes stable.

Right panel presentation forks on width, not tier: (max-width: 980px) flips inline sidebar -> right sheet (rightPanelLayout.ts:3, ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:463-520); phone promotes to full-screen surface. Redesigned chrome must survive all three modes of the same panel content (DiffPanelMode: inline|sheet|sidebar|phone).
House ease is cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (= --app-motion-ease); new chrome motion should consume the token rather than repeat literals.

Shell chrome rows carry drag-region only on Electron and always pair it with a wco height + right-inset reservation — any new top-of-window strip must do all three (see DiffPanelShell.tsx:15-23 as the canonical helper).

prefers-reduced-transparency and forced-colors blocks in index.css @layer components are the single enforcement point for material fallbacks — extend those blocks, don't scatter per-component fallbacks.

The app html/body paint --app-chrome-background (index.css:199-206), a token aliased to --background (index.css:372) — this is the hook for a future vibrancy/transparent-window path and must stay the only body-level paint.

issues.title: Entire sidebar-* token family is undefined — every bg-sidebar/sidebar-accent/sidebar-border utility is dead CSS
issues.evidence: ui/sidebar.tsx is written in the shadcn sidebar dialect: `bg-sidebar text-sidebar-foreground` (lines 214, 232, 302), `hover:bg-sidebar-accent hover:text-sidebar-accent-foreground` (line 764 sidebarMenuButtonVariants, line 960 SidebarMenuSubButton), `bg-sidebar-border` (SidebarSeparator line 657), `hover:after:bg-sidebar-border` (rail, line 581). But index.css defines no `--color-sidebar*` in @theme (the only @theme blocks are index.css:134-193 and 1397; grep for `--color-sidebar` returns nothing), and Tailwind v4 CSS-first emits nothing for unknown color utilities. Visible casualties: worktree tree-child guide lines `before:bg-sidebar-border/70 after:bg-sidebar-border/70` render as invisible pseudo-elements (SidebarThreadRow.tsx:408), and the left resize rail has no hover indicator at all (see separate finding). The app only looks correct because call sites re-override with real tokens: AppSidebarLayout passes `bg-card` (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:121), thread rows use resolveThreadRowClassName's `bg-accent`/`bg-primary/22` (Sidebar.logic.ts:506-534), project headers use `hover:bg-accent` (SidebarProjectHeader.tsx:72).
issues.glassImpact: Directly blocks the redesign: the natural restyle target ('the sidebar tokens') does not exist. A liquid-glass sidebar needs the --color-sidebar* namespace declared in @theme and routed through the theme/appearance patch layers first, or every surface change must keep chasing per-call-site overrides.
issues.recommendation: Declare --color-sidebar, -foreground, -accent, -accent-foreground, -border, -ring in @theme mapped to :root vars (default them to card/accent/border), then delete the per-call-site re-implementations so the component layer becomes the single source of sidebar styling.

issues.title: Workspace panel's top strip sits in the titlebar zone with no drag region and no WCO control inset; the WCO reservation is applied one row too low
issues.evidence: The right panel is a fixed, full-height surface (`fixed inset-y-0 z-10 h-svh`, ui/sidebar.tsx:288), so its first row touches the window top edge in the frameless Electron shell. That first row is the workspace tab strip: `"flex shrink-0 items-center gap-1 border-b border-border bg-card/40 px-2", isPhoneSurface ? "h-14" : "h-12"` (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:790-793) — no drag-region, no wco:pr reservation, and the panel-close X button sits at its top right (lines 898-908) exactly where Windows/Linux WCO paints native window controls. Meanwhile DiffPanelShell still applies `drag-region h-[52px] ... wco:pr-[calc(100vw-env(titlebar-area-width)-env(titlebar-area-x)+1em)]` (DiffPanelShell.tsx:20) to its own header, which now renders 48px below the window top, inside the tab panel — reserving control space where no controls are.
issues.glassImpact: Any glass titlebar treatment must decide which strip is the real titlebar over the right panel; today two stacked headers (48px + 52px) both half-claim it. On WCO platforms the native controls visually overlap panel chrome — glass would make the collision more obvious.
issues.recommendation: Move the drag-region + wco height/right-inset treatment up to the workspace tab strip (make it the 52px chrome row), and demote DiffPanelShell's sidebar-mode header to a plain h-12 content toolbar.

issues.title: Desktop sidebar has no collapse affordance at all — offcanvas machinery is unreachable
issues.evidence: SidebarTrigger is exported but mounted nowhere (grep across src finds zero usages outside ui/sidebar.tsx). The rail explicitly suppresses toggling while resizable and open: `if (resolvedResizable && open) { event.preventDefault(); return; } toggleSidebar();` (ui/sidebar.tsx:539-543). No keybinding or command-palette entry calls toggleSidebar (grep 'toggleSidebar' finds only phone-sheet consumers of setOpenMobile). Yet AppSidebarLayout configures collapsible="offcanvas" (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:120) and the sidebar ships 200ms width/left transitions for a collapse that can never trigger (ui/sidebar.tsx:277, 288-291).
issues.glassImpact: An Apple-style glass shell usually trades chrome for content (collapsible sidebar, full-bleed content under glass); the primitive supports it but the shell never exposes it — the redesign must add the affordance, and doing so will hit the cookieStore bug below on web.
issues.recommendation: Either mount a collapse control (SidebarTrigger in SidebarChromeHeader + keybinding) or remove collapsible/offcanvas config and its transitions; decide before the redesign, since glass chrome layout depends on whether the sidebar can vanish.

issues.title: Sidebar open-state persistence writes an unguarded cookieStore cookie that is never read back
issues.evidence: setOpen does `await cookieStore.set({ expires: ..., name: SIDEBAR_COOKIE_NAME, ... })` (ui/sidebar.tsx:120-125). `cookieStore` is undefined in Firefox and older Safari, so the first collapse toggle throws a ReferenceError in the hosted web build; and SIDEBAR_COOKIE_NAME ('sidebar_state') is written but never read anywhere (grep shows only the two definition lines and the write), so persistence is a no-op even where the API exists — state always resets to defaultOpen.
issues.glassImpact: Currently latent (desktop never calls setOpen — see collapse-affordance finding) but becomes a live crash the moment the redesign adds a collapse button.
issues.recommendation: Replace with the existing getLocalStorageItem/setLocalStorageItem pattern already used for widths (ui/sidebar.tsx:385, 555) and read it back in SidebarProvider's initial state.

issues.title: Left and right resize rails: same primitive, divergent affordances — the left rail's hover indicator is invisible
issues.evidence: Left rail: `w-4 ... after:w-[2px] hover:after:bg-sidebar-border` + `in-data-[side=left]:cursor-w-resize` (ui/sidebar.tsx:581-583) — `bg-sidebar-border` is an undefined token (see high finding), so hovering the left rail shows nothing but a cursor change. Right rail overrides with real tokens: `w-5 cursor-ew-resize after:w-px after:bg-border/50 hover:after:bg-border focus-visible:ring-2` (ChatRightPanel.tsx:36-37). Widths (16px vs 20px), indicator weights (2px vs 1px), cursors (w-resize vs ew-resize), and visibility all differ for the identical interaction.
issues.glassImpact: Resize handles are exactly the kind of edge affordance a glass chrome must render as a consistent, subtle system; today one edge is invisible and the other ad hoc.
issues.recommendation: Give SidebarRail one styled default (visible 1px indicator on hover/drag, one cursor, one width) using real border tokens and delete the right panel's override.

issues.title: Three secondary chrome strips, three heights, three near-invisible tints
issues.evidence: Chat header: `border-b border-border bg-muted/24` at min-h-[52px] (ChatView.tsx:3422-3425) — --muted is already black/4% (index.css:382), so /24 yields ~1% black. Workspace tab strip: `border-b border-border bg-card/40` at h-12 (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:791-792) — card is white in light mode, so white/40 over white is invisible. Terminal tab strip: `h-7 ... border-border/70 border-b bg-muted/10` (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1419) — ~0.4% black. Same concept (a chrome bar capping a work surface) at 52px/48px/28px with three different, effectively-zero tints.
issues.glassImpact: These are the prime candidates for the glass chrome material; the redesign should collapse them into one 'toolbar material' token instead of three hand-tuned alphas that currently do nothing in light mode.
issues.recommendation: Define a single chrome-strip surface token (and a height scale of exactly two steps: titlebar 52px, toolbar 32-36px) and apply it to all three strips.

issues.title: Surface token topology is flat — background = card = popover in light mode — so chrome hierarchy is border-only and translucency has nothing to separate
issues.evidence: Light: `--background: var(--color-white); --card: var(--color-white); --popover: var(--color-white)` (index.css:371-377). Dark: card/popover are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--background) 98%, var(--color-white))` (index.css:413-415) — a 2% lift. The sidebar paints bg-card against bg-background content (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:121, ui/sidebar.tsx:609) — identical colors in light mode, separated solely by `border-r border-border` at 8% black. html/body paint opaque `--app-chrome-background: var(--background)` (index.css:200-206, 372).
issues.glassImpact: Fights translucency head-on: with everything the same opaque white there is no depth stack for glass to reveal, and no transparent-window path (body is hard-painted). A liquid-glass shell needs a real elevation ramp (base canvas < content < chrome material) expressed in tokens before any blur is added.
issues.recommendation: Introduce a canvas/base tone distinct from content surfaces (even 2-3% in light mode), keep --app-chrome-background as the sole body paint so a vibrancy/transparent-window variant can swap it, and let borders drop to hairline separators over material contrast.

issues.title: Desktop shell ignores the existing Material (surfaceTransparency) axis entirely — chrome is hard opaque
