issues.evidence: The Material preference rewrites --app-surface-opacity and the glass alphas (themes/appearancePreferences.ts:572-596), but the only desktop consumers are the popup layer (.app-surface in menu/select/popover/dialog/toast, index.css:539-541) and selection-glass-surface. The shell paints hard tokens: sidebar `bg-card` (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:121), right panel `bg-card` (ChatRightPanel.tsx:251), workspace panel `bg-background` (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:788), terminal drawer `bg-background` (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1397-1398), DiffPanelShell `bg-background` (DiffPanelShell.tsx:35).
issues.glassImpact: This is the central gap the redesign fills: the preference axis, its reduced-transparency enforcement, and the pattern (opacity via color-mix over a token) all exist — the chrome just never subscribes. Desktop glass should be new chrome-tier classes on this axis, not a parallel system.
issues.recommendation: Add desktop chrome material classes (e.g. app-chrome-surface for sidebar/headers/panels) whose alphas derive from the same surfaceTransparency step, defaulting to today's opaque values at the 'Solid' step.

issues.title: Shell motion is unsystematic: five durations, three easings, none using the house tokens; sidebar animates layout properties
issues.evidence: Left sidebar: `transition-[width] duration-200 ease-linear` (gap, ui/sidebar.tsx:277) and `transition-[left,right,width] duration-200 ease-linear` (container, line 288) — linear easing, layout-property animation. Right panel: 360ms `cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)` width (ChatRightPanel.tsx:242-243) with 300ms content translate (line 112) — two durations inside one gesture. Terminal drawer: `animate-[terminal-drawer-in_220ms_ease-out]` (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1398). Terminal tab indicator: 240ms ease-out (line 1426). Sidebar list auto-animate: 180ms ease-out (Sidebar.tsx:107-110). The tokens --app-motion-ease/--app-motion-duration-* (index.css:364-370) are consumed by none of these.
issues.glassImpact: Glass chrome makes motion much more visible (blurred backdrops shimmer during panel slides); animating width/left forces continuous relayout and, once backdrop-filter is present, continuous re-filtering — prefer transform-based slides on one shared duration/curve.
issues.recommendation: Route all shell transitions through --app-motion-ease with a two-step duration scale (chip ~120ms, panel ~260-360ms), and convert sidebar open/close to transform-based motion before adding blur.

issues.title: Resize affordances are pointer-only: rail is tabIndex=-1, terminal resizer is a bare div
issues.evidence: SidebarRail renders `<button ... tabIndex={-1}>` (ui/sidebar.tsx:576-601) — carries aria-label "Resize Sidebar" yet is unreachable by keyboard and has no arrow-key resize handling. The terminal drawer's resize handle is `<div className="absolute inset-x-0 top-0 z-20 h-1.5 cursor-row-resize" onPointerDown=... />` (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1403-1409) — no role, no label, no keyboard path at all.
issues.glassImpact: Neutral to glass, but the redesign will touch every one of these handles; fixing keyboard operability then is nearly free.
issues.recommendation: Make rails focusable separators (role=separator, aria-orientation, aria-valuenow) with arrow-key resizing; share one implementation across left rail, right rail, and terminal drawer.

issues.title: Chrome text leans on sub-contrast alpha ramps of muted-foreground (/40-/70)
issues.evidence: Toolbar controls: `text-muted-foreground/70 hover:text-foreground/80` at text-xs (BranchToolbar.tsx:161, 199) — muted-foreground light is ~#686868 (index.css:383); at 70% over white that is ~#9a9a9a ≈ 2.9:1. "No active thread" titlebar label: `text-xs text-muted-foreground/50` ≈ 2.2:1 (NoActiveThreadState.tsx:25). Sidebar timestamps: `text-muted-foreground/40` at 10px (SidebarThreadRow.tsx:606-610) ≈ 1.9:1. All are informative text, below WCAG 4.5:1.
issues.glassImpact: Directly blocks glass: translucent chrome lowers effective contrast further, and the phone material system's documented contrast guarantee (appearancePreferences.ts:483) has no desktop equivalent. These alphas set the baseline the glass material must still clear.
issues.recommendation: Replace alpha-modifier text colors with dedicated ramp tokens (e.g. muted-foreground-2/-3) tuned to ≥4.5:1 on the lightest surface they may sit over, then let the glass material's scrim guarantee the rest.

issues.title: Right-panel resize acceptance forces double reflow per animation frame
issues.evidence: shouldAcceptInlineSidebarWidth runs inside the rail's rAF loop and, per candidate width: writes `wrapper.style.setProperty("--sidebar-width", ...)`, then reads `window.getComputedStyle(composerViewport)`, `composerForm.getBoundingClientRect()`, two more getComputedStyle calls and scrollWidth/clientWidth (ChatRightPanel.tsx:196-223) — each read forces synchronous layout of the whole shell — then reverts the property (lines 225-229), forcing another layout when the accepted width is applied (ui/sidebar.tsx:493).
issues.glassImpact: With backdrop-filter chrome, every forced layout also invalidates the blur backdrop, so drag-resize would compound layout thrash with re-filtering; this needs to be cheap before glass lands.
issues.recommendation: Measure the composer's minimum once per drag-start (or observe via ResizeObserver) and evaluate candidate widths arithmetically instead of trial-applying the CSS var and reflowing.

issues.title: WCO header heights disagree: sidebar header is exact env height, chat header is min-height + padded content
issues.evidence: SidebarChromeHeader: `h-[52px] ... wco:h-[env(titlebar-area-height)]` — exact height (SidebarChrome.tsx:101). Chat header: `min-h-[52px] ... wco:min-h-[env(titlebar-area-height)]` (ChatView.tsx:3425) wrapping ChatHeader's own `py-3` content row (ChatHeader.tsx:141), which floors it near 52px regardless. With a Windows WCO titlebar of ~40px the sidebar header renders 40px and the adjacent chat header ~52px — their bottom borders (border-b) misalign across the sidebar seam. NoActiveThreadState uses a third variant: exact `h-[52px]` + wco height with items-center (NoActiveThreadState.tsx:20).
issues.glassImpact: A continuous glass titlebar spanning sidebar + content reads as one plane only if the strip heights match exactly; today they diverge under WCO.
issues.recommendation: Extract one TitlebarRow component (exact height 52px / env(titlebar-area-height), drag-region, wco insets) and use it in all three places.

issues.title: NoActiveThreadState empty card is nearly invisible and offers no action
issues.evidence: `rounded-3xl border border-border/55 bg-card/20 px-8 py-12 shadow-sm/5` (NoActiveThreadState.tsx:54) — bg-card/20 is white at 20% over a white background (invisible in light mode); border-border/55 is 55% of 8% black ≈ 4.4% — a barely-there outline. The copy instructs "Select an existing thread or create a new one to get started" (lines 56-59) but renders no button; the only new-thread affordances live in the sidebar.
issues.glassImpact: Empty states are where a glass hierarchy shows most (a floating material card against the canvas); the current card demonstrates the flat-token problem — translucent fills of white-on-white produce nothing.
issues.recommendation: Give the empty state a real surface (the future chrome material) and a primary "New thread" action wired to the same handler as SidebarNewThreadButton.

issues.title: Boot surfaces have no drag region — frameless window is undraggable while starting
issues.evidence: AppBootLoadingSurface renders `flex min-h-screen items-center justify-center bg-background` with no drag-region anywhere (AppBootLoadingSurface.tsx:6-9); SplashScreen likewise (`flex min-h-screen items-center justify-center bg-background`, SplashScreen.tsx:5). In the frameless Electron shell the window cannot be moved until the shell chrome mounts.
issues.glassImpact: None directly; worth folding into the shared TitlebarRow extraction so boot surfaces get the drag strip for free.
issues.recommendation: Add a top drag-region strip (h-[52px] wco:h-[env(titlebar-area-height)]) to boot/splash surfaces when isElectron.

issues.title: WCO right-inset formula and 52px constant are copy-pasted magic strings across the shell
issues.evidence: `wco:pr-[calc(100vw-env(titlebar-area-width)-env(titlebar-area-x)+1em)]` appears verbatim in DiffPanelShell.tsx:20, ChatView.tsx:3427, and NoActiveThreadState.tsx:25; `52px` appears as h-[52px]/min-h-[52px] in four files; the macOS traffic-light inset is a hardcoded `pl-[90px]` (SidebarChrome.tsx:101). ChatView's `reserveTitleBarControlInset` prop (ChatView.tsx:342, 413) is never passed by any caller — dead API guarding one of the copies.
issues.glassImpact: The glass titlebar will have to touch every copy; consolidating first shrinks the redesign diff and removes drift risk.
issues.recommendation: Promote the inset formula and titlebar height to CSS custom properties / a shared utility (like RIGHT_PANEL_SHEET_CLASS_NAME already does for sheets) and drop the unused prop.

issues.title: Session tabs exist only on the frozen phone tier; desktop pays the selector cost but renders no strip
issues.evidence: ChatView computes activeWorktreeSessionTabs on every tier (ChatView.tsx:842-853) and feeds useChatSessionTabsPrefetch (lines 879-882), but the only rendering consumer is the phone dock (`sessionTabs: activeWorktreeSessionTabs` inside the isPhoneTier-gated phoneThreadDock memo, lines 3370-3393). On desktop, switching between a worktree's sessions means round-tripping through the sidebar tree.
issues.glassImpact: A desktop session-tab strip in the chrome (the natural liquid-glass element) is nearly free: state, prefetch, and selection handler (handleSelectSessionTab, lines 857-877) already exist tier-agnostically.
issues.recommendation: Treat the desktop session-tab strip as an in-scope redesign candidate reusing the existing selector + handler; if rejected, gate the selector/prefetch to phone to stop paying for unused work.

issues.title: Content-layer glass already exists ad hoc — future chrome blur will nest backdrop roots over it
issues.evidence: The scroll-to-bottom pill uses `bg-card/80 ... ring-1 ring-inset ring-foreground/6 backdrop-blur` (ChatView.tsx:3603); ThreadMessageSearchBar and ComposerCommandMenu also carry backdrop-blur (grep hits); the popup layer relies on non-blur .app-surface opacity instead. So blur is used in the content layer but not the chrome layer — the inverse of a glass architecture, and the pill hand-rolls its material (bg-card/80 + ring) rather than using any shared class.
issues.glassImpact: Backdrop-filter on new chrome ancestors will change what these descendants' filters sample (backdrop-root nesting), risking double-blur or missing-blur artifacts in Chromium; the redesign needs a single rule for which layers may own backdrop-filter.
issues.recommendation: Fold floating content-layer elements (scroll pill, search bar) into the same material class system as the future chrome, and document one blur-owning layer per stacking context.

verdicts.title: Entire sidebar-* token family is undefined — every bg-sidebar/sidebar-accent/sidebar-border utility is dead CSS
verdicts.note: No --color-sidebar* token exists anywhere: index.css's two @theme blocks (134-193, 1397) define color tokens only for background/card/accent/etc., there is no tailwind.config.*, and Tailwind v4 emits nothing for color utilities without a matching --color-* theme key. ui/sidebar.tsx uses bg-sidebar/text-sidebar-foreground (214, 232, 302), hover:bg-sidebar-accent (779, 960-area), bg-sidebar-border (SidebarSeparator ~654), hover:after:bg-sidebar-border (rail, ~581) — all dead. Cited casualties verified: sidebar/SidebarThreadRow.tsx:408 guide lines (before/after:bg-sidebar-border/70) are invisible; AppSidebarLayout renders a plain <SidebarRail /> so the left rail hover indicator is dead (the right panel rail only works via RIGHT_PANEL_RESIZE_RAIL_CLASS_NAME's after:bg-border override); AppSidebarLayout.tsx:121 overrides with bg-card. Note the file is at src/components/sidebar/SidebarThreadRow.tsx, not src/components/SidebarThreadRow.tsx.

verdicts.title: Workspace panel's top strip sits in the titlebar zone with no drag region and no WCO control inset; the WCO reservation is applied one row too low
verdicts.note: Desktop route views (ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:479, DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:445) mount RightPanelInlineSidebar with mode="sidebar"; its Sidebar side="right" renders the fixed inset-y-0 z-10 h-svh container (ui/sidebar.tsx:288) with no transformed ancestor, so the panel's first row touches the window top. That row is ThreadWorkspacePanel's tab strip (lines 789-793: h-12, no drag-region, no wco classes) with the close X button at its right end (desktop branch ~898-908). DiffPanel/PreviewPanel then render DiffPanelShell whose sidebar-mode header applies drag-region h-[52px] + wco:pr reservation (DiffPanelShell.tsx:20) inside the tabpanel, ~48px below the window top. apps/desktop/src/main.ts:2671-2696 confirms frameless titleBarStyle hidden/hiddenInset + titleBarOverlay. The structural defect is exactly as described; actual native-control overlap occurs on WCO platforms (Windows/Linux), while on macOS the cost is a non-draggable top-right strip.

verdicts.title: Sidebar open-state persistence writes an unguarded cookieStore cookie that is never read back
verdicts.note: ui/sidebar.tsx:120-125 does an unguarded bare-global `await cookieStore.set(...)` inside setOpen (runs even on the controlled onOpenChange path), and repo-wide grep shows SIDEBAR_COOKIE_NAME/'sidebar_state' only at definition and write — SidebarProvider initializes solely from defaultOpen, so persistence is a no-op. setOpen is reachable via SidebarRail's click->toggleSidebar (line 543). One evidence caveat: cookieStore is no longer 'undefined in Firefox' generally (shipped in Firefox 132, late 2024; Safari 18.4) — the ReferenceError applies to older Firefox/Safari and non-secure contexts. The write-only persistence bug and the unguarded access pattern are real regardless.

verdicts.title: Boot surfaces have no drag region — frameless window is undraggable while starting
verdicts.note: AppBootLoadingSurface.tsx (lines 6-9) and SplashScreen.tsx (line 5) render min-h-screen centered surfaces with no drag-region class; a repo-wide grep shows drag-region only in DiffPanelShell, NoActiveThreadState, ChatView, and sidebar/SidebarChrome. __root.tsx uses AppBootLoadingSurface as the pre-mount and Suspense fallback surface (lines 161, 223, 237), and apps/desktop/src/main.ts sets titleBarStyle hidden/hiddenInset (frameless), so the window is undraggable until shell chrome mounts. Low severity as claimed.

strengths: Streaming performance architecture is excellent and must survive the redesign: split stable/streaming contexts so token updates never invalidate row memoization (apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:118-141), structural row sharing (useStableRows, 1684), and self-ticking timers that mutate textContent instead of committing React state every second (WorkingTimer/LiveMessageMeta, 1146-1194).

Adaptive streamed-text reveal (apps/web/src/hooks/useSmoothStreamedText.ts) — backlog-draining rAF cadence, low-pass velocity smoothing, snap-on-settle, surrogate-pair-safe slicing, and a full bypass under prefers-reduced-motion.

Clear role grammar with strong information density: user = right-aligned foreground/8 bubble, assistant = full-width plain prose, tool events = 12px muted icon rows, with progressive disclosure via turn folds and work-group recaps ('+N previous tool calls' summaries, MessagesTimeline.tsx:1261-1307). Distinction is achieved through layout and tone, not chrome — very compatible with a restrained glass language.

The composer is treated as the primary control with deliberate state design: fill never re-tints on hover/focus (documented rationale at apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:2257-2263), only focus lifts the shadow, drag-over gets an explicit ring, and stacking is disciplined via `relative isolate` + z-0/z-10 in ChatView.tsx:3676-3684.

The phone glass material layer (index.css:586-664) is a model implementation: filter+alpha+scrim token triples per tier, isolation for the scrim layer, @supports no-backdrop-filter fallback, prefers-reduced-transparency and forced-colors overrides all handled in one place. The desktop tier should copy this shape, not invent a new one.

Token hygiene at the base: --muted/--accent/--secondary/--border are alpha-based (index.css:380-388), which composites correctly over any translucent base; a dedicated --chat-link token tracks --primary (index.css:397).

Scroll UX is well-engineered: initialScrollAtEnd/maintainScrollAtEnd with live re-evaluation on content-size changes (MessagesTimeline.tsx:283-344), a glass scroll-to-bottom pill, and the hover minimap with per-item in-view marking.

Accessibility care in interaction flows: ApprovalCard announces via role=alert sr-only summary (chat/ApprovalCard.tsx:69), minimap is fully keyboard-operable (MessagesTimeline.tsx:692-711), reduced motion is dual-gated (media query in CSS + prefersReducedMotion prop threading in ChatView).
One house easing curve — cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) — is used essentially everywhere, so motion already feels like one system even though the durations are hardcoded.
patterns: Web phone tier is FROZEN: [data-tier="phone"] variants, GlassSurface.tsx, and the phone Build-mode exemption (ChatView.tsx:542-544) must not be extended or altered by the desktop redesign.

Appearance is a CSS-variable patch pipeline: theme registry JSON and themes/appearancePreferences.ts inject a <style> that rewrites tokens (appearancePreferences.ts:379). Any hardcoded palette literal (blue-400, rose-500, sky-500…) permanently escapes all 9 themes, the optional primary override, and the Material axis — components must consume tokens only.

Cascade trap: surface classes like .app-surface live in @layer components (index.css:539) and LOSE to any Tailwind bg-* utility on the same node. Never combine them (see ComposerStashPicker.tsx:126 for the existing violation).

The ui-kit elevation grammar is: app-surface + border + shadow-lg/5 + hairline before: highlight (dark: before:shadow-[0_-1px_white/6%]) — popover.tsx:62, tooltip.tsx:41, dialog.tsx:81. A desktop glass primitive should extend this grammar, not add an eighth recipe.

Composer focus protocol is load-bearing: data-chat-composer-collapsed-controls markers plus onFocusCapture/onBlurCapture on the surface (ChatComposer.tsx:2271-2321) govern phone collapse; data-chat-composer-form / -footer / -actions='right' attributes are queried by the right-panel resize guard (ChatRightPanel.tsx:192-223). Restructuring the composer DOM must preserve all of these hooks.

The transcript is a LegendList virtualized scroller (MessagesTimeline.tsx:525-543): rows self-measure, estimatedItemSize=90, maintainScrollAtEnd, keyExtractor by row id, hidden scrollbar by design. Glass bars must be positioned as overlays outside the scroller, never as in-list sticky rows.

Bottom bar padding composes env(safe-area-inset-bottom) with --app-keyboard-inset via max() (ChatView.tsx:3667-3674); the header doubles as the Electron drag region with wco: titlebar-area insets (3423-3429). Floating glass replacements must reproduce both.
Elapsed/timestamp text updates flow through visibleSecondTicker subscriptions writing textContent directly — do not convert to React state.

Motion tokens exist (--app-motion-ease, --app-motion-duration-* at index.css:367-370, rewritten by the Motion preference) and there is a phone dock clearance pattern (.app-dock-scroll-clearance, index.css:650) that is the template for 'content scrolls under a floating bar'.

issues.title: Markdown headings in assistant replies render as plain body text
issues.evidence: `.chat-markdown p, .chat-markdown ul, .chat-markdown ol, .chat-markdown blockquote, .chat-markdown pre, .chat-markdown table { margin: 0.65rem 0; }` is the complete block list — there are no `.chat-markdown h1`–`h6` rules anywhere in the stylesheet, and ChatMarkdown.tsx's components map (lines 618-757) overrides only p/li/blockquote/table/td/th/a/pre. Tailwind v4 preflight sets h1-h6 to `font-size: inherit; font-weight: inherit` with zero margin, so `## Section` in an assistant reply (or in ProposedPlanCard's plan markdown) is visually indistinguishable from a body line.
issues.recommendation: Add a heading ramp to .chat-markdown (e.g. h1 1.25em/weight 650, h2 1.125em/620, h3 1em/600, top margin ~1.25em, bottom ~0.4em) plus hr styling. This is the single biggest reading-rhythm defect in the transcript and should land before any material work.
issues.glassImpact: None directly, but the redesign's typography pass must fix this first — glass polish on top of flattened document structure would be lipstick.

issues.title: Chat chrome is layout-reserved slabs; nothing ever scrolls under the header or composer, so glass has no backdrop
issues.evidence: Root: `flex min-h-0 min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden bg-background`; header (3418-3422) `border-b border-border bg-muted/24` and the input bar (3667) are flex siblings; the LegendList scroller is `h-full` inside only the messages wrapper (`relative flex min-h-0 flex-1`, 3497; list class MessagesTimeline.tsx:540). The only true overlays today are the scroll pill, search bar, minimap, and floating overview.
issues.recommendation: For the liquid-glass tier, extend the transcript scroller to own the full column and float the header and composer over it (bottom bar via the .app-dock-scroll-clearance pattern from index.css:650 so the last row can clear it). This is the structural prerequisite everything else hangs on.
issues.glassImpact: Blocking: backdrop-filter on the header/composer currently samples flat background, so a glass treatment would be invisible. Separation is border-driven (border-b, border-t) throughout — the redesign replaces borders with material depth.

issues.title: Seven-plus hand-rolled translucency recipes on chat overlays, all bypassing the shared app-surface Material axis
issues.evidence: Command menu `border-border/80 bg-popover/96 shadow-lg/8 backdrop-blur-xs`; scroll pill `bg-card/80 … ring-foreground/6 backdrop-blur` (ChatView.tsx:3603); search bar `border-border/80 bg-popover/96 shadow-lg/12 backdrop-blur` (ThreadMessageSearchBar.tsx:50); minimap preview `border-border/70 bg-popover/95 shadow-xl shadow-black/25 backdrop-blur` (MessagesTimeline.tsx:770); overview panel `backdrop-blur` + `bg-card/90 supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-card/75` sidebar / `bg-card/95 dark:bg-card/90` floating (PlanSidebar.tsx:120-125); stash picker `bg-popover/96 backdrop-blur-xs` (ComposerStashPicker.tsx:126). Meanwhile every ui-kit popup uses `app-surface` driven by --app-surface-opacity (popover.tsx:62, tooltip.tsx:41, toast.tsx:557).
issues.recommendation: Define one desktop glass surface primitive (mirroring the phone .app-glass-surface tier architecture with filter/alpha/scrim tokens) and migrate all seven chat overlays onto it. This is the redesign's core consolidation move.
issues.glassImpact: These are precisely the surfaces that become liquid glass; today each hand-picks alpha (80/90/95/96), blur (xs vs default), border alpha (60/70/80) and shadow independently, and none respond to the existing surface-transparency preference.

issues.title: Stash picker's app-surface is dead code — hardcoded utility wins the cascade, Material preference ignored
issues.evidence: `className="app-surface relative overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border/80 bg-popover/96 shadow-lg/8 backdrop-blur-xs"` — .app-surface is declared in @layer components (index.css:539) while bg-popover/96 is a utilities-layer declaration, so the Material-axis background never applies.
issues.recommendation: Remove `bg-popover/96` (keeping app-surface) or vice versa; add a lint/grep rule against combining app-surface with bg-* utilities.
issues.glassImpact: Demonstrates the cascade trap the whole glass migration must avoid: the material class silently loses to any leftover bg utility.

issues.title: Conversation column uses two widths, and queued messages ignore the column entirely
issues.evidence: Composer form `relative mx-auto w-full min-w-0 max-w-208` (52rem) and ComposerBannerStack `mx-auto mb-2 max-w-208` (ComposerBannerStack.tsx:107) vs transcript rows `mx-auto w-full min-w-0 max-w-3xl` (48rem, MessagesTimeline.tsx:506) and ProviderStatusBanner/ThreadErrorBanner `pt-3 mx-auto max-w-3xl` (ProviderStatusBanner.tsx:24, ThreadErrorBanner.tsx:14). ComposerQueuedMessages has no width constraint at all (`mb-2 rounded-lg border border-border/60 bg-muted/30 p-1.5`, ComposerQueuedMessages.tsx:33) so it spans the full window width above a centered 52rem composer.
issues.recommendation: Introduce a single conversation-measure token; align composer, banners, queued messages, and transcript to it (or make the composer's extra width an explicit, consistent +2rem design decision applied to all bottom-stack elements).
issues.glassImpact: A floating glass composer makes edge misalignment far more conspicuous than the current flush layout does.

issues.title: Banner stack cap always wears the warning tone, and hover-revealed banners are near-transparent over the transcript
issues.evidence: Both cap variants hardcode `border-warning/24 bg-background/96` (lines 137, 147) regardless of the stacked banners' variants (error/info/success). The revealed stack (`absolute inset-x-0 bottom-[calc(100%+0.5rem)] z-20`, line 176) renders Alert variants whose fills are 4% tints with no opaque base — `error: "border-destructive/32 bg-destructive/4"` etc. (ui/alert.tsx:15-18) — so with 2+ banners the hover-revealed ones composite illegibly over timeline text.
issues.recommendation: Derive cap tone from items[1].variant; give overlay-positioned alerts an opaque or glass base layer beneath the 4% tint.
issues.glassImpact: The 4%-tint alert design assumes a plain background behind it — exactly the assumption a translucent redesign must remove; these banners need the shared glass base.

issues.title: Composer loses edge definition in dark theme: borderless with black-on-black shadows
issues.evidence: Surface: `border-0 bg-card/82 shadow-[0_6px_18px_rgba(0,0,0,0.06),0_1px_3px_rgba(0,0,0,0.05)]`. Dark `--card` is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--background) 98%, var(--color-white))` (index.css:413) — ~2% lighter than the page — and hardcoded rgba-black shadows vanish on a near-black backdrop, so the primary control's resting elevation reads as almost nothing in dark mode.
issues.recommendation: Adopt the ui-kit's theme-aware edge (hairline `dark:before:shadow-[0_-1px_white/6%]` top highlight, e.g. popover.tsx:62) or a token-driven shadow pair; do not encode literal black shadows on themable surfaces.
issues.glassImpact: Glass lives or dies on its specular edge; define the light/dark rim treatment once in the material primitive.

issues.title: Selection states hardcode blue-400/blue-500 — poor light-mode contrast and detached from --primary
issues.evidence: Selected option `border-blue-500/40 bg-blue-500/8`, shortcut kbd `bg-blue-500/20 text-blue-400` (169), check `text-blue-400` (184); plan-toggle open state `text-blue-400 hover:text-blue-300` (ComposerFooter.tsx:359). tailwind blue-400 on white is ≈2.6:1, and none of these track --primary (oklch(0.488 0.217 264)) or a theme's primary override.
issues.recommendation: Switch to text-primary / border-primary/40 / bg-primary/8 so themes and the appearance primary override apply, and light-mode contrast is met by the token.

issues.title: Stop button and mode/reasoning chips use off-token palette colors, including a gradient chip
issues.evidence: Stop: `bg-rose-500/90 text-white hover:bg-rose-500` (while --destructive exists); full-access runtime mode `text-orange-700 … dark:text-orange-400` (ComposerFooter.tsx:238-239); ThinkingChip `bg-sky-500/15 text-sky-800 dark:bg-sky-500/20 dark:text-sky-300` (ThinkingChip.tsx:32); ReasoningChip a slate→blue→indigo→violet→fuchsia ramp with ultra as `bg-gradient-to-br from-pink-500/20 to-purple-500/25 … ring-fuchsia-500/25` (ReasoningChip.tsx:37-53); skill chips fuchsia (composerInlineChip.ts:9).
issues.recommendation: Map to tokens (destructive for stop, warning for full-access) or declare deliberate accent tokens in the theme layer. In a restrained zinc system the pink/purple gradient 'Ultra' chip is the one flourish to retire; a filled solid tone communicates the same tier.

issues.title: Placeholder and message-meta text sit far below readable contrast, via ad-hoc alpha dilution
issues.evidence: Composer placeholder `text-muted-foreground/35` (muted-foreground at 35% over white ≈ 1.4:1) — this carries the primary affordance copy 'Ask anything, @tag files/folders, or use / to show available commands'. Assistant meta is `text-[10px] text-muted-foreground/30` (MessagesTimeline.tsx:1027) while user timestamps are `text-[11px] text-muted-foreground/50` (990) — two different treatments for the same concept, both failing any contrast floor.
issues.recommendation: Floor incidental text at ~muted-foreground/70, unify user/assistant meta into one style, and express de-emphasis through the tone scale rather than stacking opacities.
issues.glassImpact: Alpha-diluted text over translucent surfaces inherits whatever scrolls beneath — contrast becomes content-dependent. Replace opacity dimming with explicit tone tokens before introducing glass.

issues.title: Micro-typography is an ad-hoc ramp: seven sub-14px sizes and ~13 foreground alpha steps in the timeline alone
issues.evidence: `text-[9px] uppercase tracking-[0.16em]` (work-log label), `font-mono text-[9px] leading-3` (edit chips, 2144), `text-[10px]` (1027), `text-[11px]` (990, 2292, 2316), `text-[12px]` (1299, 2034), `text-[13px]` (TURN_FOLD_LABEL, 1080), plus text-xs/text-sm; foreground/muted-foreground alphas /92, /88, /85, /84, /80, /75, /72, /70, /56, /55, /50, /45, /35, /30 across the same file.
issues.recommendation: Define a 3-4 step caption/label/body ramp and a 3-step text-tone scale as tokens, then sweep the chat surface. A materials redesign without a type/tone system will re-litigate every one of these values.

issues.title: Overline labels styled four different ways; the approval header — the most urgent interrupt — is both the loudest and the least toned
issues.evidence: `PENDING APPROVAL` (14px!), vs `text-[10px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.08em]` (ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:184), `text-[9px] uppercase tracking-[0.16em]` (MessagesTimeline.tsx:1224), `text-[10px] … tracking-[0.14em]` (compaction pill, 1322), `text-[11px] font-semibold tracking-widest uppercase` (ComposerPendingUserInputPanel.tsx:137). The approval header also carries no warning tone — plain foreground — while routine info banners get tinted icons.
issues.recommendation: One overline token (size/weight/tracking); give the approval state a warning-toned treatment proportional to its importance rather than sheer size.

issues.title: Assistant prose — the primary reading surface — is dimmer than user text, and set on a ~105-char measure
issues.evidence: `"chat-markdown w-full min-w-0 text-sm leading-relaxed text-foreground/80"` vs user body `text-sm leading-relaxed text-foreground` (MessagesTimeline.tsx:1624). Rows cap at `max-w-3xl` (48rem, MessagesTimeline.tsx:506), which at 14px yields ~100-115 characters per line.
issues.recommendation: Lift assistant body to full foreground (or a dedicated ≥90% chat-body tone) — the answer is the product. Consider a slightly narrower measure or 15px body on the desktop tier as part of the typography pass.

issues.title: Header separation is border + a tint that is ~1% with default tokens but explodes under theme patches
issues.evidence: `border-b border-border bg-muted/24` — light --muted is `--alpha(var(--color-black) / 4%)` (index.css:382), so /24 composites to ~0.96% black (invisible); a registry theme that overrides --muted with an opaque value suddenly renders a 24% wash. Alpha-of-alpha token layering makes the header's appearance theme-dependent in an unintended way.
issues.recommendation: Give the header its own surface token. In the glass pass this bar (which is also the Electron drag region with wco: titlebar-area insets, 3423-3429) is the prime translucent candidate — keep drag-region and inset behavior intact.
issues.glassImpact: Prime glass candidate #1; currently border-instead-of-elevation with a fragile tint.

issues.title: PlanSidebar applies backdrop-blur unconditionally, even in modes where nothing renders beneath it
issues.evidence: Base class `"flex min-h-0 flex-col backdrop-blur"` applies to all three modes; only mode="floating" (absolute top-3 right-3 z-40 overlay, ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:146) actually has transcript behind it. The inline sidebar and sheet modes pay a compositing layer + backdrop-root for a blur of flat background.
issues.recommendation: Scope the blur to the floating mode; inline surfaces need only the tint.
issues.glassImpact: Every stray backdrop-filter becomes a nested backdrop root once a glass ancestor exists — descendants' blurs then sample already-blurred content. Audit and minimize filter roots before layering the material system.

issues.title: Motion durations/easings are hardcoded per component instead of using the declared motion tokens
issues.evidence: `duration-[320ms] ease-[cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)]` (overview sidebar), 260ms (line 151), 300ms (ChatRightPanel.tsx:112), 360ms (ChatRightPanel.tsx:242/251), banner exit `transition: transform 220ms ease-in, opacity 220ms ease-in` (ComposerBannerStack.tsx:24 — the only plain ease-in exit in the surface), disclosure 220ms (index.css:843). The token layer already defines --app-motion-ease and --app-motion-duration-* (index.css:367-370), rewritten by the Motion preference — desktop chat components never reference them.
issues.recommendation: Bind chat-surface transitions to the motion tokens so the appearance Motion axis governs the desktop tier, and normalize exits onto the house curve (the ease-in banner exit visibly differs from every other dismissal).

issues.title: hover:scale on send/stop buttons rides transition-all and is not reduced-motion gated
issues.evidence: Send: `transition-all duration-150 hover:bg-primary hover:scale-105`; stop: `transition-all duration-150 hover:bg-rose-500 hover:scale-105` (127). transition-all animates transform for prefers-reduced-motion users, and this is the only scale-on-hover affordance in the surface.
issues.recommendation: Drop the scale (or add motion-reduce:transform-none) and transition only background-color/color — matches the restrained language everywhere else.

issues.title: Transcript has no scrollbar at all; position feedback exists only via the pointer-fine minimap above a size threshold
issues.evidence: List: `[scrollbar-width:none] … [&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden` (with a comment noting the gutter removal is deliberate); the minimap returns null when `items.length < TIMELINE_MINIMAP_MIN_ITEMS` (661) and is `hidden … [@media(pointer:fine)]:block` (667). Short-to-medium threads on desktop, and everything on touch/large-text setups, give zero scroll-position feedback beyond the scroll pill.
issues.recommendation: Keep the minimal aesthetic but add an overlay-style scrollbar (auto-hiding) or lower the minimap threshold; a glass redesign that also floats the chrome will further remove spatial anchors, making some position indicator more important.

issues.title: Two disclosure-row implementations: div role=button vs native button
issues.evidence: ExpandableWorkEntryRow: `<div role="button" tabIndex={0} aria-expanded … onKeyDown Enter/Space>`; WorkGroupToggleTimelineRow (1284) and TurnFoldTimelineRow (1088) use `<button type="button" aria-expanded>` for the same interaction pattern.
issues.recommendation: Standardize on the native button element (the manual keydown replication is correct today but is duplicate surface area).

issues.title: Collapsed plan-card fade is painted more opaque than its own surface
issues.evidence: Fade overlay `bg-linear-to-t from-card/95 via-card/80 to-transparent` sits on a `bg-card/70` card (140) — the fade's terminal opacity exceeds the surface it fades into, producing a visible band wherever card ≠ background.
issues.recommendation: Use mask-image on the clipped content instead of a painted gradient.
issues.glassImpact: Painted fades assume opaque surfaces; masks are the only fade mechanism that survives translucency — establish that convention now.

issues.title: Focus-ring grammar varies in width and alpha across adjacent controls
issues.evidence: `focus-visible:ring-1 focus-visible:ring-ring/60` (message action buttons) vs `ring-2 ring-ring/70` (tool rows 1094/2241) vs `ring-2 ring-ring` (ComposerQueuedMessages.tsx:16) vs `ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40` (resize rail, ChatRightPanel.tsx:37) vs `ring-1 ring-ring/70` (headerChrome.ts:4).
issues.recommendation: One focus token pair (width + alpha) for the surface; ring-2/ring/70 inset appears to be the de facto majority.

issues.title: Static user bubbles animate elevation on row hover with no attached action
issues.evidence: Bubble: `bg-foreground/8 … shadow-md/5 transition-[background-color,box-shadow] duration-200 group-hover:bg-foreground/10 group-hover:shadow-lg/8` — the bubble itself is inert (copy/revert live in the row below), so pointer travel across the transcript makes content pulse.
issues.recommendation: Reserve the hover response for the action row (which already reveals via opacity); keep the bubble visually stable.

issues.title: Ad-hoc z-index ladder across chat overlays
issues.evidence: Scroll pill z-30, search bar z-30 (ThreadMessageSearchBar.tsx:48), minimap z-40 (MessagesTimeline.tsx:667), floating overview z-40 (ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:146), banner stack escalates to z-50 on hover (ComposerBannerStack.tsx:111) — above the search bar and every other overlay — stash badge z-20 (ComposerStashBadge.tsx:20), command menu z-20 (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:368), composer z-0/z-10 inside `isolate`.
issues.recommendation: Codify a small named z-scale for the chat surface (content < floating chrome < transient overlays < interrupts). Glass layering multiplies stacking contexts (every backdrop-filter and isolate creates one), so implicit ladders will break.

verdicts.title: Markdown headings in assistant replies render as plain body text
verdicts.note: No h1-h6 rules anywhere in apps/web/src/index.css (the .chat-markdown block at 1037-1290 covers only p/ul/ol/blockquote/pre/table/li/a/code/th/td); ChatMarkdown.tsx's components map (apps/web/src/components/ChatMarkdown.tsx:618-757) overrides only p/li/blockquote/table/td/th/a/pre. Tailwind v4 preflight is active via @import "tailwindcss" and resets headings to font-size/weight inherit with zero margin; no typography plugin or prose class exists. Headings inside the text-sm wrapper are visually identical to body text.

verdicts.title: Chat chrome is layout-reserved slabs; nothing ever scrolls under the header or composer, so glass has no backdrop
verdicts.note: All cited facts verified: ChatView.tsx:3416 root flex-col overflow-hidden bg-background; header 3418-3430 (border-b border-border bg-muted/24) and input bar 3667 are flex siblings of the messages wrapper (relative flex min-h-0 flex-1, 3497); the LegendList scroller is h-full scoped to the messages wrapper only (chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:540). backdrop-filter on header/composer would sample flat background — content never passes beneath them. Design finding, but factually accurate.

verdicts.title: Seven-plus hand-rolled translucency recipes on chat overlays, all bypassing the shared app-surface Material axis
verdicts.note: Every cited recipe matched verbatim: ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:160 (bg-popover/96 backdrop-blur-xs), ChatView.tsx:3603 scroll pill (bg-card/80 ring-foreground/6), ThreadMessageSearchBar.tsx:50 (bg-popover/96), MessagesTimeline.tsx:770 minimap (bg-popover/95 shadow-black/25), PlanSidebar.tsx:120-126 (three mode-specific recipes), ComposerStashPicker.tsx:126. ui-kit popover.tsx:62 / tooltip.tsx:41 / toast.tsx:557 use app-surface driven by --app-surface-opacity (index.css:539), which is injected by the appearance-preferences system; none of the chat overlays respond to it (the stash picker's app-surface is dead per the next finding).

verdicts.title: Stash picker's app-surface is dead code — hardcoded utility wins the cascade, Material preference ignored
verdicts.note: ComposerStashPicker.tsx:126 combines app-surface with bg-popover/96. .app-surface is declared in @layer components (index.css:538-541) and only sets background-color; Tailwind v4's layer order (theme, base, components, utilities) makes the utilities-layer bg-popover/96 win unconditionally. The Material/surface-opacity preference therefore never affects this surface.

verdicts.title: Banner stack cap always wears the warning tone, and hover-revealed banners are near-transparent over the transcript
verdicts.note: Both cap variants hardcode border-warning/24 bg-background/96 (ComposerBannerStack.tsx ~137-138 and ~147) with no derivation from stacked items' variants (error/info/success items exist per the ComposerBannerStackItem type). The revealed stack (absolute bottom-[calc(100%+0.5rem)] z-20, ~176) renders bare Alert variants whose fills are 4% tints over transparent (ui/alert.tsx:15-18) with no opaque base; ChatView.tsx:3657-3666's own comment confirms banners overlap the timeline upward, so revealed banners composite over transcript text.

strengths: DiffPanelShell is a genuinely shared shell: DiffPanel and PreviewPanel render through one header/body contract with matching loading affordances (DiffPanelHeaderSkeleton, DiffPanelLoadingState with role=status/aria-live, apps/web/src/components/DiffPanelShell.tsx:53-99) — the right seam to hang a glass chrome on.

The diff material bridge is exactly right for a translucent redesign: third-party @pierre/diffs surfaces are recolored purely via tokens + color-mix (--card/--background/--success/--destructive) injected as unsafeCSS into shadow roots (apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:64-111), so the opaque editor surface tracks all 9 themes automatically; PreviewPanel's file header uses the identical color-mix(var(--card) 94%, var(--foreground)) formula as the diff [data-file-info] strip (PreviewPanel.tsx:625, DiffPanel.tsx:98-102) — one coherent code-surface chrome.

ThreadWorkspacePanel's tab bar is a proper ARIA tabs implementation: roving tabindex, aria-controls/labelledby wiring, Arrow/Home/End navigation (apps/web/src/components/ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:737-772, 824-836).

Panel motion is disciplined where it exists: one easing family cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) at 300-360ms, motion-reduce guards, and exit-animation content kept mounted but gated with inert + content-visibility (PreviewTreeMotionFrame PreviewPanel.tsx:154-183, RightPanelContentMotionFrame ChatRightPanel.tsx:107-118, resolveInactivePanelContentVisibilityStyle).

Terminal engineering is strong: rAF-batched output writes (createTerminalOutputBatcher), snapshot+event-replay hydration, live font-family resync on appearance-preference change (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:447-453), and xterm instances survive chrome changes via the hidden-div persistence pattern (chat/ChatTerminalShell.tsx:167).

Disabled git actions always explain themselves — every disabled menu item and quick action carries a computed reason surfaced via hover popover (getMenuActionDisabledReason, GitActionsControl.tsx:287-354, 1834-1861); provider-aware terminology/icons are centralized in sourceControlPresentation.ts rather than scattered.

The diff turn strip's scroll affordances are carefully built: arrow-state-synced mask-image fade, wheel-to-horizontal mapping, overscroll containment, auto-scroll to selected chip (DiffPanel.tsx:856-919, 964-978).
patterns: Presentation is driven by DiffPanelMode ('inline'|'sheet'|'sidebar'|'phone'); Electron drag-region chrome activates only when isElectron && mode !== 'sheet' && mode !== 'phone' (DiffPanelShell.tsx:16,30). Any new chrome must reproduce this matrix — and the phone branches inside these same files are FROZEN.

Drag-region hygiene is two-layer: interactive clusters get explicit [-webkit-app-region:no-drag] wrappers (DiffPanel.tsx:923,1036; PreviewPanel.tsx:550,561) and index.css:502-508 auto-no-drags button/input/textarea/select/a inside .drag-region.

wco (window-controls-overlay) variant + env(titlebar-area-*) arithmetic pervades top-row chrome (index.css:5, ChatView.tsx:3425-3427, rightPanelLayout.ts RIGHT_PANEL_SHEET_CLASS_NAME) — glass chrome must keep these offsets working.

Diff/preview code surfaces are themed exclusively through unsafeCSS strings injected into @pierre/diffs shadow roots plus .diff-panel-viewport/.diff-render-file bridge rules (DiffPanel.tsx:64-145, PreviewPanel.tsx:62-85, index.css:1295-1304); a material change must go through these strings, not component classes.

Panel visibility is router search-param state (diff=1, preview=1, workspaceOpen/workspaceTab); panels stay mounted through exit animations via useDelayedUnmount + inert + contain-intrinsic-size (ChatRightPanel.tsx:172-179, RightPanelSheet.tsx:12-15). Terminal state lives in terminalStateStore keyed by scoped thread ref — the redesign must not unmount PersistentThreadTerminalDrawer's hidden subtree (ChatTerminalShell.tsx:167).

Appearance preferences patch :root tokens with !important (fonts, --radius-* set from a radius axis, surface transparency, motion durations — themes/appearancePreferences.ts:379,432-445); components must consume tokens (rounded-md, text-xs, semantic colors) to stay patchable — raw px sizes and raw Tailwind palette colors silently opt out of the whole system.

The phone-tier glass material already defines the token grammar a desktop tier should mirror: tier → (backdrop-filter, background alpha, scrim alpha) triples with an @supports fallback and isolation-based scrim layering (index.css:586-660) — desktop glass should extend this token shape, not invent a parallel one.

Chat-header control chrome is a shared recipe (HEADER_CHROME_BUTTON/ICON_BUTTON_CLASS_NAME, components/chat/headerChrome.ts) — panel headers currently do NOT use it; a redesign should unify on it or a successor.
Ease family cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) with 300-360ms durations is the established panel enter/exit signature; reduced-motion guards are expected on every transition.

issues.title: User-facing copy leaks internal 'refName' identifier throughout git actions
issues.evidence: Button label "Commit on new refName" (line 2214); "Warning: default refName" (2080); dialog title fallback "Run action on default refName?" (2241); menu hint "Detached HEAD: create and checkout a refName to enable push..." (2030-2033); disabled reasons "Detached HEAD: checkout a refName before pushing." (319) and "...before creating a ${terminology.singular}." (339).
issues.recommendation: Replace every user-facing 'refName' with 'branch' (the same file already says 'Checkout feature branch & continue' at 2267 — the vocabulary exists). Grep-audit GitActionsControl.logic.ts copy too.
issues.glassImpact: None — pure copy bug, but it ships in the panel this redesign will re-skin, so fix it in the same pass.

issues.title: Stale Electron drag-region: draggable strip is the second row of the right panel, not the row in the titlebar band
issues.evidence: In mode='sidebar' the shell header gets "drag-region h-[52px] border-b border-border wco:h-[env(titlebar-area-height)] wco:pr-[calc(100vw-env(titlebar-area-width)-env(titlebar-area-x)+1em)]" (lines 16-21). But ThreadWorkspacePanel now renders its own tab bar ABOVE it (h-12, ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:789-794, no drag-region), inside a Sidebar that is 'fixed inset-y-0 h-svh' (ui/sidebar.tsx:288). So the row actually beside the window controls is not draggable, while a mid-panel toolbar is — and the wco right-padding reserves window-control space on a row 48px below the controls.
issues.recommendation: Move the drag-region + wco offsets to the workspace tab bar (the true top row) and strip them from DiffPanelShell; make drag ownership a property of whatever chrome strip is top-of-window, decided once in the shell.
issues.glassImpact: Glass chrome concentrates identity in the top strip; the drag/wco model must live there. This stale layering must be resolved before the chrome can be rebuilt as one material.

issues.title: Four different header-chrome treatments across chat / workspace / diff-preview / terminal
issues.evidence: Chat header: "drag-region flex min-h-[52px] ... border-b border-border bg-muted/24" (ChatView.tsx:3421-3427). Workspace tab bar: "h-12 border-b border-border bg-card/40" (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:791). Diff/preview shell header: h-12 / h-[52px] on the shell's plain bg-background (DiffPanelShell.tsx:20-21,35). Terminal tab strip: "h-7 ... border-border/70 border-b bg-muted/10" (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1419). Search sub-toolbar: "border-b border-border/50 bg-card/40" (DiffPanel.tsx:1133); preview filter row: "border-b border-border/60 p-2" (PreviewPanel.tsx:669).
issues.recommendation: Define one chrome-strip material token pair (surface + hairline) with two heights (primary 48/52px, secondary 28-32px) and apply it to all panel headers/toolbars; today's four tints (muted/24, card/40, background, muted/10) and three heights make a unified glass material impossible without per-panel exceptions.
issues.glassImpact: This is the core blocker: 'liquid glass' means these strips become one shared material. Every divergent tint/height becomes a visible seam once translucency reveals what is behind each strip.

issues.title: Panel chrome is opaque, triple-painted, and separated by borders only — headers are layout siblings so glass would have nothing to blur
issues.evidence: Opaque stack: Sidebar forces 'bg-card' (ChatRightPanel.tsx:251), ThreadWorkspacePanel root repaints 'flex h-full ... bg-background' (line 788), DiffPanelShell repaints 'bg-background' (line 35), terminal drawer repaints 'bg-background' (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1397-1398). All separation is hairline borders ('border-l border-border', 'border-b border-border') — no elevation/scrim model. Headers and toolbars are shrink-0 flex siblings stacked above the scrollers (DiffPanel.tsx:1110-1234), so content never scrolls beneath chrome.
issues.recommendation: For the desktop glass tier: collapse to one opaque base per panel (the code surface), make chrome strips overlay the scroller (position sticky/absolute with scroll-padding) so backdrop-filter has real content behind it, and replace border-only separation with the material's scrim+hairline recipe. Keep the editors themselves opaque.
issues.glassImpact: Direct: applying backdrop-filter to today's strips would blur a solid background — the 'glass' would read as flat tint. The layout relationship between chrome and scroll containers must change, which is why this is high.

issues.title: Terminal cannot sit under translucent chrome: xterm theme is scraped from computed background and the canvas is created without allowTransparency
issues.evidence: new Terminal({ cursorBlink: true, lineHeight: 1.2, fontSize: 12, scrollback: 5_000, ... theme: terminalThemeFromApp(mount) }) — no allowTransparency (423-430; repo-wide grep for allowTransparency: none). terminalThemeFromApp reads getComputedStyle(drawerSurface).backgroundColor (210-227) and normalizeComputedColor only rejects fully transparent values ('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)', 197-208) — any semi-transparent glass background (e.g. rgba(14,18,24,0.6)) would be fed to an opaque-only canvas. The full ANSI palette is also hardcoded rgb() (229-282), ignoring the 9-theme registry beyond bg/fg.
issues.recommendation: Treat the xterm viewport as an intentionally opaque editor surface: give it an explicit opaque token (not a computed-style scrape of its chrome ancestor), and only frame it with glass. If translucent terminal is ever wanted, it requires allowTransparency + rgba background, at a WebGL-renderer perf cost. Consider deriving the ANSI palette from theme tokens while there.
issues.glassImpact: Blocker for putting glass anywhere in the terminal drawer's ancestry: the theme scrape walks to '.thread-terminal-drawer' or body, so a translucent drawer background silently corrupts the terminal's rendered background color.

issues.title: Double chrome: workspace tab bar stacks on each panel's own full-height header, with duplicated or missing identity
issues.evidence: Active 'review' renders <DiffPanel mode={props.mode}/> (916-917) whose shell adds a second h-12/h-[52px] header row; 'files' adds PreviewPanel's header containing its own title block ('File Preview' + uppercase 'Workspace tree' subtitle, PreviewPanel.tsx:551-553) even though the tab above already says Files; 'review' has no title at all — its header is only the turn-chip strip + toggles (DiffPanel.tsx:921-1092); 'terminal' adds a third-height h-7 strip. Result: ~96px of stacked chrome on review/files and three header grammars.
issues.recommendation: Merge each panel's toolbar into (or directly under) the workspace tab row as a single secondary strip: tabs left, panel-specific actions right. Delete PreviewPanel's redundant title; give the merged strip one height.
issues.glassImpact: Glass rewards a single continuous chrome plate; two stacked opaque bars of different tints is the opposite. Merging is a prerequisite for the material to read as one piece.

issues.title: Sheet-mode header clamps to titlebar height even though the sheet is already offset below the titlebar (wco builds)
issues.evidence: Non-drag branch: "h-12 wco:max-h-[env(titlebar-area-height)]" (line 21) — but RIGHT_PANEL_SHEET_CLASS_NAME already pushes the whole sheet down with "wco:mt-[env(titlebar-area-height)] wco:h-[calc(100%-env(titlebar-area-height))]" (rightPanelLayout.ts:5). On a Windows WCO titlebar (~32px) the sheet header renders squished to 32px while its content (turn chips, size-7 toggles + py) was designed for 48px.
issues.recommendation: Drop the wco:max-h clamp from the non-drag branch — it only makes sense for a header that actually occupies the titlebar band.
issues.glassImpact: Minor, but the redesign will rewrite exactly this class string; carry the fix along.

issues.title: Three unrelated resize affordances for panel splits
issues.evidence: PreviewPanel tree: 8px-wide <button> with visible center line, 'w-2 cursor-ew-resize ... hover:bg-accent/40' + 'w-px bg-border/80' (784-799). Right panel: SidebarRail 'w-5 cursor-ew-resize after:w-px after:bg-border/50 hover:after:bg-border focus-visible:ring-2' (ChatRightPanel.tsx:36-37). Terminal drawer: invisible plain div 'absolute inset-x-0 top-0 z-20 h-1.5 cursor-row-resize' (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1403-1409). Three hit widths (8/20/6px), three visual treatments, three implementations.
issues.recommendation: Extract one ResizeHandle primitive (orientation prop, shared hit size, hover/focus treatment, persistence callback) and use it in all three places.
issues.glassImpact: Split handles sit exactly on the seams a glass chrome makes visible; they need one consistent treatment or the seams will look accidental.

issues.title: Resize handles are not keyboard-operable; terminal handle is not even focusable
issues.evidence: Terminal drawer resize: <div className="absolute inset-x-0 top-0 z-20 h-1.5 cursor-row-resize" onPointerDown=.../> — no role, no tabIndex, no aria (1403-1409). PreviewPanel's resizer is a <button aria-label="Resize workspace tree"> but handles only onPointerDown/Move/Up — arrow keys do nothing, and it lacks role='separator'/aria-valuenow (PreviewPanel.tsx:784-796).
issues.recommendation: In the shared ResizeHandle: role='separator', aria-orientation, aria-valuenow/min/max, and Arrow-key stepping (e.g. 16px, Shift for 64px).
issues.glassImpact: None directly; fold into the ResizeHandle extraction.

issues.title: Terminal tab close button is invisible to keyboard users and 14px on desktop
issues.evidence: className="inline-flex size-3.5 items-center justify-center rounded text-muted-foreground opacity-0 transition hover:bg-accent hover:text-foreground group-hover:opacity-100 pointer-coarse:...opacity-100..." — opacity-0 with only group-hover reveal, no focus-visible:opacity-100, so tabbing lands on an invisible 14x14px control.
issues.recommendation: Add focus-visible:opacity-100 (and group-focus-within:opacity-100); raise the desktop hit target to at least size-5 like the workspace tab close (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:857).
issues.glassImpact: None.

issues.title: Terminal tablist has no keyboard tab navigation and role='tab' sits on a non-interactive div
issues.evidence: <div role="tab" aria-selected={isActive} ...> wraps a separate inner <button> that actually activates the tab (1033-1053); the role element is unfocusable, there is no roving tabindex and no Arrow/Home/End handling — while the sibling workspace tab bar implements the full pattern (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:737-772,824-836).
issues.recommendation: Reuse the workspace tab bar's keyboard/ARIA implementation (or a shared Tabs primitive) for the terminal tablist; put role='tab' on the focusable element.
issues.glassImpact: None; but if the redesign merges tab strips (issue: double chrome), this inconsistency disappears for free — merge rather than patch twice.

issues.title: Terminal drawer entrance and tab-indicator motion ignore reduced-motion and the app motion preference
issues.evidence: Drawer: "animate-[terminal-drawer-in_220ms_ease-out]" (1398); keyframes at index.css:1306 have no prefers-reduced-motion override (the reduce blocks at index.css:222, 267, 446, 1479 cover other animations only). Tab indicator: "transition-[transform,width,opacity] duration-[240ms] ease-out" (1426), no motion-reduce. Contrast: PreviewPanel and ChatRightPanel frames all carry motion-reduce:transition-none (PreviewPanel.tsx:163-176, ChatRightPanel.tsx:112). Neither consumes the --app-motion-duration-* variables the appearance system zeroes out (index.css:1470-1477).
issues.recommendation: Add motion-reduce:animate-none / motion-reduce:transition-none, and route panel chrome durations through the --app-motion-* tokens so the Motion preference governs them.
issues.glassImpact: Glass panels animating in/out are more visually loud than opaque ones; consistent motion gating becomes more important, not less.

issues.title: Hardcoded Tailwind palette colors bypass the theme token system in panel status UI
issues.evidence: Running dot: 'bg-emerald-500' (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1051); subagent entry dots: 'bg-sky-400' / 'bg-emerald-400' (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:216-217); diff error text: 'text-red-500/80' (DiffPanel.tsx:1116); 'No Git' badge: 'text-amber-600 dark:text-amber-400' (chat/ChatHeaderBar.tsx:58). Meanwhile the same panels correctly use var(--success)/var(--destructive)/var(--warning) in the diff unsafeCSS (DiffPanel.tsx:81-93,139).
issues.recommendation: Swap to semantic tokens (bg-success, bg-info/primary, text-destructive, text-warning). The VS Code-style theme registry patches tokens only — raw palette classes will not retint under any of the 9 themes or a custom primary.
issues.glassImpact: Glass surfaces amplify tint mismatches: a hardcoded emerald dot on a theme-tinted translucent strip will visibly clash.

issues.title: Empty/error states are bare text in DiffPanel but designed cards everywhere else
issues.evidence:
DiffPanel: "
Select a thread to inspect turn diffs.
" and same for 'not a git repository' / 'No completed turns yet.' (1096-1107) plus error as a raw red paragraph (1114-1118). PreviewPanel has an icon+title+body empty state (PreviewOpenFileEmptyState, PreviewPanel.tsx:186-199) and ThreadWorkspacePanel has icon-card unavailable states (252-263, 131-147).
issues.recommendation: Adopt the icon+title+body pattern for DiffPanel's three states (and render errors via the shared Alert used in PreviewPanel.tsx:690-712); the review panel is the most-visited surface and currently has the weakest states.
issues.glassImpact: Empty panels show the material at its purest — a bare 11px string floating on glass will look unfinished.

issues.title: Sub-10px px-fixed type in panel chrome ignores legibility floor and the text-size preference
issues.evidence: Turn chip timestamp 'text-[9px] leading-tight opacity-70' (1027) on already-70% muted chips; chip labels 'text-[10px]' (999,1021); 'Truncated' badge 'text-[9px]' (PreviewPanel.tsx:555); MenuGroupLabel 'text-[10.5px]' (GitActionsControl.tsx:1911). These are absolute px, so the appearance system's --font-size-base scaling (themes/appearancePreferences.ts:379) never touches them.
issues.recommendation: Floor chrome type at 11px and express it in rem/text-* scale steps so the Text Size preference applies; drop the 9px timestamp to a tooltip if space is the constraint.
issues.glassImpact: Low-contrast micro-type is the first casualty of a translucent background; fixing size/contrast now is cheaper than fighting it on glass.

issues.title: Monospace body sizes drift across preview (11px), chat code (12px), terminal (12px), raw patch (11px)
issues.evidence: PREVIEW_FILE_UNSAFE_CSS forces '[data-line]...{ font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.25rem; }' (76-80) and the fallback pre is 'text-[11px] leading-5' (654); chat markdown code is 0.75rem=12px (index.css:1186 'font-size: 0.75rem'); xterm is fontSize 12/lineHeight 1.2 (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:425-426); DiffPanel's diff lines take the @pierre/diffs default (no size override in DIFF_PANEL_BASE_UNSAFE_CSS).
issues.recommendation: Define one --code-font-size token (rem-based, preference-scalable) and feed it to the unsafeCSS strings, the pre fallbacks, and the xterm options.
issues.glassImpact: None directly; consistency work that the redesign pass should absorb.

issues.title: Two scrollbar systems inside the same panel stack
issues.evidence: AgentThreadPanel and WorkspaceLauncher use the ScrollArea component (189, 560), GitActionsControl's commit file list too (2120); DiffPanel/PreviewPanel use native overflow-auto divs styled by the global 6px ::-webkit-scrollbar rules (DiffPanel.tsx:1219, PreviewPanel.tsx:688, index.css:511-526).
issues.recommendation: Pick one (native styled scrollbars are fine for heavy virtualized surfaces) and document the rule; today adjacent tabs show different scrollbar chrome.
issues.glassImpact: Overlay-style ScrollArea thumbs float over content — under glass chrome the two systems will look even less related.

issues.title: Dead 'inline' presentation styling in DiffPanelShell misleads the redesign
issues.evidence: mode==='inline' branch applies "w-[42vw] min-w-[360px] max-w-[560px] shrink-0 border-l border-border" — but no production call site passes 'inline': ThreadWorkspacePanel forwards only sidebar/sheet/phone (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:917-919 via LazyRightPanel, ChatRightPanel.tsx:265,ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:452,511), leaving 'inline' reachable only as DiffPanel's unused default parameter (DiffPanel.tsx:438).
issues.recommendation: Delete the inline branch (or the mode) before the redesign so the mode matrix being restyled matches reality.
issues.glassImpact: Prevents wasted effort styling a presentation that cannot render.

issues.title: GitActionsControl's compact toolbar path is dead in production but carries container-query styling for a header it no longer lives in
issues.evidence: Sole production call site passes showLabels + block (ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:278-285), yet the compact path keeps '@3xl/header-actions:not-sr-only @3xl/header-actions:truncate...' label classes (1775-1783) and 'h-7 ... bg-background/35 dark:bg-background/20' button chrome (1778-1787) tuned for the chat header container (@container/header-actions, ChatHeaderBar.tsx:31).
issues.recommendation: Either delete the compact branch or re-scope it; if it survives, restyle it with the shared header-chrome recipe rather than bespoke translucent tints.
issues.glassImpact: Those bg-background/35 semi-transparent buttons were hand-tuned against bg-muted/24 header — a new glass header invalidates the tuning; better to kill or tokenize it first.

issues.title: PublishRepositoryDialog repaints the dialog surface with one-off opaque overrides
issues.evidence: Inside DialogPopup: "<div className='flex min-h-0 flex-col overflow-hidden border-foreground/10 bg-background shadow-2xl'>" plus "DialogHeader className='border-b border-border/70 bg-background'" (607) and "DialogPanel className='...bg-muted/20...'" (663) — the sibling commit dialog (2065-2220) uses the shared dialog surface untouched.
issues.recommendation: Remove the wrapper's bg/shadow overrides and let the shared dialog material own the surface; keep only the wizard-specific layout.
issues.glassImpact: If dialogs adopt the popover glass material (--app-glass-*popover-alpha tokens exist, index.css:315-317), this hardcoded opaque interior will punch a visible hole in it.

issues.title: Terminal viewport hardcodes rounded-[4px], bypassing the radius preference axis
issues.evidence: className="relative h-full w-full overflow-hidden rounded-[4px] bg-background" — every other panel surface uses rounded-md/rounded-sm tokens, and the appearance system rewrites --radius-* with !important from the user's radius setting (appearancePreferences.ts:432-445).
issues.recommendation: Use rounded-sm (or rounded-md) so the terminal corner tracks the user's radius preference like the diff cards (.diff-render-file uses var(--radius-md), index.css:1301).
issues.glassImpact: Radius consistency is what makes an inset opaque editor read as intentional within a glass frame.

issues.title: Preview tree open/close animates width for 360ms, reflowing the code pane every frame
issues.evidence: PreviewTreeMotionFrame: "transition-[width,opacity] duration-[360ms] ease-[cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)]" with style width px (159-171), plus the content panel simultaneously runs "transition-[min-width] duration-[320ms]" (780) — both are layout properties, so the (potentially large, syntax-highlighted) DiffsFile pane relayouts continuously during the toggle.
issues.recommendation: Animate transform/clip on a fixed-width rail (like the inner translate-x-4 frame already does) and snap the layout width once, or accept it but exclude the code pane from reflow via contain: layout on the rail.
issues.glassImpact: Adding backdrop-filter to nearby chrome raises compositing cost; concurrent 360ms layout animation is the kind of budget item the glass tier will need back.

verdicts.title: User-facing copy leaks internal 'refName' identifier throughout git actions
verdicts.note: All cited strings are literal user-facing copy in apps/web/src/components/GitActionsControl.tsx: JSX text 'Commit on new refName' (2214), 'Warning: default refName' (2080, rendered next to a 'Branch' label), dialog-title fallback 'Run action on default refName?' (2241), menu hint 'Detached HEAD: create and checkout a refName to enable push and pull request actions.' (2030-2033), and returned disabled-reason strings at 318 and 339. Not template placeholders — nothing interpolates them; adjacent copy correctly says 'branch' ('Branch is behind upstream...'), so this reads as a variable rename (branch→refName) that also hit string literals.

verdicts.title: Stale Electron drag-region: draggable strip is the second row of the right panel, not the row in the titlebar band
verdicts.note: Verified the full chain: DiffPanelShell puts drag-region + wco height/right-padding on its header for isElectron && mode not in {sheet, phone} (DiffPanelShell.tsx:16-21). But DiffPanel/PreviewPanel are always rendered inside ThreadWorkspacePanel (ChatRightPanel.tsx LazyRightPanel → ThreadWorkspacePanel → DiffPanel mode={props.mode}), whose own h-12 tab bar (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx ~789-794, no drag-region) sits above the shell header, inside a Sidebar container that is 'fixed inset-y-0 z-10 flex h-svh' (ui/sidebar.tsx ~288). So in Electron sidebar/inline modes the row in the titlebar band is the non-draggable tab bar, while the drag-region and the wco:pr window-control reservation land on the row ~48px below. Repo-wide grep confirms no other drag-region covers the right panel's top row.

verdicts.title: Four different header-chrome treatments across chat / workspace / diff-preview / terminal
verdicts.note: All six citations verified verbatim: ChatView.tsx:3418-3427 header 'border-b border-border bg-muted/24' + 'drag-region flex min-h-[52px]'; ThreadWorkspacePanel tab bar 'border-b border-border bg-card/40' h-12 (h-14 phone); DiffPanelShell header h-[52px]/h-12 with no own bg on the shell's bg-background; ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1419 'flex h-7 ... border-border/70 border-b bg-muted/10'; DiffPanel.tsx:1133 'border-b border-border/50 bg-card/40'; PreviewPanel.tsx:669 'border-b border-border/60 p-2'. Four distinct surface tints (muted/24, card/40, background, muted/10) and three heights (52, 48, 28) across sibling chrome strips — the inconsistency is real; severity is a design judgment but the facts hold.

verdicts.title: Panel chrome is opaque, triple-painted, and separated by borders only — headers are layout siblings so glass would have nothing to blur
verdicts.note: Every factual leg verified: Sidebar wrapper paints 'bg-card' (ChatRightPanel.tsx ~250), ThreadWorkspacePanel root repaints 'bg-background' (~788), DiffPanelShell repaints 'bg-background' (line 35), terminal drawer repaints 'bg-background' in both layouts (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1397-1398); separation is exclusively border-l/border-b hairlines; headers/toolbars are shrink-0 flex siblings stacked above a separate flex-1 overflow scroller (DiffPanel.tsx:1095-1145 header via shell, sub-toolbar shrink-0, viewport below), so content never passes under chrome and backdrop-filter on these strips would blur only an opaque parent background. The 'design' framing is a forward-looking judgment, but the code facts it rests on are all accurate.

verdicts.title: Terminal cannot sit under translucent chrome: xterm theme is scraped from computed background and the canvas is created without allowTransparency
verdicts.note: Verified: new Terminal({...theme: terminalThemeFromApp(mount)}) with no allowTransparency (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx ~423-430) and zero repo-wide hits for allowTransparency; terminalThemeFromApp walks to '.thread-terminal-drawer' (or body) and reads getComputedStyle(...).backgroundColor (~210-227); normalizeComputedColor (~197-208) only rejects fully-transparent values, so any semi-transparent rgba would pass through (xterm forces the background opaque when allowTransparency is false, silently dropping the alpha). The full ANSI palette is hardcoded rgb() (~229-282) while the app ships a 9-theme built-in registry (apps/web/src/themes/builtin.ts: default, nord, high-contrast, midnight-graphite, one-dark-pro, dracula, github, catppuccin, tokyo-night) — the theme only feeds bg/fg via computed style. All evidence accurate.

verdicts.title: Sheet-mode header clamps to titlebar height even though the sheet is already offset below the titlebar (wco builds)
verdicts.note: Verified both halves: the non-drag branch (mode='sheet' hits it since shouldUseDragRegion excludes sheet) applies 'h-12 wco:max-h-[env(titlebar-area-height)]' (DiffPanelShell.tsx:21), while RIGHT_PANEL_SHEET_CLASS_NAME (apps/web/src/rightPanelLayout.ts:5) already offsets the whole sheet with 'wco:mt-[env(titlebar-area-height)] wco:h-[calc(100%-env(titlebar-area-height))]', and the wco class is toggled on the root exactly when navigator.windowControlsOverlay is visible (lib/windowControlsOverlay.ts) — i.e., Windows/Linux Electron overlay builds. So the sheet header, which never occupies the titlebar band, still gets max-h clamped to the ~32px titlebar height while its content (size-7 controls, h-6 chips) was laid out for 48px. The clamp only makes sense in the drag branch; in the sheet branch it is a real, reachable squish (Electron window under 980px wide triggers sheet mode).

strengths: The appearance system is a genuinely token-driven material axis: one preference rewrites every scrim/alpha/blur variable coherently (apps/web/src/themes/appearancePreferences.ts buildSurfaceTransparencyCssVariables, lines 572-600), with documented per-tier WCAG coverage floors (lines 509-513), a @supports no-backdrop-filter fallback, prefers-reduced-transparency and forced-colors enforcement in CSS (apps/web/src/index.css lines 656-793). This is exactly the foundation a liquid-glass redesign needs.

Two-layer patch architecture is clean and validated: theme registry JSON patches + appearancePreferences style element, with option allow-lists (OPTION_VALUES), tier-dependent defaults that preserve explicit choices (TIER_DEPENDENT_DEFAULT_KEYS), cross-tab storage sync (AppearanceSettings.tsx lines 163-171), and live re-publication on media/tier changes (syncAppearancePreferenceEnvironment).

Settings form grammar is consistent across all panels: SettingsSection / SettingsRow / SettingResetButton / SettingsPageContainer (apps/web/src/components/settings/settingsLayout.tsx) gives every row a title/description/control/per-row-reset shape, plus a section-scoped 'Restore defaults' driven by an explicit changed-labels diff (SettingsPanels.tsx useSettingsRestore, lines 337-430). Every control carries an aria-label.

Dialog family shares real choreography: nested-dialog scale/translate driven by Base UI's --nested-dialogs var, keyboard-inset-aware viewports (pb-[var(--app-keyboard-inset,0px)]), phone bottom-stick handling, and keydown stopPropagation discipline (apps/web/src/components/ui/dialog.tsx lines 76-92, alert-dialog.tsx lines 57-76).

Command palette keyboard affordances are excellent: mode-aware footer hints (Navigate/Select/Back/Esc), Kbd chips hidden on coarse pointers (pointer-coarse:hidden), inline Enter/Cmd-Enter hints on the submit button, and disabled provider rows that carry a 'Setup Required' escape hatch straight to Settings -> Source Control (CommandPaletteDialog.tsx lines 911-932, 2014-2050).

Toast system is unusually careful: thread-scoped rendering, visible-time-only auto-dismiss that pauses on blur/hidden (toast.tsx ThreadToastVisibleAutoDismiss lines 417-493), copy-error affordance, expandable detail panels with a height cap, and a stacked+anchored dual-manager split.

Semantic alpha tokens compose over glass for free: --muted, --accent, --secondary, --border are alpha-based (--alpha(var(--color-black)/4%) etc., index.css lines 380-388 and dark block), so hover states, separators, and Kbd chips already read correctly on translucent surfaces.

The desktop glass convention already exists and is used consistently at call sites: surface="glass" + project-glass-surface across SettingsDialog, CommandPaletteDialog, ProjectSettingsDialog, ProjectExplorerDialog, worktree dialogs, sidebar dialogs — one idiom to redesign, not ten.
patterns: Floating surfaces must use .app-surface / .app-muted-surface (color-mix of --popover/--muted with --app-*-opacity, index.css lines 528-557) — never raw bg-popover — or they silently opt out of the Material axis. Toasts, dialogs, command panel all follow this; SettingsSection (bg-card) does not.

Desktop glass = surface="glass" on DialogPopup/CommandDialogPopup (applies .selection-glass-surface, index.css line 666) plus .project-glass-surface as a blur intensifier (blur(30px) saturate(142%) contrast(1.04), index.css line 795). The intensifier wins only by stylesheet source order — a redesign must formalize this into named tiers.

Scrim tokens are preference-driven: --app-dialog-viewport-light/dark-alpha, --app-sheet-backdrop-alpha, --app-command-backdrop-opacity (index.css lines 308-311) are rewritten by buildSurfaceTransparencyCssVariables and pinned to Solid values under prefers-reduced-transparency (index.css lines 752-766). Any new scrim must join this pipeline.

Nested-dialog choreography is contractual: popups transition only [scale,opacity,translate] and derive offset/scale/opacity from --nested-dialogs (dialog.tsx line 78); AlertDialog opened above a glass dialog inherits the push-back effect. Keep transitions on those three properties.

Motion tokens exist and are the reduction mechanism: --app-motion-ease cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) and --app-motion-duration-sheet/stack/chip are zeroed by the motion axis and prefers-reduced-motion (appearancePreferences.ts lines 607-617, index.css lines 449-456). Today only phone components consume them — new desktop motion MUST consume these vars instead of literal durations.

Settings IA: single zustand store settingsDialogStore.ts (open + section); deep links via openSettings("source-control") from anywhere (e.g. CommandPaletteDialog.tsx lines 870-874). Sections lazy-load via React.lazy in SettingsDialog.tsx.
Keyboard-hint grammar: Kbd/KbdGroup chips for footer-level hints, CommandShortcut for per-row shortcuts, both hidden on coarse pointers; every hidden hint has a tap-reachable equivalent.

Toast layering: stacked toastManager at z-100 top-right offset below the header (--toast-header-offset, toast.tsx line 529) + anchoredToastManager for positioner-anchored toasts; thread scoping via data.threadRef.

Dialog content scroll is owned by the popup's ScrollArea (SettingsDialog.tsx line 261, DialogPanel in dialog.tsx line 170); panels rendered inside must not introduce their own scrollport (SettingsPageContainer currently violates this — see issues).

issues.title: Modal scrim model splinters into four behaviors; glass dialogs get no scrim at all
issues.evidence: Default dialogs: viewport gets "app-dialog-viewport-scrim ... backdrop-blur-[2px]" (dialog.tsx:40; white 48% / black 28%). Glass dialogs: DialogViewport gets `surface === "glass" && "bg-transparent backdrop-blur-none dark:bg-transparent"` (dialog.tsx:67) and DialogBackdrop has no background — zero dimming. Command palette (also surface="glass") keeps "app-command-backdrop" = color-mix(var(--background) 60%, transparent), no blur, 200ms (command.tsx:33, index.css:571-577). Sheets: "app-sheet-backdrop ... backdrop-blur-sm" black 32%, 200ms (sheet.tsx:25).
issues.glassImpact: This is the core layering decision a liquid-glass redesign must own. The settings dialog floats blurred over full-contrast content while Cmd-K gets a heavy 60% wash — same material, opposite modality signals. A glass language needs one scrim scale (none/thin/regular) mapped to surface roles, all fed by the existing token pipeline.
issues.recommendation: Define a single scrim tier system (e.g. --app-scrim-none/thin/regular) consumed by dialog, alert-dialog, command, and sheet backdrops; give glass dialogs a deliberate thin scrim rather than an accidental absence, and unify durations.

issues.title: Theme palette radiogroup is not keyboard operable
issues.evidence: div role="radiogroup" wraps div role="radio" items with `tabIndex={isActive ? 0 : -1}` (line 577) and onKeyDown handling only " "/"Enter" (lines 579-584). No ArrowUp/ArrowDown roving — inactive radios are tabIndex -1, so the only focusable radio is the already-selected one.
issues.glassImpact: None directly; blocks the Appearance panel from being shippable as the redesign's showcase surface.
issues.recommendation: Implement roving-tabindex arrow-key navigation (Up/Down/Left/Right moves focus and selection per WAI-ARIA radio group pattern), or render real <input type=radio> elements.

issues.title: Desktop overlays hardcode durations; neither OS reduced-motion nor the app Motion axis reaches dialogs, palette, or toasts
