issues.evidence: Toast.Root: "[transition:transform_.5s_cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),opacity_.5s,height_.15s]" — literal 500ms and a curve that differs from the house --app-motion-ease (0.16,1,0.3,1). DialogPopup/AlertDialogPopup/CommandDialogPopup: "duration-[240ms] ease-out" (dialog.tsx:78, alert-dialog.tsx:65, command.tsx:75). Settings nav indicator "duration-[240ms]" (SettingsDialog.tsx:228). Only sheet.tsx:25 has motion-reduce:transition-none. --app-motion-duration-* is consumed exclusively by mobile/phone components (grep: MobileSheet, MobileDock, PhoneAppearanceSettings…).
issues.glassImpact: Glass sells itself through motion; if the redesign adds more choreography on this foundation, reduced-motion users get more untamed movement, not less.
issues.recommendation: Add desktop motion tokens (--app-motion-duration-overlay etc.) consumed via arbitrary values (duration-(--app-motion-duration-overlay)), so the existing zeroing in appearancePreferences.ts covers all overlays; standardize on --app-motion-ease.

issues.title: Toasts join the transparency axis without a blur tier — unreadable at High/Glass steps
issues.evidence: Toast.Root uses "app-surface" (alpha = --app-surface-opacity, i.e. 72% at the Glass step) with no backdrop-filter; only the 24px dismiss orb has "backdrop-blur-sm" (toast.tsx:100). Meanwhile the Appearance copy promises the axis covers toasts: "Adjust glass and floating surfaces like dialogs, menus, popups, and toasts." (AppearanceSettings.tsx:469).
issues.glassImpact: Direct: at translucent steps toast text composites over scrolling code/diff content with no blur and no scrim floor — the one surface class that took the alpha without taking the material.
issues.recommendation: Give toasts a material tier (blur + scrim floor) like the phone GlassSurface tiers, or exempt them from the alpha axis; the tier-coverage-floor method in appearancePreferences.ts (GLASS_TIER_COVERAGE_FLOORS) is the template.

issues.title: ThemeEditor's sticky Save/Cancel bar never sticks inside the settings dialog
issues.evidence: "sticky top-0 z-10 ... bg-muted/72 backdrop-blur-sm" — but its nearest scroll container is SettingsPageContainer's "flex-1 overflow-y-auto" (settingsLayout.tsx:120), which never actually scrolls because the dialog's outer ScrollArea (SettingsDialog.tsx:261, viewport "h-full ... overflow-y-auto", scroll-area.tsx:26) owns scrolling. Sticky therefore resolves against a non-scrolling scrollport and behaves as static: editing a long token list scrolls Save/Cancel out of view.
issues.glassImpact: Also a nested backdrop-filter root inside the blur(30px) glass popup — harmless today but exactly the kind of accidental nesting a glass redesign must inventory.
issues.recommendation: Remove the inert overflow-y-auto from SettingsPageContainer (let the dialog ScrollArea own scroll) so sticky resolves against the real scrollport; or hoist editor actions into the dialog header.

issues.title: Destructive confirmations use three different mechanisms within settings alone
issues.evidence: window.confirm(getDesktopUpdateInstallConfirmationMessage(...)) at SettingsPanels.tsx:210; (api ?? ensureLocalApi()).dialogs.confirm(...) for Restore defaults at :402; ensureLocalApi().dialogs.confirm(`Remove MCP server "${server.name}"?`) at McpServersSettings.tsx:825 — while theme deletion uses a styled AlertDialog with variant="destructive" button (AppearanceSettings.tsx:828-850) and ThemeEditor uses AlertDialog for discard (:396). On web, localApi.ts:67 falls back to window.confirm.
issues.glassImpact: Native OS confirm sheets over a glass dialog are the single loudest break of the material illusion.
issues.recommendation: Standardize on AlertDialog (Cancel + destructive action, destructive button variant) for all in-app confirmations; reserve dialogs.confirm for pre-window contexts only.

issues.title: AlertDialog has no glass variant — opaque confirms stack on glass parents
issues.evidence: AlertDialogPopup hardcodes "app-surface ... shadow-lg/5" with no surface prop, while its sibling DialogPopup grew surface="default"|"glass" (dialog.tsx:56-61). Deleting a theme from the glass settings dialog opens an opaque-family popup above a glass one.
issues.glassImpact: Two material families visible in one stack; the nested-dialog push-back animation makes the mismatch conspicuous.
issues.recommendation: Port the surface prop to AlertDialogPopup (or decide alerts are always the most opaque tier and document that as the elevation rule).

issues.title: Settings content cards are opaque bg-card, ignoring the material axis their own panel controls
issues.evidence: SettingsSection body: "relative overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border bg-card text-card-foreground shadow-sm/4 ...". --card is fully opaque (index.css: --card: var(--color-white); dark: color-mix(in srgb, var(--background) 98%, ...)). The palette's content panel instead uses "app-surface" (command.tsx:160), which follows --app-surface-opacity.
issues.glassImpact: Inside the flagship glass dialog, the Transparency slider changes the dialog shell but the section cards stay solid — the two glass flagships answer 'what is content sitting on glass' differently. A redesign must pick one (opaque content islands on glass is a defensible Apple-style answer — but then CommandPanel should match).
issues.recommendation: Decide the content-on-glass rule and encode it as one class (e.g. .app-content-surface); apply to both SettingsSection and CommandPanel.

issues.title: Appearance IA gaps: Motion axis absent on desktop and reduced-transparency override never reported
issues.evidence: AppearanceSettingsPanel renders rows for fonts/size/radius/primary/transparency/panel-layout but none for the "motion" preference (MOTION_OPTIONS is consumed only by components/shell/phone/PhoneAppearanceSettings.tsx:91). isSurfaceTransparencyReducedBySystem() (appearancePreferences.ts:339-341, whose doc-comment promises "the settings UI can report the override") has zero call sites in any UI.
issues.glassImpact: When the OS forces surfaces opaque, the Transparency slider silently shows a selection that isn't rendering — confusing precisely for the users the redesign targets.
issues.recommendation: Add a Motion row (System/Reduced) to the desktop panel and a status line on the Transparency row ("Overridden by system Reduce Transparency") using the existing helpers.

issues.title: No dialog size/motion scale — every large dialog invents its own geometry and one overrides the house duration
issues.evidence: SettingsDialog: "h-[min(88dvh,880px)] max-w-[1180px]" (SettingsDialog.tsx:213). ProjectSettingsDialog: "h-[min(70vh,620px)] max-w-[760px] ... duration-[320ms] ease-[cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)]" — 320ms vs the family 240ms, house curve inlined as a literal. ProjectExplorerDialog "h-[88vh] w-[90vw] max-w-[1340px]"; NewWorktreeDialog "h-[90vh] max-w-7xl"; LinkedWorktreeItemDialog "h-[92vh] w-[96vw] max-w-[1440px]". dvh and vh are mixed.
issues.glassImpact: A glass redesign restyles the popup shell once; five bespoke geometries and two durations mean five review sites and visible entrance-speed drift between sibling dialogs.
issues.recommendation: Introduce size presets on DialogPopup (e.g. size="md"|"workspace"|"full") using dvh throughout, and forbid per-dialog duration/easing overrides (consume motion tokens).

issues.title: Radio-styled option grids lack radiogroup semantics or arrow navigation
issues.evidence: Token-mode options: buttons with role="radio" aria-checked inside a plain div "flex w-full flex-col gap-2 sm:w-80" (line 751) — no role="radiogroup". FontPreferencePicker and PrimaryColorPreferencePicker do have role="radiogroup" (lines 903-906, 1007-1010) but every radio is tabbable and there is no arrow-key movement, so SRs announce a radio group that ignores its own interaction contract.
issues.glassImpact: None.
issues.recommendation: Wrap token-mode options in role="radiogroup" and add shared roving-tabindex arrow handling for all three pickers (one hook, reused).

issues.title: Two kbd hint treatments coexist inside the command palette
issues.evidence: Row shortcuts: CommandShortcut renders a bare <kbd> "ms-auto font-medium font-sans text-muted-foreground/72 text-xs tracking-widest" (no chip). Footer hints: Kbd renders "h-5 min-w-5 rounded bg-muted px-1 ..." chips (kbd.tsx:9). Same surface, same semantics, two visual languages.
issues.glassImpact: Minor; bg-muted is alpha-based so chips already sit fine on glass.
issues.recommendation: Pick the chip treatment for both (or reserve bare text for rows deliberately and document it).

issues.title: Transparency preview hand-duplicates the material step values
issues.evidence: TRANSPARENCY_PREVIEW_OPACITY = { default: 1, light: 0.92, medium: 0.84, high: 0.78, glass: 0.72 } mirrors 1 - SURFACE_TRANSPARENCY_STEPS (appearancePreferences.ts:238-244: 0/.08/.16/.22/.28) by hand; a new step or retuned value silently falls back to `?? TRANSPARENCY_PREVIEW_OPACITY.default`.
issues.glassImpact: The preview is the user's mental model of the material axis; drift here misrepresents the redesigned material.
issues.recommendation: Derive the preview opacity from SURFACE_TRANSPARENCY_STEPS (export it or a helper) instead of a parallel record.

issues.title: Glass blur tier depends on stylesheet source order between two equal-specificity classes
issues.evidence: .selection-glass-surface sets "backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(132%) contrast(1.03)" (index.css:688-689); .project-glass-surface sets "backdrop-filter: blur(30px) saturate(142%) contrast(1.04)" (index.css:796-797). Both are single-class selectors applied to the same element (e.g. SettingsDialog.tsx:213 + surface="glass"); the 30px tier wins only because it is declared later in the file.
issues.glassImpact: Core material mechanism held together by declaration order; any refactor that reorders or layers these rules silently downgrades every large dialog to the 10px tier.
issues.recommendation: Make tiers explicit: have .project-glass-surface set a --app-glass-blur/-saturate custom property that .selection-glass-surface consumes, or split into named tier classes that are never combined.

issues.title: Toast stack renders above modal dialogs and their scrims via a z-index jump
issues.evidence: Toast viewport is "fixed z-100" while the entire dialog/palette/sheet family sits at z-50; inside the stack each root uses "z-[calc(9999-var(--toast-index))]". A background toast (e.g. clone failure) lands visually on top of the open glass settings dialog, unscrimmed and undimmed.
issues.glassImpact: In a glass system, layer order is the elevation story; an un-materialized surface leapfrogging the topmost glass pane reads as a rendering glitch.
issues.recommendation: Document the intended layer ladder (scrim < dialog < alert < toast) as named z tokens; if toasts should top modals, they need the strongest material tier (see toast blur finding).

issues.title: Dead form primitives: ui/field and ui/fieldset are used nowhere; every settings form is ad-hoc
issues.evidence:
grep for imports of ui/field or ui/fieldset across apps/web/src returns zero call sites. ThemeEditor builds fields from raw (ThemeEditor.tsx:320-337); error text is a bare

(:386).
issues.glassImpact: None directly; it means the redesign has no single field grammar to restyle — label/description/error styling must be chased through each form.
issues.recommendation: Either adopt Field/FieldLabel/FieldError in ThemeEditor and the provider/MCP dialogs, or delete the primitives so they cannot drift as a phantom second system.

issues.title: Settings section nav uses aria-current="page" on non-page tabs and an unlabeled nav landmark
issues.evidence: Nav buttons inside the dialog get `aria-current={isActive ? "page" : undefined}` (line 247) though they switch in-dialog panels, and the <nav> element (line 226) has no aria-label; 12 items are plain tab-stops with no arrow-key movement.
issues.glassImpact: None.
issues.recommendation: Use a tablist/tab/tabpanel pattern (or at minimum aria-current="true" and aria-label="Settings sections"), with Up/Down arrow navigation matching the visual list.

verdicts.title: Modal scrim model splinters into four behaviors; glass dialogs get no scrim at all
verdicts.note: All cited lines check out. The layering mechanics hold: .app-dialog-viewport-scrim is in @layer components (index.css:538+), so the utilities-layer bg-transparent/backdrop-blur-none on the glass viewport (dialog.tsx:67) defeat it regardless of the .dark rule's higher specificity, and DialogBackdrop (dialog.tsx:27) paints no background — glass dialogs (SettingsDialog, ProjectSettingsDialog, PullRequestThreadDialog, etc.) genuinely get zero dimming. Meanwhile the glass command palette keeps app-command-backdrop's 60% wash (command.tsx:33, index.css:571-577), sheets keep black 32% + backdrop-blur-sm (sheet.tsx:25), and default dialogs keep the white-48%/black-28% + 2px-blur viewport scrim. Four distinct backdrop treatments confirmed; the same-material divergence (glass dialog vs glass Cmd-K) is real. The zero-scrim state may be an intentional redesign choice, but it is implemented as a cross-layer override rather than an owned tier, and the inconsistency is factual.

verdicts.title: Theme palette radiogroup is not keyboard operable
verdicts.note: AppearanceSettings.tsx:568-589 confirmed: plain div role=radiogroup / role=radio, tabIndex={isActive ? 0 : -1}, onKeyDown handles only Space/Enter, no Arrow-key handling anywhere in the file and no wrapping primitive (not Base UI RadioGroup). A keyboard user can only reach the already-selected radio; arrow keys do nothing, so no other theme can be selected via the radio pattern (the inner Edit/Duplicate/Export buttons remain tabbable, but the radio items themselves are unreachable). Violates the WAI-ARIA radiogroup pattern as claimed.

verdicts.title: Desktop overlays hardcode durations; neither OS reduced-motion nor the app Motion axis reaches dialogs, palette, or toasts
verdicts.note: Verified: toast.tsx:557 hardcodes 500ms with cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) (vs house ease 0.16,1,0.3,1); dialog.tsx:78, alert-dialog.tsx:65, command.tsx:75, SettingsDialog.tsx:228 all use duration-[240ms] with no motion-reduce variant; grep confirms zero motion-reduce/prefers-reduced-motion handling in those files, index.css has no global reduced-motion kill-switch (only per-animation rules for shimmer/pulse/etc.), and --app-motion-duration-* is consumed exclusively by mobile/phone components (MobileDock, MobileSheet, MobileContextStrip, MobileSegmentedControl, PhoneGetAppInterstitial). appearancePreferences.ts:607-613 zeroes only those phone tokens. Minor evidence nit: sheet.tsx:84 (popup) also has motion-reduce:transition-none, not only the backdrop at line 25 — does not change the conclusion.

verdicts.title: Toasts join the transparency axis without a blur tier — unreadable at High/Glass steps
verdicts.note: Mechanism verified: Toast.Root uses app-surface (toast.tsx:557), whose alpha is --app-surface-opacity = 72% at the Glass step (SURFACE_TRANSPARENCY_STEPS glass=0.28, appearancePreferences.ts:238-244, 576; .app-surface at index.css:539-541), with no backdrop-filter on the root; only the size-6 dismiss orb has backdrop-blur-sm (toast.tsx:100). The Appearance copy explicitly promises toast coverage (AppearanceSettings.tsx:469). prefers-reduced-transparency forces app-surface opaque, so only users who opt into translucent steps are affected — but for them the composite-over-arbitrary-content-without-blur gap is real. One overstatement: popover.tsx:62 and tooltip.tsx:41 also pair app-surface alpha with no blur, so toasts are not uniquely 'the one surface class', though they are the one that floats over arbitrary scrolling content with no positioning anchor. Core finding stands.

verdicts.title: ThemeEditor's sticky Save/Cancel bar never sticks inside the settings dialog
verdicts.note: Structure verified: SettingsDialog wraps sections in ScrollArea (SettingsDialog.tsx:261; viewport h-full overflow-y-auto, scroll-area.tsx:26) whose inner unconstrained flex-col div grows to content height, so scrolling happens in the ScrollArea viewport. SettingsPageContainer (settingsLayout.tsx:120) declares flex-1 overflow-y-auto but never overflows in this host — yet per the CSS spec a non-scrolling overflow:auto ancestor still becomes the sticky element's scrollport. The ThemeEditor bar (sticky top-0, ThemeEditor.tsx:261) therefore resolves against a dead scrollport and scrolls out of view with the content — the classic sticky-trap. Confirmed for the settings-dialog host, which is where ThemeEditor renders (AppearanceSettings.tsx:685 inside SettingsPageContainer at line 344).

verdicts.title: Glass blur tier depends on stylesheet source order between two equal-specificity classes
verdicts.note: Verified: .selection-glass-surface sets backdrop-filter blur(10px) saturate(132%) contrast(1.03) at index.css:688-689 and .project-glass-surface sets blur(30px) saturate(142%) contrast(1.04) at index.css:796-797; both are single-class (0,1,0) selectors inside the same @layer components block (opened at line 538), so source order alone decides, and 30px wins only because line 795 > line 666. The combination is applied to one element in at least 8 places (SettingsDialog.tsx:213+216, PullRequestThreadDialog.tsx:205, ProjectScriptsControl.tsx:383, SidebarProjectList.tsx:678, SidebarProjectRenameDialog.tsx:32, SidebarProjectGroupingDialog.tsx:37, ProjectExplorerDialog, ProjectSettingsDialog). No current misbehavior — the .dark and reduced-transparency variants don't perturb the order — but the fragility is real and severity=low is apt.

strengths: A genuine house motion token layer already exists: --app-motion-ease: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) (expo-out) plus a three-step duration scale (chip 120ms / sheet 200ms / stack 260ms) in apps/web/src/index.css:367-370, emitted and zeroed by buildMotionCssVariables in apps/web/src/themes/appearancePreferences.ts:607-617 for both the OS setting and the in-app Motion preference, with a pre-script @media (prefers-reduced-motion) fallback at index.css:446-452. This is exactly the shape a desktop liquid-glass motion language should extend.

Ambient status motion is deliberately duty-cycled for perf: .animate-status-pulse / .animate-status-ping run 6s cycles that front-load all movement into the first ~24% then hold still (index.css:228-272, with an explicit comment), and both are killed under prefers-reduced-motion. This is the right template for always-on 'working' cues sitting on glass.

Disciplined JS-side reduced-motion + cost gating: lib/perf/motion.ts exports PREFERS_REDUCED_MOTION_QUERY and shouldEnableAutoAnimate; Sidebar.tsx:720-727 gates @formkit/auto-animate list reordering by both reduced motion and list-size thresholds; useDelayedUnmount exit delays collapse to 0 under reduce (ChatView.tsx:3355-3364, ChatRightPanel.tsx:172-175); useSmoothStreamedText.ts:61-62 returns the raw streamed text under reduce. Exit-duration constants are exported next to the CSS they must match (OVERVIEW_FLOATING_EXIT_DURATION_MS=260 / OVERVIEW_SIDEBAR_EXIT_DURATION_MS=320 in ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:67-68 matching duration-[260ms]/duration-[320ms] at lines 151/100).

One shared disclosure primitive with full a11y: lib/disclosureMotion.ts centralizes 220ms grid-template-rows+opacity+chevron motion with motion-reduce:transition-none on every class (lines 21, 31, 38), and DisclosureRegion.tsx adds aria-hidden + inert on the collapsed region. Measurement-free grid-rows collapse is the right mechanic to standardize on.

Theme-switch transition suppressor: .no-transitions zeroes all transition/animation durations (index.css:290-297) and useTheme.ts:109-122 stamps it around theme swaps with a forced reflow — essential to keep when surfaces become translucent, since a theme change would otherwise cross-fade every glass layer at once.

Every text-shimmer effect carries a reduced-motion kill switch that also restores solid text fill: .chat-file-edit-text--active (index.css:834-840), .sidebar-status-text--shimmer (985-989), the vendored shadcn shimmer utility (1479-1485), plus forced-colors fallbacks (991-997).

Toast auto-dismiss is attention-aware: ThreadToastVisibleAutoDismiss (ui/toast.tsx:417-493) pauses the dismiss timer while the window is blurred or hidden and resumes with remaining time, so timed motion never expires content the user could not have seen.

Interruptible CSS-driven enter/exit everywhere: all Base UI popups use data-starting-style/data-ending-style + transitions (dialog, popover, menu, select, tooltip, toast, sheet), so open/close is reversible mid-flight — the correct foundation for springy glass transitions, no JS animation library needed.
patterns: Token-consumption pattern to replicate on desktop: phone components apply motion as duration-[var(--app-motion-duration-sheet)] ease-[var(--app-motion-ease)] + motion-reduce:transition-none (components/mobile/MobileSheet.tsx:123,152; MobileDock.tsx:108; MobileSegmentedControl.tsx:94; MobileContextStrip.tsx:83). Any desktop glass motion must consume the same variables so the appearance-preference layer (themes/appearancePreferences.ts buildMotionCssVariables) keeps owning reduced motion.

Enter/exit convention: Base UI data-starting-style/data-ending-style classes drive mount/unmount transitions; conditional unmounting uses useDelayedUnmount(visible, EXIT_MS) with the ms constant exported beside the component's duration-[...] classes (hooks/useDelayedUnmount.ts; ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:67-68; ChatRightPanel.tsx:35). A redesign must keep these constants and CSS durations in lockstep or derive both from one token.

Popup scale grammar: overlays enter at scale-98 + opacity-0 from origin-(--transform-origin) (popover.tsx:59, menu.tsx:65, select.tsx:137, tooltip.tsx:41); dialogs use translate-y-3/scale-96 in, translate-y-2/scale-97 out at 240ms with nested-dialog stacking via --nested-dialogs calc (dialog.tsx:78, command.tsx:75, alert-dialog.tsx:65). Tooltip/popover reposition uses data-instant:transition-none / data-instant:duration-0 (tooltip.tsx:34,41).

Disclosure convention: grid-rows-[0fr/1fr] shell + min-h-0 overflow-hidden inner + content drift, 220ms ease-out, from lib/disclosureMotion.ts — used across transcript folds; DISCLOSURE_CLEANUP_BUFFER_MS = 40 grace before unmount.

Animations are registered in @theme (--animate-skeleton, --animate-boot-logo-pulse with their @keyframes, index.css:135-192) rather than as loose CSS — the precedent for adding named glass motion utilities instead of arbitrary values.

Perf conventions around motion: will-change-transform only on actively transitioning surfaces (MobileSheet.tsx:152, dialog.tsx:78, menu.tsx:65); content-visibility:hidden + containIntrinsicSize for inactive panels (lib/perf/motion.ts:18-31); auto-animate size thresholds before enabling list animation (Sidebar.tsx:721-727).
The .no-transitions class (index.css:290-297) is the sanctioned way to suppress global motion during wholesale style swaps (useTheme.ts:109-122); appearance/theme work must route through it.

Scrim/backdrop alphas are appearance-preference variables, not literals: .app-dialog-viewport-scrim / .app-sheet-backdrop / .app-command-backdrop (index.css:559-577) are rewritten per Material step by buildSurfaceTransparencyCssVariables — any new glass-transition choreography must animate these classes, not hardcoded colors.

issues.title: OS prefers-reduced-motion is ignored by nearly every desktop base primitive
issues.evidence: DialogPopup animates "transition-[scale,opacity,translate] duration-[240ms] ease-out ... data-starting-style:translate-y-3 data-starting-style:scale-96" with no motion-reduce variant. Same absence in alert-dialog.tsx:65, popover.tsx:59, menu.tsx:65 and 107, select.tsx:137, command.tsx:75, tooltip.tsx:41, collapsible.tsx:25, switch.tsx:19, and toast.tsx:557 ("[transition:transform_.5s_cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),opacity_.5s,height_.15s]"). Only sheet.tsx:25,84 carries motion-reduce:transition-none among ui/ primitives (22 files app-wide use the variant, but almost none are the base overlays). There is no global reduced-motion CSS collapse — index.css:446-452 only zeroes the --app-motion-* variables, which these components do not consume.
issues.glassImpact: Liquid glass adds larger translate/scale/blur choreography to exactly these surfaces; shipping it on primitives that already ignore reduced motion compounds an existing a11y gap. Fixing consumption (route durations through the zeroable tokens) solves both at once.
issues.recommendation: Make every ui/ primitive consume the --app-motion-* duration tokens (which collapse to 0ms under both the OS setting and the app preference) instead of literal durations, or minimally add motion-reduce:transition-none beside every data-starting-style/data-ending-style transition.

issues.title: House motion tokens are phone-only; desktop hardcodes the same curve as arbitrary values
issues.evidence: buildMotionCssVariables emits --app-motion-ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) and three durations, but the only consumers are five phone components (MobileSheet.tsx:123,152; MobileDock.tsx:108; MobileSegmentedControl.tsx:94; MobileContextStrip.tsx:83; PhoneGetAppInterstitial.tsx:27). Desktop panels hardcode the identical curve as ease-[cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)] in ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:100,111,151, ChatRightPanel.tsx:112,242,251, and PreviewPanel.tsx:164,174,780,789 (11 occurrences), and the Motion preference UI itself is phone-only (PhoneAppearanceSettings.tsx:94 is the sole MOTION_OPTIONS consumer; isReducedMotionEffective at appearancePreferences.ts:344-346 has no other callers).
issues.glassImpact: The redesign's motion language has nothing to hang on at desktop tier today: the token layer exists but zero desktop components would inherit a retuned curve, duration ramp, or the user's Reduce Motion choice.
issues.recommendation: Promote --app-motion-* into @theme (e.g. --ease-glass, --duration-chip/sheet/stack/panel) so ease-glass / duration-sheet become first-class utilities; migrate the 11 hardcoded cubic-bezier occurrences; expose the Motion preference in desktop AppearanceSettings.

issues.title: No unified duration/easing scale: 13 ad-hoc durations and 5 easing families across equivalent surfaces
issues.evidence: Overlay enter/exit alone spans: popover/menu/select duration-200 ease-out, dialog/command duration-[240ms] ease-out, sheet duration-200 ease-in-out (sheet.tsx:84), tooltip 150ms Tailwind default ease, toast root "transform_.5s_cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)" plus Toast.Content "transition-opacity duration-250" (toast.tsx:647), banners exit with ease-in (ComposerBannerStack.tsx:24), SidebarProviderUpdatePill uses "duration-180 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)]" (SidebarProviderUpdatePill.tsx:126), sidebar width uses ease-linear (sidebar.tsx:277,288). Grep tally: durations 100/120/150/180/200/220/240/250/260/300/320/360/500 all in active use.
issues.glassImpact: Apple-style glass reads as one material because everything shares one physics. Five easing families guarantee the redesign will look stitched together unless the scale is consolidated first.
issues.recommendation: Define a 4-step duration ramp (~120 micro / 200 control / 260 surface / 320-360 panel) plus one primary ease (the existing expo-out) and one exit ease; codemod the outliers (toast .5s quint-out, pill 180ms, sheet ease-in-out, sidebar ease-linear) onto it.

issues.title: Dead animate-in/fade-in classes: no animation plugin exists, so intended entrances render as instant pops
issues.evidence: "!prefersReducedMotion && \"animate-in fade-in slide-in-from-bottom-1\"" — but package.json has no tailwindcss-animate/tw-animate-css and index.css imports only "tailwindcss", so Tailwind v4 emits nothing for these classes. Same dead classes at KeybindingsSettings.tsx:711 ("animate-in fade-in slide-in-from-top-1") and contextMenuFallback.ts:63 ("animate-in fade-in zoom-in-95"). The prefersReducedMotion gate proves the entrance was intended to animate.
issues.glassImpact: The scroll-to-bottom pill and fallback context menu are floating chrome that will become glass chips; today they pop in frame-instant, which will be far more visible on a translucent capsule.
issues.recommendation: Either add tw-animate-css to index.css or replace with the codebase's own pattern (data-starting-style transitions or a small @theme keyframe like chat-final-diff-section-in, index.css:842-861).

issues.title: Dialog scrim + blur snap in/out: fade classes sit on the unpainted Backdrop while paint sits on the untransitioned Viewport
issues.evidence: DialogViewport carries the visible layer ("app-dialog-viewport-scrim ... backdrop-blur-[2px]") with no transition or data-starting-style classes, while DialogBackdrop (line 27) has "transition-all duration-[240ms] data-ending-style:opacity-0 data-starting-style:opacity-0" but paints nothing by default. Base UI's Viewport does receive transitionStatus data attributes (node_modules/@base-ui/react/dialog/viewport/DialogViewport.js maps startingStyle), so the fade could live there. Identical split in alert-dialog.tsx:21 vs 37. Contrast sheet.tsx:25 and command.tsx:33 where the painted layer and the fade are the same element.
issues.glassImpact: At 2px blur/48% alpha the one-frame snap is subtle; a liquid-glass redesign will raise blur radius and material presence on this exact layer, turning the snap into a hard flash. Must be fixed before increasing the material.
issues.recommendation: Move the scrim+blur classes onto the faded element (or add opacity transition + starting/ending styles to the Viewport), keeping the popup's 240ms timing.

issues.title: Panel choreography animates width/min-width (layout), which will force per-frame re-blur under glass
issues.evidence: "transition-[width] duration-[360ms] ease-[cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)]" on the right panel spacer; PreviewPanel.tsx:164 "transition-[width,opacity]", :780 "transition-[min-width]", :789 "transition-[width,opacity,background-color]"; ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:100 "transition-[width,opacity]"; ui/sidebar.tsx:277,288 "transition-[width] duration-200 ease-linear". 16 layout-property transitions app-wide. The content layers correctly pair a transform (translate) with the width spacer, but the width tween itself reflows every frame.
issues.glassImpact: These are precisely the surfaces the desktop glass redesign targets. A backdrop-filter surface whose ancestor reflows re-samples and re-blurs its backdrop every frame; width-tweened glass panels will jank on 4K/120Hz. Scroll containers (transcript) sit directly under these panels, compounding cost.
issues.recommendation: Keep width transitions only on opaque spacers; render glass layers at final size and animate transform/opacity/clip-path only. Where the reveal must track width, use grid-template-columns transitions on the parent and translate on the glass child (the existing frame/translate split in ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:111 is already halfway there).

issues.title: Three parallel expand/collapse primitives with different mechanics, timings, and a11y
issues.evidence: (1) ui/collapsible.tsx: "h-(--collapsible-panel-height) overflow-hidden transition-[height] duration-200" — no motion-reduce, no easing (consumers: settings/HubAdvancedOptions.tsx, settings/ProviderInstanceCard.tsx). (2) lib/disclosureMotion.ts: grid-rows 220ms ease-out with motion-reduce (4 consumer files). (3) AnimatedHeight.tsx: measured height, "transition-[height] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none" with a 250ms JS fallback (HEIGHT_TRANSITION_FALLBACK_MS, line 5; consumers GitActionsControl, HubSection, ConnectionsSettings, AddProviderInstanceDialog).
issues.glassImpact: Two of the three animate the height property; inside a translucent card that means per-frame backdrop re-blur. The grid-rows variant is the glass-safe one (it can be composited if inner content is transform-clipped) and already has the best reduced-motion story.
issues.recommendation: Standardize on disclosureMotion's grid-rows mechanic at one duration token; fold ui/collapsible styling into it and reserve AnimatedHeight for the rare unknown-size resize case.

issues.title: Skeleton shimmer is a continuous full-surface animation with no reduced-motion fallback
issues.evidence: "animate-skeleton" applies --animate-skeleton: skeleton 2s -1s infinite linear (index.css:135) sweeping a gradient via background-position with the `fixed` attachment trick; neither skeleton.tsx nor index.css contains a prefers-reduced-motion override for it (unlike status-pulse/ping and every shimmer, which are all gated).
issues.glassImpact: Loading states will sit on glass surfaces where a moving highlight is doubly prominent (it interacts with the material's own specular language).
issues.recommendation: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .animate-skeleton { animation: none; background: var(--color-muted); } } or motion-reduce:animate-none plus a static fill in the component.

issues.title: Interactive feedback language is split: base controls pop hover state instantly while bespoke controls animate
issues.evidence: buttonVariants base transitions only shadow ("transition-shadow") while hover swaps background ("[:hover,[data-pressed]]:bg-primary/90", ghost "[:hover,[data-pressed]]:bg-accent") — an instant pop. Sidebar rows likewise: "transition-[width,height,padding] hover:bg-sidebar-accent" (ui/sidebar.tsx:764). Meanwhile ComposerPrimaryActions.tsx:127,196 animate "transition-all duration-150 hover:bg-rose-500 hover:scale-105" (the app's only hover scale, not reduced-motion gated), terminal tabs use "transition-colors duration-150" (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1036), and chat copy buttons use 120ms ease (index.css:1235-1238).
issues.glassImpact: Hover 'lensing' on liquid glass (specular/backdrop response to pointer) needs one declared stance on hover timing. Today half the app says crisp-instant and half says 120-150ms smooth; a lensing layer added on top would expose the inconsistency on every mixed toolbar.
issues.recommendation: Decide the micro-tier: either keep base-mira's instant color pops and restrict animation to shadow/lens layers, or add a ~120ms color transition app-wide via the button base. Remove the one-off hover:scale-105 or make press-scale a system-wide token-driven behavior.

issues.title: Toast stack animates height and carries its own z-index arithmetic and nested blur orb
issues.evidence: Toast.Root: "z-[calc(9999-var(--toast-index))] ... [transition:transform_.5s_cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),opacity_.5s,height_.15s]" — height tween on stack collapse; the corner dismiss orb adds "backdrop-blur-sm" inside an app-surface card (line 100).
issues.glassImpact: If toasts become glass cards, the height .15s tween re-blurs per frame, the 9999-based z calc must reconcile with any glass overlay stacking plan, and the orb's blur creates a nested backdrop root inside the card's own material.
issues.recommendation: Move stack collapse to transform/scale-only (the peek math already runs on translateY/scale), drop the orb's backdrop-blur once the card itself is a material, and fold the .5s quint-out curve into the house scale.

issues.title: One-shot entrance and countdown animations lack reduced-motion gates
issues.evidence: "animate-[terminal-drawer-in_220ms_ease-out]" (keyframes index.css:1306-1315) has no motion-reduce:animate-none; .provider-update-pill-progress runs "provider-update-pill-countdown var(--provider-update-pill-dismiss-ms) linear forwards" (index.css:1281-1292) with no reduce fallback (used at SidebarProviderUpdatePill.tsx:153); .chat-final-diff-section (index.css:842-861) by contrast is properly gated.
issues.glassImpact: Minor, but the drawer entrance translate will read larger once the drawer is a floating glass sheet.
issues.recommendation: Add motion-reduce:animate-none to the drawer entrance; for the countdown, swap to a static remaining-time affordance under reduce (it conveys information, so removal alone is not enough).

issues.title: transition-all on full-viewport backdrops transitions every property including backdrop-filter
issues.evidence: DialogBackdrop "transition-all duration-[240ms]"; command.tsx:33 "app-command-backdrop ... transition-all duration-200"; alert-dialog.tsx:21 same; sheet.tsx:25 "backdrop-blur-sm transition-all duration-200" — the sheet backdrop actually carries a blur, so transition-all makes backdrop-filter itself animatable there.
issues.glassImpact: Once backdrops gain real material (heavier blur/saturate), transition-all invites accidental animated blur — the single most expensive transition possible on a viewport-sized layer.
issues.recommendation: Replace with transition-opacity on all backdrop/scrim layers; animate blur only ever via opacity of a pre-blurred layer.

issues.title: Banner stack exits with ease-in via inline style, off every convention
issues.evidence: exitTransitionStyle: "transition: `transform ${DISMISS_TRANSITION_MS}ms ease-in, opacity ${DISMISS_TRANSITION_MS}ms ease-in`" — the only ease-in transition in the app, defined as an inline style object rather than classes, though its reduced-motion handling (JS gate at lines 50-52) is correct.
issues.glassImpact: None specific; just curve-family drift.
issues.recommendation: Use the house exit curve (or expo-out reversed) and the shared duration token when the composer surfaces are re-skinned.

issues.title: No motion vocabulary exists for what liquid glass needs: no springs, no named utilities, no panel-tier tokens
issues.evidence: The token set is exactly one ease + three durations (--app-motion-ease, -sheet 200ms, -stack 260ms, -chip 120ms, index.css:367-370); every consumer spells them as arbitrary values (duration-[var(--app-motion-duration-sheet)]); there is no overshoot/spring curve anywhere (grep shows only ease-out/ease-in-out/linear plus two hand-rolled beziers), no duration token for the 300-360ms desktop panel tier (those are literals in ChatRightPanel/PreviewPanel/ChatOverviewPanel), and @theme registers only two animations (--animate-skeleton, --animate-boot-logo-pulse, index.css:135-136).
issues.glassImpact: Sheet/dock/panel glass transitions in the Apple idiom need a gentle-overshoot family (CSS linear() spring approximations work without a JS library and degrade to the expo-out), a panel-tier duration, and named utilities so 40+ call sites do not each re-spell variables. The existing appearancePreferences pipeline is the right owner — it already scales durations to 0 for reduce.
issues.recommendation: Extend buildMotionCssVariables with --app-motion-duration-panel (~320ms) and --app-motion-ease-spring (linear() approximation with expo-out fallback); mirror all of them into @theme as --ease-* / --duration-* so duration-sheet / ease-glass / ease-spring become first-class Tailwind utilities; then migrate desktop call sites in the same pass as the glass reskin.

verdicts.title: OS prefers-reduced-motion is ignored by nearly every desktop base primitive
verdicts.note: All cited lines verified: dialog.tsx:78, alert-dialog.tsx:65, popover.tsx:59, menu.tsx:65/107, select.tsx:137, command.tsx:75, tooltip.tsx:41, collapsible.tsx:25, switch.tsx:19, toast.tsx:557 all animate with literal durations and no motion-reduce variant; only sheet.tsx:25,84 has it among ui/ primitives. All seven @media (prefers-reduced-motion) blocks in index.css are keyframe-specific kills or the --app-motion-* zeroing at 446-452; none of these primitives consume those variables and there is no global transition disable. Minor: 28 files (not 22) use motion-reduce app-wide, which strengthens rather than weakens the claim.

verdicts.title: House motion tokens are phone-only; desktop hardcodes the same curve as arbitrary values
verdicts.note: grep confirms --app-motion-* has exactly 5 non-test consumers, all phone/mobile (MobileSheet, MobileDock, MobileSegmentedControl, MobileContextStrip, PhoneGetAppInterstitial). Desktop hardcodes ease-[cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)] at all cited ChatOverviewPanel/ChatRightPanel/PreviewPanel lines (10 occurrences there, an 11th in ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx:1079). MOTION_OPTIONS is consumed only by PhoneAppearanceSettings.tsx:94-95; isReducedMotionEffective's only non-test caller is the style-injection in appearancePreferences.ts:379; desktop AppearanceSettings.tsx has no motion control. Nuance: the desktop panels do carry motion-reduce:transition-none, so OS reduced-motion is honored there via the Tailwind variant — the gap is tokens/curve/app-level preference, exactly as claimed.

verdicts.title: No unified duration/easing scale: 13 ad-hoc durations and 5 easing families across equivalent surfaces
verdicts.note: Duration tally across apps/web/src: 100/150/180/200/220/240/250/260/300/320/360/500 utility durations in active use (plus duration-2000 and inline .5s/.25s/.15s/.1s values in toast/switch), matching the claimed spread. Easing families verified: ease-out (popover/menu/dialog), ease-in-out (sheet.tsx:84), ease-in (ComposerBannerStack.tsx:24 exit), ease-linear (sidebar.tsx:277,288), cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (panels/tokens), cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) (toast.tsx:557, SidebarProviderUpdatePill.tsx:126 duration-180), and Tailwind's 150ms default ease on tooltip (no duration/ease class). Severity is a judgment call for an inconsistency finding, but every factual assertion checks out.

verdicts.title: Dead animate-in/fade-in classes: no animation plugin exists, so intended entrances render as instant pops
verdicts.note: package.json has no tailwindcss-animate or tw-animate-css; index.css imports only "tailwindcss" with no @plugin/@config; no legacy tailwind.config.* exists; no animate-in/fade-in/slide-in/zoom-in keyframes or @utility definitions anywhere in project CSS. Tailwind v4 core does not ship these utilities, so they emit nothing. All three sites verified: ChatView.tsx:3621 (with the !prefersReducedMotion gate proving intent), KeybindingsSettings.tsx:711, and contextMenuFallback.ts:63 (actual path is apps/web/src/contextMenuFallback.ts, not lib/ — trivial citation error, code matches).

verdicts.title: Dialog scrim + blur snap in/out: fade classes sit on the unpainted Backdrop while paint sits on the untransitioned Viewport
verdicts.note: DialogViewport (dialog.tsx:40) carries app-dialog-viewport-scrim — a real painted layer (index.css:559-565/752-758: white/48% light, black/28% dark) — plus backdrop-blur-[2px], with no transition or starting/ending-style classes; DialogBackdrop (line 27) has the 240ms opacity fade but paints nothing, and no consumer passes it a background (DialogPopup renders it bare). Base UI's DialogViewport (node_modules @base-ui/react 1.3.0, dialog/viewport/DialogViewport.js) includes transitionStatusMapping, so data-starting-style/data-ending-style are available on the Viewport and the fade could live there. Identical split confirmed in alert-dialog.tsx (Backdrop line ~17-28 vs Viewport line ~30-44); command.tsx (app-command-backdrop) and sheet.tsx put paint and fade on the same element. Statically certain: scrim+blur appear at full strength on mount frame and hold until unmount after the popup's exit transition, i.e. snap in/out.

strengths: Phone material tier architecture is the right skeleton for desktop liquid glass: tier = where a surface sits, Material step = how it guarantees contrast; each tier resolves to a token triple (backdrop filter, bg alpha, scrim alpha). Blur+saturation travel as ONE token so Solid resolves to `none` instead of `blur(0px)`, deliberately avoiding a backdrop root and offscreen pass (apps/web/src/themes/appearancePreferences.ts:550-559, apps/web/src/index.css:579-595).

Composited WCAG contrast floors are asserted per tier x Material step x color scheme against the real production stylesheet in apps/web/src/components/mobile/GlassSurface.browser.tsx (BODY_TEXT_CONTRAST 4.5, ICON_CONTRAST 3), with a per-tier text-role inventory documented as evidence (sheet 90/96%, chip 88/82%, dock 34/43% floors in appearancePreferences.ts:509-513). This test harness is directly reusable as the acceptance gate for new desktop glass tiers.

One transparency axis, no forks: the phone Material control is a 3-step subset writing the SAME surfaceTransparency key as the desktop 5-step control (PHONE_MATERIAL_OPTIONS, appearancePreferences.ts:113-131), with tier-dependent unstored defaults handled explicitly (TIER_DEPENDENT_DEFAULT_KEYS, :234-236).

Environment fallbacks are centralized and preference-preserving: prefers-reduced-transparency (index.css:717-767), forced-colors (index.css:769-793), and @supports not (backdrop-filter) (index.css:656-664) all pin presentation in CSS without mutating the stored choice, and the settings UI can report the OS override via isSurfaceTransparencyReducedBySystem() (appearancePreferences.ts:333-341).

Scrim implementation is correct: .app-glass-surface::before with isolation:isolate on the host and z-index:-1, border-radius:inherit, pointer-events:none (index.css:586-609) — lands above the material, below content, in every engine.

Glass dialogs drop the viewport scrim and its blur: surface="glass" adds `bg-transparent backdrop-blur-none dark:bg-transparent` to the DialogViewport (apps/web/src/components/ui/dialog.tsx:67), avoiding both scrim-behind-glass mud and a nested backdrop-filter pass.

Two-layer runtime patch system is clean: theme patch (#ryco-active-theme, themes/registry.ts:255-267) + appearance patch (#ryco-appearance-preferences), and the appearance layer re-appends its style element on every apply so it deterministically wins the cascade (appearancePreferences.ts:668-678). Themes' build-time --alpha() is materialized to runtime color-mix (registry.ts:87-123).

The class-not-wrapper decision is documented and correct: material is applied as a class to elements consumers don't own (Base UI Drawer.Popup, the pill's own button) so no extra box must be made transparent again (GlassSurface.tsx:28-31).
patterns: Material tokens: --app-glass-<tier>-filter / -<scheme>-alpha / -<scheme>-scrim-alpha declared with Solid values in :root (index.css:323-337), rewritten by the injected appearance patch; tier classes bind them and .dark swaps scheme (index.css:611-642). Consumers select via glassSurfaceClassName(tier) and never name blur or alpha (GlassSurface.tsx:42-44). New desktop tiers must extend this token grammar, not invent parallel classes.

All glass tint derives from --popover via color-mix (index.css:592, 667-671, 608): themes recolor every material by patching --popover alone. Any adaptive-tint scheme must stay behind this single indirection.

Desktop overlay primitives fork on a `surface` prop: "default" -> app-surface + hairline ::before edge shadows; "glass" -> selection-glass-surface (dialog.tsx:79-81, popover.tsx:60-62, command.tsx:77-80, select.tsx:147, menu.tsx:65 always glass). project-glass-surface is an intensity modifier stacked on selection-glass-surface whose blur(30px) wins purely by source order inside @layer components (index.css:666 vs :795) — that ordering is load-bearing.

OS accessibility settings are enforced in CSS only and never written into storage; the stored selection survives and the settings UI reports the override (appearancePreferences.ts:312-341). Any new glass class MUST be added to all three fallback blocks (reduced-transparency, forced-colors, @supports-not) or it silently escapes them.

House motion: --app-motion-ease cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) + sheet/stack/chip durations (index.css:364-370), collapsed to 0s under reduced motion with the invariant 'no correctness depends on a transition completing' (appearancePreferences.ts:602-617).

Shell chrome: html AND body paint --app-chrome-background (index.css:199-206); themes may split chrome from content (themes/builtin.ts:105 'app-chrome-background': palette.chrome); frameless titlebar uses .drag-region + the wco variant (index.css:4-5, 497-508; SidebarChrome.tsx:101 'drag-region h-[52px] ... wco:h-[env(titlebar-area-height)]').

The desktop sidebar's two-tone look (sidebar shows chrome color, content shows bg-background via SidebarInset ui/sidebar.tsx:609) currently works only because the sidebar token family is undefined and bg-sidebar compiles to nothing — treat the shell as chrome-vs-content, and fix or formalize the sidebar tokens before layering glass (see issues).

Tier stamping: data-tier on the root element with phone/not-phone custom variants (index.css:6-8); presentation tier can flip mid-session without remount (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:100-110). The phone tier is frozen: desktop glass must consume the same surfaceTransparency key and the same GLASS token grammar, not extend the phone tiers themselves.

Contrast floors are the governing constraint, not taste: 'Raise a floor rather than the assertion threshold' (appearancePreferences.ts:480-508). A desktop tier inventory (which text roles a surface can render) must be written before its coverage floor is chosen.

issues.title: 12+ ad-hoc translucency recipes bypass the material system entirely
issues.evidence: PlanSidebar.tsx:120-123 "backdrop-blur ... bg-card/90 shadow-xl supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-card/75"; ChatView.tsx:3603 "bg-card/80 ... backdrop-blur"; overviewLayouts.tsx:303 "bg-card/92 px-3 py-2.5 backdrop-blur supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-card/85"; ThreadMessageSearchBar.tsx:50 "bg-popover/96 ... backdrop-blur"; MessagesTimeline.tsx:770 "bg-popover/95 ... backdrop-blur"; ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:160 "bg-popover/96 shadow-lg/8 backdrop-blur-xs"; PendingContextHandoffChip.tsx:24 "bg-popover/95 ... backdrop-blur-xs"; ThemeEditor.tsx:261 "bg-muted/72 ... backdrop-blur-sm"; PairingRouteSurface.tsx:35 and routes/__root.tsx:258 "bg-card/90 ... backdrop-blur-md"; SidebarThreadRow.tsx:599 "bg-background/90". Alphas range 72-96%, blur radii xs/sm/md/default — none driven by --app-surface-opacity or the glass tokens.
issues.glassImpact: These are exactly the surfaces a desktop liquid-glass system would own (panel, sticky headers, floating pills, inline menus). Each hardcodes its own frost level, ignores the Material axis, and ignores prefers-reduced-transparency — the redesign must inventory and absorb every one into named tiers or the material language will read as 5 different glasses.
issues.recommendation: Define desktop material tiers (panel / bar / floating-chip / inline-popover) in the same --app-glass-* token grammar and migrate all listed sites; forbid raw bg-*/N + backdrop-blur-* combinations via lint or review convention.

issues.title: Glass AA guarantee is void under themes; theme registry has no material tokens
issues.evidence: GlassSurface.browser.tsx:4-6: "this asserts against the `:root` default palette only. A bundled or custom theme replaces --popover, --muted-foreground and the status colours, so its material contrast is NOT covered here." THEME_TOKEN_NAMES (themes/types.ts:1-39) contains no glass/coverage/scrim token, so a theme cannot compensate either.
issues.glassImpact: Blocks the redesign as scoped: extending glass desktop-wide multiplies uncovered combinations across 9 built-in themes plus custom imports. A theme that lightens --popover or desaturates --muted-foreground can silently take glass surfaces below AA with nothing catching it.
issues.recommendation: Before adding desktop tiers, either (a) compute coverage floors at runtime from the active theme's resolved colors, or (b) extend the browser assertion matrix to run per built-in theme and clamp custom themes (e.g. raise --app-glass-*-alpha floors when measured contrast fails).

issues.title: Entire `sidebar` color token family is undefined — utilities silently compile to nothing
issues.evidence: sidebar.tsx:214 "bg-sidebar text-sidebar-foreground", :764/:777 "hover:bg-sidebar-accent hover:text-sidebar-accent-foreground", :581-584 "hover:after:bg-sidebar-border", :657 SidebarSeparator "mx-2 w-auto bg-sidebar-border". No --color-sidebar* exists in the @theme block (index.css:134-176) or themes/types.ts; grep for "color-sidebar" across src/ returns nothing. Tailwind v4 drops unknown utilities. SidebarSeparator (used at Sidebar.tsx:1137) is worse: twMerge (lib/utils.ts:8-10) strips the Separator base's working `bg-border` (separator.tsx:9) in favor of the nonexistent `bg-sidebar-border`, so the separator renders invisible. Call sites patch hovers ad hoc with `hover:bg-accent` while keeping dead classes like `group-hover/folder-row:text-sidebar-accent-foreground` (SidebarProjectList.tsx:278).
issues.glassImpact: Double-edged: the sidebar is accidentally transparent (shows --app-chrome-background), which is exactly the substrate a glass sidebar wants — but it is an accident, not a contract. Defining the tokens naively during the redesign would repaint the shell; leaving them undefined leaves dead classes and an invisible separator.
issues.recommendation: Decide the contract: either define --color-sidebar* tokens (sidebar: transparent / chrome-derived) in @theme and delete the ad-hoc patches, or strip the sidebar-* utilities from ui/sidebar.tsx. Fix SidebarSeparator to a visible token either way.

issues.title: selection-glass-surface and project-glass-surface run backdrop-filter unconditionally — even opaque at the default Solid step
issues.evidence: index.css:688-689 "backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(132%) contrast(1.03)" and :796-797 "backdrop-filter: blur(30px) saturate(142%) contrast(1.04)" are hardcoded, while the background alpha IS step-driven: --app-glass-light-popover-alpha resolves to 100% at Solid (index.css:315; appearancePreferences.ts:585). Desktop default is Solid (DEFAULT_APPEARANCE_PREFERENCES.surfaceTransparency: "default", appearancePreferences.ts:199). So every menu, select, combobox, command palette and every project-glass dialog (SettingsDialog max-w-[1180px], ProjectExplorerDialog 90vw) pays a full backdrop root + offscreen blur pass behind a fully opaque background.
issues.glassImpact: Directly contradicts the phone system's core discipline — 'a blur(0px) backdrop filter still forces a backdrop root and an offscreen pass, which is exactly the cost Solid exists to avoid' (appearancePreferences.ts:550-553). A desktop-wide glass rollout built on these classes inherits the waste at scale, and blur(30px) over a 1180x880 dialog runs during its scale/translate open animation.
issues.recommendation: Move both filters into step-driven tokens (e.g. --app-glass-popover-filter / --app-glass-project-filter) emitted by buildSurfaceTransparencyCssVariables, resolving to `none` at Solid — same collapse the phone tiers already implement.

issues.title: prefers-reduced-transparency does not reach ad-hoc surfaces or utility backdrop blurs
issues.evidence: The @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) block (index.css:717-767) covers only app-surface, app-muted-surface(::before), selection-glass-surface, app-glass-surface and the four scrims. It never reaches the Tailwind-utility surfaces: ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:160 "bg-popover/96 backdrop-blur-xs", PendingContextHandoffChip.tsx:24 "bg-popover/95", PlanSidebar.tsx:122 "bg-card/90", overviewLayouts.tsx:303 "bg-card/92", ThemeEditor.tsx:261 "bg-muted/72", plus the scrim-layer blurs sheet.tsx:25 "backdrop-blur-sm", dialog.tsx:40 "backdrop-blur-[2px]", MobileSheet.tsx:111 "backdrop-blur-sm", toast.tsx:100 "backdrop-blur-sm".
issues.glassImpact: The redesign's a11y story claims 'OS setting renders everything as Solid' — currently false for a dozen surfaces. Consolidating ad-hoc recipes into the token system (see the high-severity inconsistency) fixes this for free; keeping utilities keeps the hole.
issues.recommendation: Route every translucent surface through a tokened class covered by the reduced-transparency block; audit remaining `backdrop-blur-*` utilities and either tokenize or add them to the media-query override.

issues.title: One Material axis produces two different materials: app-surface goes translucent with no blur
issues.evidence: .app-surface is pure alpha: "background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--popover) var(--app-surface-opacity), transparent)" (index.css:539-541), no backdrop-filter. It skins tooltips (tooltip.tsx:41), desktop sheets (sheet.tsx:84), toasts (toast.tsx:557), autocomplete (autocomplete.tsx:107), alert dialogs (alert-dialog.tsx:65) — while menus/popovers/selects on the same axis get blur via selection-glass-surface (menu.tsx:65). At High/Glass steps, tooltip text sits over unblurred moving content at 78/72% coverage.
issues.glassImpact: This is the central design decision the liquid-glass redesign must make: whether app-surface becomes a thin blurred material or stays a plain veil. Today the same setting yields frosted menus next to watery tooltips — visibly two systems.
issues.recommendation: Fold app-surface consumers into the tier model (small overlays likely a 'chip-like' desktop tier: small blur + tight coverage floor), or clamp app-surface translucency harder than glass surfaces. Decide per-surface using the contrast-floor method already established.

issues.title: Three divergent modal backdrop grammars (white scrim+2px blur, black scrim+4px blur, tint+no blur)
issues.evidence: Dialogs: white-in-light/black-in-dark scrim at 48%/28% + backdrop-blur-[2px] (index.css:559-565, dialog.tsx:40). Sheets: black 32% + backdrop-blur-sm in both schemes (index.css:567-569, sheet.tsx:25). Command palette: background-tint at 60%, no blur (index.css:571-577, command.tsx:33). All three scale differently with the axis: dialog 48-34%, sheet 32-18%, command 60-38% (appearancePreferences.ts:578-581).
issues.glassImpact: A liquid-glass language needs one dimming grammar behind floating glass; three curves and three hues will read as unrelated systems once surfaces themselves are translucent and the backdrop shows through more.
issues.recommendation: Unify to one scrim token pair (color + alpha curve) with per-overlay-class multipliers, and decide blur-on-scrim once (Apple: none on the scrim, blur on the material).

issues.title: Desktop surfaces ignore the house motion tokens; the app Motion preference only affects phone-tier consumers
issues.evidence: House tokens exist (--app-motion-ease cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), durations 200/260/120ms, index.css:364-370) and buildMotionCssVariables zeroes them for motion="reduce" (appearancePreferences.ts:607-617). But desktop primitives hardcode: menu.tsx:65 "duration-200 ease-out", dialog.tsx:78 "duration-[240ms] ease-out", toast.tsx:557 "[transition:transform_.5s_cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),...]", ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx:1079 "duration-[320ms] ease-[cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)]" (inlines the token's value literally). No root class is stamped for the stored preference (only useTheme's .no-transitions during theme swap), so a Motion=Reduced choice made on the phone tier stops applying after a mid-session tier flip to desktop.
issues.glassImpact: Glass motion (material morph, sheet slides, popover scale) should share one curve family; today the redesign has no desktop-side token consumers to hook into, and the Motion preference contract silently breaks at the tier seam.
issues.recommendation: Migrate desktop primitive durations/easings to the --app-motion-* tokens (add a popover-scale duration token if needed); tokens already collapse for both OS and stored reduce.

issues.title: Opaque shell assumptions at the root block any window-level glass/vibrancy
issues.evidence: html and body both paint background-color: var(--app-chrome-background) (index.css:199-206); SidebarInset hardcodes "bg-background" (ui/sidebar.tsx:609); routes re-assert it (routes/_chat.index.tsx:41-42 "bg-background" twice, _settings.diagnostics.tsx:15-16). The theme system treats chrome as always-opaque color (builtin.ts:105).
issues.glassImpact: Apple-style liquid glass ultimately wants the sidebar/chrome region to admit environment light (Electron vibrancy or at least a wallpaper-tint gradient). Every one of these opaque layers sits UNDER whatever glass is added, so sidebar-glass or chrome-glass has literally nothing to refract — the material machinery is only wired for overlays above app content.
issues.recommendation: For the desktop redesign, introduce a chrome-material token (opaque today) consumed by html/body and SidebarInset instead of raw bg-background, so the shell can later go translucent per-platform without re-plumbing.

issues.title: No glass optics anywhere in the token system: flat tint, no edge highlight on app-glass tiers, three edge idioms
issues.evidence: .app-glass-surface is a flat color-mix of --popover + blur/saturate (index.css:592-594); tiers differ only by three scalars (GLASS_TIER_BLUR_SCALE/SATURATION_SCALE, appearancePreferences.ts:467-478). Edge treatment exists in three unrelated idioms: selection-glass inset highlights "inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.36)" (index.css:683-687), app-surface hairline ::before shadows "before:shadow-[0_1px_--theme(--color-black/4%)]" (popover.tsx:62), and plain borders on phone glass "border border-border/60" (MobileDock.tsx:82). No adaptive tint, no displacement/refraction, no scroll-edge treatment tokens exist.
issues.glassImpact: This is the gap inventory the redesign fills: specular top edge, luminance-adaptive tint, and a consistent border-vs-highlight rule need to become tier tokens (e.g. --app-glass-<tier>-edge) rather than three hand-rolled idioms, or desktop glass will inherit the current mismatch.
issues.recommendation: Extend the tier token triple to a quad/quint (filter, alpha, scrim, edge-highlight, tint-mix) and give selection-glass's proven highlight recipe a tokened home; keep restraint — no displacement gimmicks, Chromium backdrop-filter has no refraction primitive worth faking.

issues.title: ComposerStashPicker's app-surface is dead — utility bg-popover/96 always wins
issues.evidence: "app-surface relative overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border/80 bg-popover/96 shadow-lg/8 backdrop-blur-xs" — .app-surface lives in @layer components (index.css:538-541) which loses to Tailwind's utilities layer, so bg-popover/96 pins the surface at 96% regardless of the Material step, and the reduced-transparency override of app-surface is also defeated.
issues.glassImpact: A surface that claims membership in the material system but is actually pinned — exactly the kind of silent drift a glass migration must catch. Same pattern risk anywhere app-surface is combined with a bg-* utility.
issues.recommendation: Drop bg-popover/96 (app-surface already provides the popover surface) or drop app-surface; add a review rule that tokened surface classes never co-exist with bg-* utilities.

issues.title: Bare .app-glass-surface without a tier class renders fully transparent
issues.evidence: background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--popover) var(--app-glass-alpha), transparent) — --app-glass-alpha/-filter/-scrim-alpha are only bound by the tier classes (index.css:611-642). Used alone, the var() is invalid at computed-value time, so background-color and backdrop-filter both collapse and the surface paints nothing. Only the TS helper (GlassSurface.tsx:42-44) guards the pairing.
issues.glassImpact: When desktop tiers are added, hand-written class strings become more likely; a missing tier class fails to transparent (worst possible failure for text contrast) instead of failing safe.
issues.recommendation: Give .app-glass-surface safe fallbacks: var(--app-glass-alpha, 100%) and var(--app-glass-filter, none), so an unpaired class degrades to Solid.

issues.title: GlassSurface.tsx contract doc overstates: consumers do name radius and shadow
issues.evidence: Doc: "No consumer names a blur, alpha, radius or shadow." (GlassSurface.tsx:22-23). MobileDock.tsx:82 names "rounded-[22px] ... shadow-lg/10"; MobileSheet.tsx:144 "rounded-t-2xl ... shadow-lg/5"; PhoneGetAppInterstitial.tsx:54 "rounded-3xl border border-border/70 p-6 shadow-xl shadow-black/15". The invariant that actually holds is blur and background-alpha only.
issues.glassImpact: The redesign will be built by trusting these contracts; if geometry/elevation are meant to be consumer-owned (they clearly are), the desktop tier docs should say so precisely so elevation doesn't accidentally get tokenized twice.
issues.recommendation: Correct the comment to 'no consumer names a blur or a background/scrim alpha'; decide during the redesign whether shadow/edge move into the tier (they should, for consistency — see the optics issue).

issues.title: Nested backdrop-filter roots: blurred wrappers containing blurred surfaces
issues.evidence: PhoneGetAppInterstitial: full-screen wrapper "bg-background/72 ... backdrop-blur-sm" (:27) contains the sheet-tier glass section (:54) whose filter reaches blur(28px) at the Glass step — the wrapper forms a backdrop root, so the inner blur samples an already-filtered composite (two full-screen offscreen passes on a phone). Same pattern on desktop: PlanSidebar.tsx:120 "backdrop-blur" panel containing the sticky header's "backdrop-blur" (overviewLayouts.tsx:303), and ThemeEditor.tsx:261 "backdrop-blur-sm" inside a project-glass-surface dialog running blur(30px) (SettingsDialog.tsx:213).
issues.glassImpact: Liquid glass multiplies blurred layers; without a rule ('one backdrop root per overlay stack — inner surfaces use transparency only, or plain fills over the already-blurred parent'), the redesign will compound offscreen passes exactly where frame budget is tightest (dialog open animations, sheet drags).
issues.recommendation: Adopt and document a single-backdrop-root-per-stack rule; inner sticky bars over an already-blurred panel need only a translucent fill, not their own filter.

issues.title: Toast: pointless backdrop blur over opaque surface, plus z-9999 magnitude scheme
issues.evidence: Close button: "app-surface ... shadow-sm outline-none backdrop-blur-sm" (toast.tsx:100) — app-surface is 100% opaque at the default Solid step so the blur pass is invisible but still forces a backdrop root per toast. Toast root uses "z-[calc(9999-var(--toast-index))]" (toast.tsx:557).
issues.glassImpact: Minor, but the z-9999 scheme is the kind of magnitude hack that fights a coherent overlay/glass elevation order (dialogs and sheets sit at z-50, phone interstitial at z-[120]); glass layering is more legible with a documented z-scale.
issues.recommendation: Remove backdrop-blur-sm from the close button (or tokenize it); fold toast stacking into the app's overlay z-scale during the redesign.

issues.title: Dead --noise-opacity token still declared and emitted by themes
issues.evidence: index.css:406 "--noise-opacity: 0.035" and builtin.ts:41/:222/:255/:288 still emit noise-opacity values, but themes/types.ts:32-34 documents "the composited full-screen noise layer was removed. It is no longer rendered or edited." No selector consumes the variable.
issues.glassImpact: Harmless today, but a liquid-glass pass may want a noise/grain component back for material realism — if so, revive it deliberately through the tier tokens rather than resurrecting this orphan; if not, delete it from :root (the types.ts import-compat note can stay).
issues.recommendation: Delete the :root declaration and builtin emissions, or repurpose it as an explicit glass-grain token in the new system.

verdicts.title: 12+ ad-hoc translucency recipes bypass the material system entirely
verdicts.note: All cited class strings verified in source (a few file paths in the evidence are slightly off: overviewLayouts.tsx is at components/overview/, SidebarThreadRow/SidebarProjectList at components/sidebar/, PairingRouteSurface at components/auth/). Alphas 72-96% and blur radii xs/sm/md/default are hardcoded, none reference --app-surface-opacity or the --app-glass-* tier vars, and the prefers-reduced-transparency block at index.css:717 only rewrites .app-surface/.app-glass-surface/scrims, so these sites indeed ignore it. Note SidebarThreadRow.tsx:599 (bg-background/90, no backdrop-blur) is the weakest example, but the overall finding holds. Design-debt/inconsistency rather than a runtime bug, as the auditor labeled it.

verdicts.title: Glass AA guarantee is void under themes; theme registry has no material tokens
verdicts.note: GlassSurface.browser.tsx:4-6 contains the quoted scope comment verbatim: contrast assertions run against the :root default palette only. THEME_TOKEN_NAMES (themes/types.ts:1-39) contains no glass/scrim/coverage token, so themes replace --popover/--muted-foreground with no way to compensate, and I found no runtime contrast computation or custom-theme clamping anywhere in themes/ (appearancePreferences.ts derives alphas from the Material step independent of theme colors). The gap is real and even self-documented; whether it 'blocks' the redesign is judgment, but the factual a11y claim holds.

verdicts.title: Entire `sidebar` color token family is undefined — utilities silently compile to nothing
verdicts.note: No --color-sidebar* exists in the @theme block (index.css) or anywhere in src/; index.css is the only stylesheet (Tailwind v4 CSS-first, no tailwind.config), so bg-sidebar / bg-sidebar-border / bg-sidebar-accent / text-sidebar-* utilities are never generated. The SidebarSeparator sub-claim verified end-to-end: separator.tsx:9 base has working bg-border, sidebar.tsx:654-657 cn() appends bg-sidebar-border, twMerge (lib/utils.ts:8-10) classifies both as background-color and keeps the later nonexistent one, so the h-px separator rendered at Sidebar.tsx:1137 has no background and is invisible. Ad-hoc hover:bg-accent patch plus dead group-hover/folder-row:text-sidebar-accent-foreground confirmed at sidebar/SidebarProjectList.tsx:278.

verdicts.title: ComposerStashPicker's app-surface is dead — utility bg-popover/96 always wins
verdicts.note: ComposerStashPicker.tsx:126 combines app-surface with bg-popover/96. .app-surface lives in @layer components (index.css:538-540); @import "tailwindcss" declares utilities as a later layer, so the bg-popover/96 utility (valid in v4 since --color-popover is in @theme) always overrides the layer-components background-color regardless of specificity or class order. This pins the surface at 96% and also defeats the reduced-transparency override at index.css:718-720, which targets .app-surface in the same components layer. Low severity as claimed: visual delta from the Material-derived opacity is typically small, but the surface is genuinely outside the material system.

verdicts.title: Bare .app-glass-surface without a tier class renders fully transparent
verdicts.note: Mechanics verified: --app-glass-alpha/-filter/-scrim-alpha are bound only inside .app-glass-surface-{sheet,chip,dock} (index.css:611-641); :root and appearancePreferences.ts define only the tier-suffixed vars (--app-glass-sheet-* etc.), never the unsuffixed ones. Unpaired use makes background-color/backdrop-filter invalid at computed-value time, collapsing to transparent/none — the fail-to-transparent behavior described. Currently latent: the only emitter is glassSurfaceClassName (GlassSurface.tsx:42-44), which always pairs the classes, and no raw string usage exists in src/. Accurately filed as low-severity robustness hazard; the suggested var() fallbacks would make it fail safe.

liquidGlassReact.summary: rdev/liquid-glass-react (MIT, ~5.8k stars) is a single React component that fakes Apple's Liquid Glass with a layered DOM trick: a backdrop-filtered span (blur+saturate) that ALSO carries `filter: url(#svgFilter)` pointing at an inline SVG feDisplacementMap graph — a Chromium-only quirk where the CSS filter processes the backdrop-filtered output, making the page behind the element appear refracted. Chromatic aberration comes from three parallel displacement passes (R/G/B isolated via feColorMatrix, recombined with screen blends), masked to edges only using the displacement map's own luminance. The bezel is two 1.5px gradient rings built with the mask-composite:exclude border trick under mix-blend screen/overlay, with mouse-driven gradient angles; elasticity is React-state-per-mousemove transform math (200px activation zone, directional scaleX/scaleY, 0.1-damped translation). Displacement maps are three embedded base64 JPEG/PNG textures (X in R channel, Y in B) plus an optional canvas rounded-rect-SDF generator. The project is effectively abandoned (last commit 2025-06-13, 24 open issues, fix PRs unmerged), React-only, SSR-unsafe, layout-hijacking (forced translate(-50%,-50%) centering with sibling overlay stack), Tailwind-classname-dependent, and by its own README the displacement is invisible in Safari and Firefox (Firefox is UA-sniffed and gets filter:null; Safari renders only blur+saturate+bezel). For a Tailwind v4 design system targeting Electron (Chromium) AND Safari PWA — in a Vue/Nuxt codebase where a React component is unusable anyway — the right move is to reimplement the ingredients as CSS tokens/utilities with the SVG displacement layer as a Chromium-only progressive enhancement.
keyFacts: Rendering core: one span (.glass__warp, position:absolute inset:0) carries BOTH backdrop-filter: blur((overLight?12:4) + blurAmount*32 px) saturate(saturation%) AND filter: url(#id) referencing an inline SVG filter. Chromium applies the SVG filter to the element's composited result including the backdrop-filter output, so the displacement appears to refract the page behind. This is an implementation quirk, not spec behavior — it is the entire reason the effect is Chromium-only.

SVG filter graph (region x/y -35%, width/height 170%, colorInterpolationFilters=sRGB): feImage loads a displacement map (data URI); feColorMatrix 0.3-grayscale + feComponentTransfer feFuncA discrete [0, aberration*0.05, 1] derives an EDGE_MASK from the map itself; three feDisplacementMap passes on SourceGraphic (xChannelSelector=R, yChannelSelector=B) at scales D*(-1), D*(-1 - a*0.05), D*(-1 - a*0.1) (sign flips positive in shader mode); each pass channel-isolated via feColorMatrix, recombined with two feBlend mode=screen; feGaussianBlur stdDeviation max(0.1, 0.5 - a*0.1); aberrated result composited 'in' the edge mask, clean undisplaced center composited 'in' the inverted mask, then 'over' — edges warp, center stays sharp.

Displacement maps: src/utils.ts is 41KB of three base64 raster data URIs (standard=JPEG, polar=JPEG, prominent=PNG) encoding X displacement in R and Y in B around neutral 0.5 gray. Optional 'shader' mode generates the map at runtime on a canvas: rounded-rect SDF (qx=|x|-w+r pattern) + smoothstep hermite falloff, per-pixel JS loop over width*height, output via canvas.toDataURL().

Bezel/highlight: two sibling 1.5px ring layers using padding:1.5px + WebkitMask: 'linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0)' + maskComposite:exclude; layer 1 mix-blend-mode:screen at opacity 0.2, layer 2 mix-blend-mode:overlay; both carry inset box-shadows (0 0 0 0.5px rgba(255,255,255,0.5) inset, 0 1px 3px rgba(255,255,255,0.25) inset, 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.35)); ring background is a linear-gradient whose angle is 135 + mouseOffset.x*1.2 deg with white stops 0.12–0.6 alpha shifting with mouse position.

Elasticity: mousemove listener on the element (or mouseContainer ref) writes React state per event; activation zone = 200px from element edges with linear fade; translation = (mouse - center) * elasticity * 0.1 * fade; directional scale = 1 + |normalizedAxis| * min(centerDist/300,1) * elasticity * fade * 0.3 minus 0.15 cross-axis, clamped >= 0.8; press state scale(0.96); transition all 0.2s ease-out.

Public API (default export <LiquidGlass>): children; displacementScale=70; blurAmount=0.0625 (-> 6px backdrop blur); saturation=140; aberrationIntensity=2; elasticity=0.15; cornerRadius=999; padding='24px 32px'; overLight=false (halves displacement, 12px base blur, black + black-overlay dimming layers, heavier shadow); mode='standard'|'polar'|'prominent'|'shader'; globalMousePos/mouseOffset/mouseContainer for external mouse sync; className, style, onClick.
